articles.title: Norway's King Harald dies aged 89
articles.summary: The late king, who reigned for 35 years, broke with tradition by marrying a commoner and celebrated Norway's diversity in a famous speech.

blocks.text: Norway's King Harald V has died at the age of 89, after he was taken to hospital last week for treatment for a rare blood condition.
The palace in Oslo said he passed away peacefully at 06:35 local time (04:35GMT) on Friday at the national hospital in Oslo. The royal flag on the roof of the palace has been lowered to half-mast.
In the 24 hours leading up to his death, members of the royal family had visited the king, and crowds had laid flowers at the palace.
Harald was Norway's first king born in Norway since the 14th Century. He has been succeeded by his son Haakon.

After 35 years on the throne, he will be remembered as a popular and reforming figure who modernised the monarchy, broke with tradition by marrying a commoner and served as a unifying figure at Norway's most difficult moments.
Royal observers say he was down-to-earth, respected and beloved, describing him as a "grandfather" of the nation and the "People's king" - a title also used by his father King Olav V.
In the wake of the 2011 bomb and gun attacks on Oslo and the island of Utøya, Harald appealed to Norwegians to support each other and not "let fear take over".

More recently, Harald and his family have faced health challenges and scandal, especially over his daughter-in-law Mette-Marit's association with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, and her son Marius Borg Høiby's conviction for rape.
During his reign, the Norwegian monarchy became more egalitarian and transparent with finances and health, Ole-Jørgen Schulsrud-Hansen, historian and TV2 royal correspondent, told the BBC.

Tove Taalesen, royal correspondent for Nettavisen, described the late king as "one of us", while Caroline Vagle, royal expert for Se og Hør magazine, said he had "always been very close to the people".
When Norway's national football team returned from the US after making it to the World Cup quarter-finals for the first time, Harald welcomed them home at the palace.
He is survived by his wife of almost 58 years, Queen Sonja, their daughter Princess Märtha Louise, their son, the new King Haakon, and six grandchildren.
Harald was born on 21 February 1937 on the Skaugum estate near Oslo.
He was three when dictator Adolf Hitler ordered Norway's invasion by Nazi Germany early in World War Two.
Harald's mother fled with her children across the border to Sweden, and they travelled to the US on the invitation of President Franklin D Roosevelt.

Prince Harald returned with his family to Norway at the end of the war and completed his school and compulsory military service. He became crown prince in 1957, and studied social science, history and economics at Balliol College in Oxford from 1960 to 1962.

He met Sonja Haraldsen, the daughter of a businessman, at a party, but the crown prince had to wait nine years before he was allowed to marry her. His father, King Olav, had always hoped he would marry a European princess.
Eventually he told his father that if he could not marry Sonja, he would stay single, King Harald told Norway's public broadcaster, external.
His father finally gave his consent, and the couple wed in Oslo Cathedral on 29 August 1968.
When his father became ill in 1990, the crown prince became regent. Harald then ascended to the throne when Olav died on 17 January 1991.
The new king came into his own around 2000, according to historian Trond Norén Isaksen, growing from a reserved, serious and shy man into someone who became much more open and empathetic.

In July 2011 Harald faced his greatest challenge yet as king, when neo-Nazi Anders Breivik murdered eight people with a car bomb in Oslo before moving on to a youth camp on the island of Utøya, where he shot dead 69 others, most of them teenagers.

He gave a televised address the next day, and weeks later he delivered a speech, empathising with the victims and their families as a father, grandfather, husband, and king. On the verge of tears, his voice quivered and broke.
"I can only imagine the depth of your pain. As King of this nation, I feel for each and every one of you," he said.
Looking back, historian Ole-Jørgen Schulsrud-Hansen said: "I think that moment has been burned into our minds of what a monarchy should be."
In 2016, the king made headlines again by giving an impassioned speech , externalsupporting diversity of religion, ethnicity and sexual orientation.

He said Norwegians are from "Afghanistan, Pakistan and Poland, from Sweden, Somalia, and Syria," they "believe in God, Allah, the Universe and nothing", and they "are girls who love girls, boys who love boys, and girls and boys who love each other".

The king was also a keen athlete and environmentalist - one of the initators of the Norwegian branch of the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF), who served as president of the Norwegian chapter for 20 years.
He was such an accomplished sailor, he represented Norway three times at the Olympics, and declared his competitive sailing days over in 2022.

When Crown Prince Haakon married Mette-Marit in 2001, the king and queen welcomed her four-year-old son from a previous relationship. Marius Borg Høiby was treated as one of the family, but the royal house later stressed he was never a royal.

The king's daughter Princess Märtha Louise initially married a Norwegian writer before controversially remarrying in 2024 to an American self-styled shaman. The couple's business activities eventually led to her halting her royal duties.

While some Norwegians may have felt Harald was too lenient with his family's controversial life decisions, Vagle believes he had "shown himself to be someone who puts talking things through ahead of issuing harsh instructions".
As the king's health declined, he permanently reduced his public engagements in April 2024.

More recently he was treated with cortisone for a rare blood condition, haemolytic anaemia, which causes the number of red blood cells in the body to be reduced. He entered hospital on 17 August and his son became regent, taking over his activities.
This year alone the Norwegian royal family has faced compounded personal health challenges and scandals that have left them under almost constant public scrutiny.

The rape trial of Marius Borg Høiby, convicted of a litany of offences by judges in Oslo in June, hung over the royal family for many months. He has now appealed against a four-year jail term and appeared at Harald's bedside shortly before he died.
Days before the trial began, documents were released revealing his mother Mette-Marit's frequent contact with late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

She later apologised to King Harald and Queen Sonja for her three-year friendship with Epstein and admitted to "poor judgement", adding in a national TV interview that she wished she had never met him.
Two days after her son's trial came to an end, Mette-Marit received a lung transplant. She had been diagnosed with a rare form of pulmonary fibrosis eight years earlier.
Her doctors will not declare her stable until a year after the transplant, and the new king will face a difficult period of succession as he continues to support her.
The crises surrounding the monarchy have had an effect on its popularity. One poll for Aftenposten newspaper found that support had dropped from 72% in 2024 to 54%.
Other polls suggested almost half of Norwegians believed Mette-Marit could no longer become queen, although Haakon is now highly likely to say she will become queen.
Despite that negative sentiment towards the monarchy, Vagle said criticism was rarely directed at the late king personally, leaving her with the impression that "everyone has loved King Harald".
"When things go wrong in the royal family, people tend to blame anyone but the king," historian Trond Norén Isaksen remarked.

Haakon has faced questions about how the turbulence surrounding his own household will "follow him into his position as a king", according to Tove Taalesen, however she believes he has shown leadership and dealt with recent events well.
The royal family's main strategy has been to separate itself from Marius Borg Høiby's trial, and Ole-Jørgen Schulsrud-Hansen believes that has largely succeeded.
Although there may be further scrutiny over the Epstein files, the focus for Norwegians now will be on remembering a "greatly beloved king" and supporting his son.

articles.title: LIVE UPDATES: Nepal-Tibet flash flood devastation (Aug 28, 2026)
articles.summary: A huge wall of mud and rock collapsed into a river on the Himalayan border of Nepal and China's Tibet. Here's the latest updates on Friday, August 28, 2026

blocks.text: Missing Filipino in Nepal flood identified; sister asks for help
The Filipino who has been missing following the massive flood in Nepal has been identified by Nepalese authorities, as his sister now calls for help in tracing his whereabouts.
According to an official log by Nepal's Department of Tourism, Juan Carlos Manalo of the Philippines has been listed as a missing person in the wake of Wednesday's flooding.
Manalo was identified as part of a "trekkers society."
As this developed, Chaira Manalo, who identified herself as the sister of Juan Carlos, asked for information related to his current whereabouts.
PH embassy in New Delhi confirms 1 Filipino missing in Nepal flash flood
The Philippine Embassy in New Delhi, which has jurisdiction over Nepal, confirmed Friday that one Filipino was indeed missing in the wake of the massive flash flood at the Nepal-China border.
The Embassy said the family of the missing Filipino has yet to reach out to them, but they ready to assist them.
The Nepal Tourism Board Thursday posted a list of missing persons due to the flash flood. Of the 667 missing persons from 32 countries, one is from the Philippines.
PH envoy: Filipino community in Nepal safe; 1 Pinoy still missing after flood

Members of the Filipino community in Nepal are safe and have all been accounted for, while the search continues for a missing Filipino in the wake of the massive flash flood at the Nepal-China border that left hundreds dead, a Philippine envoy said Friday.

Consul General Maria Cynthia Pelayo of the Philippine Embassy in India, which represents the Philippines in Nepal, told Super Radyo dzBB that coordination is ongoing with the Filipino community in the destated country following Wednesday's flooding.

"Mayroon kaming close communication with the Filipino community in Nepal (We have close communication with the Filipino community in Nepal). Fortunately, they are all okay. They are well accounted for," Pelayo said.

The Philippines designates a non-resident ambassador to Nepal, who is based in New Delhi, India. On the other hand, the Nepalese non-resident ambassador to the Philippines is based in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.
Filipina in Kathmandu worries about flooding, says Nepal's small PH community keeps in touch

A Filipina living in Kathmandu remains anxious after catastrophic flash floods devastated communities in Nepal's north near the Himalayan border with Tibet, an area she said is not too far from her home.

“I cannot say na sobrang layo niya kasi based on the map po, it's just 100 kilometers away," Divina, who lives in the Nepalese capital with her Nepali husband and their daughter, told GMA News. "Two to three hours' drive po siya from my place.”

A massive wall of water and mud crashed through valleys and hillsides on the border regions of Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday, and swept down a route that links Kathmandu with Lhasa in Tibet and which is usually thronged by trekkers and pilgrims. Nearly 1,000 people are still missing and at least 362 people have been killed. At least one Filipino is missing, according to Nepalese authorities.
Nepal flash flood 'unlikely' in PH —weather specialist
A weather specialist from PAGASA believes that the flash flood that occurred along the Nepal-Tibet border is unlikely to occur in the Philippines.

“Based on ‘yung ating construction ng mga kailugan po sa ngayon is somehow hindi naman ganoon ka-drastic talaga, hindi comparable doon sa nangyari sa may area ng Himalayas kasi sobrang lawak naman po atsaka ang tataas talaga ng mga bundok nila doon,” PAGASA weather specialist Benison Estareja said in an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Friday.

(Based on the current construction of our rivers, it is somehow not that drastic and is not comparable to what happened in the Himalayan region, which is much more extensive and has much higher mountains.)

“‘Yung potential energy coming from ‘yung pinakamataas papunta sa ibaba, talagang sobra ‘yung impact. Unlike dito na, yes may tendency na talagang dumami ‘yung tubig, pero ‘yung ragasa po hindi naman siya nakikita halos maladelubyo,” he added.
1 Filipino still missing after deadly Nepal flash flood

One Filipino remains missing following the deadly flash flood that struck Nepal on Wednesday, with Philippine officials continuing to coordinate with Nepalese authorities and the Filipino community to locate the missing national.
Philippine Embassy in India Consul General Maria Cynthia Pelayo said Friday that they have yet to receive information on the Filipino whose disappearance was reported following the disaster.
“Until now, we are still waiting for information about the missing Filipino which was reported yesterday,” Pelayo said in a Super Radyo dzBB interview.
The Filipino is among the 667 foreign nationals from 32 countries listed as still missing in the update released by Nepal’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Thursday evening.
Pelayo said the Philippine Embassy has maintained close communication with the Filipino community in Nepal and that those they have accounted for are safe.
“Fortunately, they are all okay. They are well accounted for,” she said.

Most members of the Filipino community are in Kathmandu, according to Pelayo. She said around 90% of the profiles they have are spouses of Nepalese nationals, while the percentage of Filipino professionals in the country is “very minimal.”

The Philippine government earlier said there were 18 overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) in Nepal based on Overseas Workers Welfare Administration records, while Department of Foreign Affairs data showed 128 Filipinos in the country.
Rescue efforts continue
Pelayo said Nepalese authorities continue rescue operations in areas affected by the flash flood, although access to some locations remains difficult.
The Philippine official also noted that getting information from the affected areas has been difficult, saying it would be challenging for her to personally reach the location.

Nepal’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has established an emergency response team to coordinate search and rescue operations, verify information concerning missing foreign nationals and provide consular assistance. It has also urged families and diplomatic missions to rely on official channels and avoid circulating unverified information.
The disaster was triggered by a glacier collapse that sent a torrent of water, rock, ice and mud through Himalayan river systems along the Nepal-China border.
A Reuters report on Thursday quoting the Nepali police said that 359 had died, with dozens of bodies swept down into the plains from where they were being recovered.

Rescuers searched for survivors in the debris-strewn valleys and hillsides of Nepal on Thursday while more than 1,000 people remained missing there and in neighboring China after a wall of ice, mud and rock collapsed into a mountain river, triggering a catastrophic flash flood.

articles.title: Gatchalian: Absent senators forgo salaries
articles.summary: Senators who have been absent from Senate plenary sessions either due to detention, medical problems, or other reasons have voluntarily decided not to receive their salaries. Senate President Sherwin…

blocks.text: Senators who have been absent from Senate plenary sessions either due to detention, medical problems, or other reasons have voluntarily decided not to receive their salaries.

Senate President Sherwin “Win” Gatchalian disclosed this on Thursday, August 27 saying that even Sen. Loren Legarda, who earlier filed for an extended medical leave, had also declined accepting her pay.
“When she filed for medical leave and she is also not collecting her salary. In fact, the detained senators and the senator-at-large are also voluntarily foregoing their salaries,” Gatchalian said.
Legarda earlier filed five medical leaves covering Aug. 3 to Aug. 5, Aug. 11 to Aug. 12, Aug. 17 to Aug. 19, and Aug. 24 and Aug. 26, as well as Sept. 1 to Sept. 2.
According to Gatchalian, he is aware of Legarda’s medical condition but declined to provide details about the issue.
“It's a very personal matter. I am aware of her illness; even before this, we were personal friends, and she had already confided in me about having a serious condition,” the Senate chief said.
Gatchalian said he has instructed the Senate’s accounting and payroll department to suspend the release of their salaries.
He said the Senate can declare the unused salaries as savings and use it for something else.
“I wish her well; illnesses like this really need to be taken seriously,” he said.
Legarda has not publicly disclosed the nature of her illness, but earlier, Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson said that her medical leave could be related to lung problems.

Legarda and her son, Rep. Leandro Leviste, are currently facing high-profile plunder and graft complaints filed by the Office of the Ombudsman, which earlier flagged their absences as “highly suspicious.”

Both were accused of alleged irregularities and “ghost electricity” projects in connection to Leviste’s solar companies, which supposedly failed to deliver committed power generation despite securing exclusive government service contracts, resulting in billions in unpaid government obligations.

Also absent from Senate while facing plunder cases are Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta. Sen. Ronald “Bato” Dela Rosa, on the other hand, remains at large in connection with a crimes against humanity case before the International Criminal Court (ICC).

articles.title: Former NPA finance officer yields in Negros
articles.summary: BACOLOD CITY - An alleged former finance logistic officer of the New People’s Army (NPA) voluntarily surrendered to the authorities in Kabankalan City, Negros Occidental on Thursday, August 27.…

blocks.text: An alleged former finance logistic officer of the New People’s Army (NPA) surrendered to the authorities, along with a firearm in Kabankalan City, Negros Occidental on Thursday, August 27. (3rd Maneuver Company)
BACOLOD CITY - An alleged former finance logistic officer of the New People’s Army (NPA) voluntarily surrendered to the authorities in Kabankalan City, Negros Occidental on Thursday, August 27.

According to a report from the 3rd Maneuver Company of the Regional Mobile Force Battalion-Negros Island Region (RMFB-NIR), the former rebel approached the authorities through intelligence-driven initiative, expressing his desire to return to the government and his family.
During the surrender, the rebel returnee turned over a caliber .38 revolver without serial number, and five live ammunition.
He then underwent initial profiling and debriefing and received cash assistance and a sack of rice as immediate assistance to his family.
In a statement, the 3rd Maneuver Company vowed to continue its efforts and remain committed to sustain peace and order in the community.
They also encouraged others who are still involved in lawless activities to lay down their arms and choose the path of lawful and peaceful living.

articles.title: UEFA prepares Swiss complaint against FIFA chief Infantino over World Cup sell-off
articles.summary: MONACO (AP) — UEFA is preparing a criminal complaint against FIFA President Gianni Infantino in Swiss courts for possible financial mismanagement over his failed plan to sell future World Cup profits…

blocks.text: MONACO (AP) — UEFA is preparing a criminal complaint against FIFA President Gianni Infantino in Swiss courts for possible financial mismanagement over his failed plan to sell future World Cup profits to private investors.

The governing body of European soccer announced its intentions in court documents filed Thursday, Aug. 27, in the U.S. seeking access to possible evidence related to the sell-off plan, which was withdrawn after a furious backlash by UEFA and other global soccer leaders.
The move increases the pressure on Infantino, who is facing the biggest crisis in his 10 years as FIFA's leader.

UEFA filed documents in a Manhattan court requesting discovery of potential evidence from the New York investment fund, Thrive Capital Management, founded by Josh Kushner — the younger brother of President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.
UEFA also filed a request in a southern Florida district for authorization of discovery “in a foreign proceeding” against FIFA itself, which has offices in the Miami suburb of Coral Gables.

Under the plan revealed in late July, Thrive and Kushner were to be the anchor investors intending to pay FIFA $4.2 billion for a 20% stake in a subsidiary that would run the soccer body’s commercial events, including the World Cup.

“UEFA and its counsel are contemplating a Swiss criminal proceeding against Infantino and possibly other FIFA officials for criminal mismanagement under Article 158 of the Swiss Criminal Code,” UEFA’s lawyers state in a 56-page document seen by The Associated Press.
The document suggests the $4.2 billion figure could be a “fraudulently off-market price promoted by Infantino for his own benefit.”
FIFA is expected to have about $5 billion in cash reserves after the World Cup in North America boosted its revenue to a record $15 billion over the 2023-26 commercial cycle.
“The question is therefore why the FIFA president believed he needed outside investors to expand development funding,” UEFA said in a statement.
Infantino dropped the sell-off plan on Aug. 1 after intense criticism led by soccer officials in Europe.
UEFA had warned against destroying potential evidence

UEFA first threatened to take legal action on Aug. 3 when it warned FIFA against destroying or hiding any "relevant materials” related to the plan. Thursday's legal move was revealed to its member federations in Monaco just two hours before the Champions League draw began.

“Infantino claimed that the plan would ‘unleash the commercial potential and opportunity that FIFA has,’” UEFA lawyers told the courts. “In truth, it was a vehicle for Infantino and that small circle to acquire a permanent stake in and otherwise profit from FIFA’s most valuable assets to the detriment of FIFA, its members, and other parties within the football family.

“Under the terms Infantino announced, those investors stood to acquire a permanent financial interest in FIFA’s commercial arm for $4.2 billion, implying an absurdly low enterprise value of only approximately $20 billion, a figure that was neither the product of an open, competitive auction, nor tested by any independent valuer.”
Thrive declined to comment. FIFA was approached for comment.
Swiss prosecutors' poor results in FIFA trials
It was unclear if UEFA would send a potential criminal complaint to the Swiss federal prosecution office in Bern or to local prosecutors in FIFA's home city Zurich.
The Swiss attorney general's office has a poor record in recent years prosecuting cases of alleged corruption linked to FIFA and soccer officials.

Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter, former UEFA president Michel Platini and the influential Qatari president of Champions League title holder Paris Saint-Germain, Nasser al-Khelaïfi, all were acquitted twice at trials in Switzerland.
UEFA committed to replacing Infantino

The crisis has raised questions about Infantino’s future. Just months ago, he was widely expected to win another four-year term in the FIFA election set for March 2027, but a growing number of soccer federations around the world but mainly in Europe have withdrawn their support, with some joining UEFA in calling on him to step down, ideally before the Nov. 18 deadline for candidates.

“Should the current FIFA president nevertheless seek another mandate, UEFA will join forces with its partner confederations to ensure that member associations are offered a credible alternative,” the European body said, “one committed to integrity, accountability, development and genuine institutional change.”

articles.title: BSP: Inflation relief in sight, but weather, wage risks loom
articles.summary: Inflation in August may have eased to as low as 5.5 percent, potentially hitting a four-month low, on the back of lower electricity rates and a stronger peso during the month. However,…

blocks.text: Inflation in August may have eased to as low as 5.5 percent, potentially hitting a four-month low, on the back of lower electricity rates and a stronger peso during the month.

However, weather-related risks threaten to stoke price growth. The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) projected that August inflation could reach an upper bound of 6.5 percent, three percentage points (ppt) higher than the June print.

“Upward price pressures for the month are likely to be driven by higher rice, vegetable, fruit, and fish prices, partly due to unfavorable weather conditions, and elevated domestic fuel costs,” the BSP said in an Aug. 28 statement.
“These upward pressures are expected to be mitigated by lower prices of meat, as well as lower electricity rates and the peso appreciation,” the central bank added.

Prior to weakening in the second half of August, the peso opened the month strong, hovering around 60 to the United States (US) dollar—levels last seen on Aug. 10, when the currency pair traded at 60.705.

Headline inflation slowed to a three-month low of 6.2 percent in July from 6.4 percent in June, after peaking at a more than three-year high of 7.2 percent in April. Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy items, also eased to 4.2 percent from 4.4 percent in June.
The BSP noted that it remains vigilant against geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and extreme weather events like El Niño.

Monetary authorities have been working to stabilize domestic prices, which have fluctuated since conflict flared in the Middle East over five months ago, disrupting shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

To counter these pressures, the BSP raised key borrowing costs in three consecutive policy meetings, including a rate hike last Thursday, Aug. 27. The move aimed to address oil-driven price volatility, the potential impact of a record-high ₱85 wage increase, and inflation risks from El Niño, which is expected to peak in the fourth quarter of 2026.

BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr. clarified that the latest rate hike was a proactive measure to get ahead of inflation risks before they materialize. Whether the five percent policy rate proves sufficient will depend heavily on how risks around wage adjustments and El Niño unfold in the coming months.
While oil price volatility remains a concern, Remolona noted that other emerging risks have taken priority in the BSP’s policy calculations, stating, “Other risks are bigger.”
In its latest policy meeting, the BSP revised its average inflation forecast for 2026 downward to 6.1 percent from 6.4 percent.

However, it raised its 2027 forecast to 5.4 percent from 4.5 percent—keeping it well above the target band of 2.0 to 4.0 percent. Headline inflation is expected to return near the 3.0 percent target midpoint by 2028.

Jonathan Ravelas, senior adviser at Reyes Tacandong & Co., holds a cautious outlook for August price growth, forecasting inflation at 6.1 percent. He suggested recent policy tightening and improving supply conditions are “gradually gaining traction” and moving inflation onto a downward trend over the near term, offering relief to consumers and businesses.

However, Ravelas noted that his estimate, still well above the 4.0 percent target ceiling, indicates that underlying price pressures remain elevated and “the fight against inflation is far from over.”

“More importantly, while inflation may ease in the near term, the combined impact of the recent wage hike, the potential effects of El Niño on food supply, and ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine conflict could pose upside risks to inflation in the coming months,” Ravelas said.

He added that these factors will force the BSP to tread carefully to prevent secondary price spikes, noting that the primary challenge for the government is ensuring that moderating inflation translates into a sustainable recovery in Filipinos’ purchasing power.

articles.title: PCG divers search for 3 missing Aeta passengers as boat capsizes off Mapanuepe Lake in Zambales; 6 dead, 4 rescued
articles.summary: Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) divers on Friday, Aug. 28, continued their underwater search for three passengers who remain missing after a motor banca carrying 13 people capsized off Mapanuepe Lake in…

blocks.text: Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) divers on Friday, Aug. 28, continued their underwater search for three passengers who remain missing after a motor banca carrying 13 people capsized off Mapanuepe Lake in San Marcelino, Zambales.
PCG spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said technical divers were sent to the area as the search resumed for the missing passengers, identified as one adult and two minors.

“As of the latest record of the PCG search and rescue team, of the 13 passengers on the boat, six died – three adults and three minors; four survived, while three are still being searched for in the water,” Cayabyab said.

The incident occurred at about 2 p.m. Thursday, Aug. 27, off the coast of Barangay Buhawen after the passengers, who were members of the Aeta Indigenous Peoples community from Sitio Lumibao, had gone there to attend a community health center activity.

“Based on the initial information, these 13 passengers went to Barangay Buhawen to attend a community health center activity. The intention was to get their food and medicine and avail themselves of the vaccination program,” Cayabyab said.

“While they were going back to Sitio Lumibao, they encountered a sudden strengthening of the wind and strong waves. If this were at sea, it appears that the story would be like a squall, something like that. But again, our investigation is ongoing into what really caused this incident. But that is the initial information we obtained based on the account of the survivors,” Cayabyab said.

According to Cayabyab, Mapanuepe Lake is a remote body of water in the mountainous portion of San Marcelino. It was formed after the 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo, and now covers nearly 600 hectares.
Because of the lake's remote location and distinct conditions, there is no established PCG unit or office in the area.
The area where the banca capsized was near the Sunken Church, which Cayabyab described as deep.
“It is somewhat deep because the area where it happened is near the Sunken Church. You can almost only see the height of the church, so the area is really deep,” she said.
Cayabyab said the PCG would carry out two search efforts depending on weather and water conditions.

“First, of course, if the weather improves and the underwater inspection becomes possible, we will conduct the diving. Second, we will continue the surface search and rescue operation together with the other responding agencies,” she said.

articles.title: Notice of check dishonor under Bouncing Checks Law can now be served electronically -- SC
articles.summary: The notice of dishonor of a check under the Bouncing Checks Law can now be served electronically aside from personal service and through the mails, whether registered or ordinary mail, the Supreme…

blocks.text: The notice of dishonor of a check under the Bouncing Checks Law can now be served electronically aside from personal service and through the mails, whether registered or ordinary mail, the Supreme Court (SC) has ruled.
A violation of the Bouncing Checks Law under Batas Pambansa Blg. 22 happens when someone issues a check for payment, knowing there are not enough funds, and the bank later dishonors the check.

Under BP 22, the issuer of a dishonored check has five banking days from receipt of the notice of dishonor to pay the amount due. If payment is not made within that period, the law presumes that the issuer knew there were insufficient funds when the check was issued.

In a full court decision written by Associate Justice Samuel H. Gaerlan in GR No. 277047 that was made public last August 24, the SC pointed out that an issuer of a bouncing check charged in court cannot defeat prosecution simply by denying receipt of the notice or refusing to accept it.
Otherwise, the SC said that issuers of bouncing checks could easily evade liability by avoiding service.

A summary of the decision issued by the SC’s Office of the Spokesperson stated that personal service remains the preferred mode. The notice may be delivered directly to the issuer or, in the case of a business, to an authorized representative.

If the issuer cannot be served at the office, the notice may be left at the issuer’s residence with an adult resident between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. The person serving the notice must execute an affidavit stating when, where, and how the service was made.
When practicable, service should be documented through photographs or video recordings, subject to proper authentication in court.
If personal service is not practicable, the notice of dishonor may be sent by registered mail, or where registry service is unavailable, by ordinary mail.
The person serving the notice must likewise execute an affidavit explaining why personal service could not be made and attach the supporting postal documents.
The SC also recognized electronic service. It said a notice of dishonor may now be served through email as a primary mode of service when the issuer previously provided their email address.

Electronic service may likewise be used through platforms such as Viber, Facebook Messenger, or similar applications, provided it can be verified that the electronic account belongs to the issuer, it added.
At the same time, the SC said that electronic service may also be used when the issuer refuses to receive the notice, avoids service, or when personal service is otherwise impracticable.
In such cases, the electronic notice must be sent within 24 hours after the final unsuccessful attempt at personal service and must state the dates and details of those failed attempts, it said.
The sender must also execute an affidavit and preserve supporting evidence, such as screenshots, messages, delivery or read receipts, or chat histories, it added.

The SC pointed out that a simple denial of receipt is not enough to invalidate electronic service. In all instances, to successfully dispute service, the issuer must show that it was physically impossible to have received the notice at the time and place it was served, it said.

It clarified that bank-generated text messages or emails informing a customer that a check has been dishonored may help corroborate service but cannot replace the notice of dishonor required by BP 22.

The decision was issued on the appeal filed before the SC by a couple who were charged with six counts of violations of BP 22. The couple (whose names the Manila Bulletin redacted) were engaged in tire dealerships. They were charged in court by their tire supplier for the six bouncing checks involving P609,972.58.

The tire supplier presented evidence that the firm’s messenger personally attempted to serve the notice of dishonor at the spouses’ office. The spouses refused to receive it and instead instructed an employee to sign for it.
The metropolitan trial court, regional trial court, and Court of Appeals all found the spouses guilty.

In their appeal, the spouses told the SC that they should be acquitted because they were not properly served with a notice of dishonor. The SC rejected their argument and affirmed the rulings of the lower courts.

The SC found that the spouses merely questioned the credibility of the messenger’s testimony but failed to challenge his affidavit of service or prove that they could not have been at their office when service was attempted.

The SC ruled: “All things considered, the Court reiterates that there is no dispute that spouses signed the checks and that the bank dishonored the checks because the account had been closed. Notice of dishonor was properly given, but the spouses failed to pay the checks or make arrangements for their payment within five days from notice. With all the above elements duly proven, the spouses cannot escape the criminal and civil liabilities that Batas Pambansa Blg. 22 imposes for its violation.”

The spouses were fined a total of P609,972.58 for the six BP 22 violations, with subsidiary imprisonment in case of nonpayment. They were also ordered to pay the tire supplier the same amount, plus six percent interest until fully paid.

articles.title: LRA probing land titles in 38-hectare 'illegal' Taguig reclamation — Lacson
articles.summary: The Land Registration Authority (LRA) is investigating the origins and ownership history of several land titles covering around 38.83 hectares of illegally reclaimed areas on the Taguig City side of…

blocks.text: The Land Registration Authority (LRA) is investigating the origins and ownership history of several land titles covering around 38.83 hectares of illegally reclaimed areas on the Taguig City side of Laguna Lake, Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson said.

blocks.caption: Senator Panfilo Lacson (OS Lacson photo)

blocks.text: Senator Panfilo Lacson (OS Lacson photo)
Lacson said the LRA began reviewing the titles based on documents and other materials submitted by the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA).

“I requested them to backtrack the history of the issued OCTs (original certificates of title) and other modes of titling, so we will find out how they were manipulated with the end in view of filing criminal charges against those responsible,” Lacson said.

Based on the senator’s initial information, some of the original certificates of title (OCTs) were issued through judicial or ordinary land registration proceedings, while others were granted through homestead patents.
Lacson said the titles could eventually be invalidated if the PRA proceeds with forfeiture proceedings as provided under the law.
He earlier disclosed that the LRA was reviewing documents from the PRA to determine whether titles had been issued over portions of Laguna Lake that had been reclaimed illegally.

Aside from the land titles, Lacson said several crates of documents from the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) concerning allegedly anomalous projects in Taguig City were also set to be submitted to the Office of the Ombudsman.

The documents form part of the evidence that Lacson and his staff have previously provided to the Ombudsman as part of their investigation into alleged irregularities involving infrastructure and reclamation projects in Taguig.
The Ombudsman is conducting a fact-finding investigation into the projects and has subpoenaed the DPWH, PRA, LRA and the Taguig Registry of Deeds for documents relevant to the probe.

Lacson’s office had earlier submitted evidence covering at least five case studies involving alleged irregularities in Taguig infrastructure projects. These included supposed ghost projects, double appropriations, the reuse of photographs for billing purposes, and the alleged diversion of funds intended for slope protection projects to finance what Lacson described as “unabated and illegal” reclamation activities.
The senator said these cases should be thoroughly examined by the Ombudsman and other government agencies responsible for establishing accountability and safeguarding public property and resources.
Lacson added that he and his staff would continue submitting documents and other evidence gathered from their case studies to assist the Ombudsman’s investigation.

articles.title: Filipino doctor among missing after Nepal flash floods
articles.summary: A Filipino doctor who went on a pilgrimage in Nepal has gone missing following the massive flash flood that tore through the Nepal-China border this week.

blocks.text: Juan Carlos Manalo, a Filipino traveler who joined a pilgrimate tour in Nepal, has been unreachable since the massive flash floods that hit the Nepal-China border this week.
Chiara Manalo
MANILA, Philippines – A Filipino doctor who went on a pilgrimage in Nepal has gone missing following the massive flash flood that tore through the Nepal-Tibet border this week.

Physician Juan Carlos Manalo was traveling with a group of pilgrims when the series of flash floods and subsequent landslides took place. He has been unreachable since, according to a Facebook post by his sister, Chiara Manalo.
Chiara said the family last heard from Juan Carlos on Tuesday, August 25, at 1:21 p.m. Philippine time, a day before the floods struck.
The group's last known location was the immigration office in Gyirong, on the Tibetan side of the border, Chiara said.
Juan Carlos had been traveling with a Kailash Mansarovar Yatra pilgrimage group organized by the Isha Foundation, an India-based spiritual organization, led by Sadhguru Jaggi Vasudev

Sadhguru said in a social media post Wednesday that 77 pilgrims from one of his Kailash groups were at the Gyirong immigration office, on their way back from the pilgrimage, when the flood struck and swamped the building and much of the town. He said there was no official information yet on their whereabouts.
Chiara told Philstar.com her brother had spent the past couple of years volunteering as a medical worker at an Isha Foundation center in India, and had gone there in May, by her recollection.
He joined this year's Kailash tour around August 6 or 8, Manalo said.
Juan Carlos had usually sent updates to his family every day until their parents got a call on the night of August 26 about the floods.
Chiara said she reached out to the group's Philippine contact person and was told her brother's group was at the immigration office — on its way back to India — when the flash flood hit.
The family is asking anyone with information to contact their family: Jose Rodrigo Manalo (+63 917 302 3077), Dinah Marie Manalo (+63 917 514 3465), or Chiara Manalo (+63 917 791 7849).
Manalo appears to be the Filipino traveler the Nepal Tourism Board has counted among hundreds of missing foreigners since Thursday.

The Department of Foreign Affairs said on Friday the Philippine Embassy in New Delhi and the honorary consulate in Kathmandu were coordinating with Nepali authorities and are "awaiting confirmation from Nepali authorities on a Filipino national who is reported missing."
The massive August 26 floods were set off by a glacier collapse in the Himalayas that triggered a landslide and sent an avalanche of water, ice and debris.

More than 300 people have been confirmed dead and hundreds more remain missing in Nepal, with additional deaths and missing reported on the Chinese side of the border, according to the latest tallies.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Impostor Facebook group shares fake DSWD cash aid offers
articles.summary: The social welfare department has repeatedly warned the public about fake cash aid offers; the misleading posts also use the name and image of former DSWD secretary Erwin Tulfo to look legitimate

blocks.text: Claim: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) is offering cash assistance to individuals who send a direct message to a Facebook account.
Why we fact-checked this: A Facebook account posted a series of graphics in the group “DSWD Cash Assistance Update PayOut” on August 17, 18, and 19.
The posts featured a graphic bearing the official DSWD logo and the face and name of Senator Erwin Tulfo, identifying him as “DSWD Secretary.”
It cites an alleged quote from Tulfo, where he supposedly says, “Ako ay nananawagan sa lahat ng hindi pa nakakatanggap ng cash assistance pakiusap paki message kami ngayon para maipadala na namin.”
(I am appealing to everyone who has not yet received cash assistance, please message us now so we can send it.)

As of writing, the series of posts has garnered 533 reactions, 1,033 comments, and 32 shares as it continues to circulate online.The comment sections of these posts were flooded with users asking why they had not yet received their cash aid, stating that they had already sent private messages as directed.
The facts: The posts are fake. Neither the DSWD nor Tulfo has issued an announcement urging people to send private Facebook messages to claim cash assistance.
Furthermore, Tulfo is no longer the secretary of the social welfare department, having served only from June to December 2022. As of writing, the current DSWD secretary is Rex Gatchalian.

The agency has repeatedly warned the public against social media posts supposedly offering cash aid or financial support.“The DSWD emphasized that it has no programs or financial assistance being implemented online or through social media platforms,” it wrote in a previous advisory.

Official financial assistance programs — such as the Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) and the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) — are administered through proper government protocols.For instance, there is no application process for 4Ps. Instead, pursuant to Republic Act 11310, eligible households are identified through the evaluation conducted by the National Household Targeting System for Poverty Reduction or the Listahanan, which serves as the primary database used by the DSWD to select potential beneficiaries.

Meanwhile, those applying for aid through the AICS program — which provides aid to individuals in crisis or those recovering from unexpected life events — must submit documentary requirements and undergo assessment and interview before receiving assistance.

Suspicious account and links: The account that shared the claim uses the DSWD name but is not affiliated with the government agency, and its page timeline consists entirely of similar fake posts.While the graphic advertises financial aid, the text caption promotes unrelated job vacancies, particularly for farmers and cleaners, and provides shortened URLs. These links redirect users to external job posting websites completely unrelated to government social welfare aid, potentially exposing users to phishing or data theft. (READ: Phishing 101: How to spot and avoid phishing)
Debunked: Rappler has previously debunked a related claim regarding alleged cash payouts and DSWD assistance programs from the same Facebook account. – Lyndee Buenagua/Rappler.com
Lyndee Buenagua is a journalist based in Bicol and Baguio, and an alumna of Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: Matet de Leon apologizes for causing brief EDSA standstill
articles.summary: She didn’t want to, but there it was. Matet de Leon took to social media recently to apologize for something she wouldn’t normally want to do: cause traffic on EDSA. No, she wasn’t shooting a scene…

blocks.text: She didn’t want to, but there it was.
Matet de Leon took to social media recently to apologize for something she wouldn’t normally want to do: cause traffic on EDSA.
No, she wasn’t shooting a scene there or selling something. She was caught in an unwanted accident.
Apparently, the vehicle carrying her family was sideswiped by a bus.
The incident briefly slowed traffic with Matet confronting the bus driver.
“Gusto kong humingi ng pasensiya sa mga taong naabala nang panandalian kanina sa may edsa,” Matet wrote in a Facebook post on Thursday, Aug. 27.
“Nasagi (?) kami ng bus kanina habang nakahinto sa kanto, sa likod ng jeep,” she added.
Matet said they decided to let the incident go rather than prolong it and cause more inconvenience to people.
“Nakakapikon. Pero para maiwasan ang abala sa mga taong pagod na at pauwi na galing trabaho, pinalipas na namin ito,” she wrote.
She did, however, have something to say to the bus driver.
“Sa’yo naman, kuya driver, kung nababasa mo to, ingat na lang sa susunod. Baka next time, maka disgrasya ka na talaga,” Matet said.
The actress also admitted that she got very angry after the collision.
“Hindi ako naging mabait sa driver kanina,” she said.
Matet explained that having her child inside the vehicle made the situation even more upsetting.
“Pero ang importante, yung mga taong sakay niya at mga mata traffic sa likod eh makauwi na agad,” she added.
“Nagalit ako kay Kuya, nang malala.”
She said her reaction was understandable, especially because her child was with her.
“Pero normal lang naman sigurong reaksiyon yon lalo na’t kasama namin sa sasakyan ang anak ko,” Matet said.
So if you’re stuck in traffic for no apparent reason, relax. There’s probably a perfectly good Filipino reason somewhere up ahead.
Like a bus sideswiping a celebrity’s car.
Nothing unusual. Just another day on EDSA.

articles.title: BI chief defends proposed CAISS border security project
articles.summary: Bureau of Immigration (BI) Commissioner Joel Anthony Viado defended the proposed Civil Aviation and Immigration Security Services (CAISS) project before the House of Representatives on Aug. 24,…

blocks.text: Bureau of Immigration (BI) Commissioner Joel Anthony Viado defended the proposed Civil Aviation and Immigration Security Services (CAISS) project before the House of Representatives on Aug. 24, saying it would strengthen the country’s defenses against terrorism, human trafficking, and transnational crime at no cost to the government.

Under the proposed ₱10.7-billion partnership with US-based Securiport LLC, the country’s existing border control system would be upgraded into an intelligence-driven security network designed to address emerging threats.

"We need a more integrative program covering a border security platform with biometrics, advanced analytics, and passenger information systems to enhance national security and immigration control," Viado told lawmakers during the House budget hearing.

According to Viado, the country’s border control system, which relies on manual checks and outdated databases, is struggling to detect terrorists and criminals employing increasingly sophisticated methods.

"At the moment, there is no particular program which can be funded by the national government at this level," he explained, stressing that the government lacks the P10.7 billion needed for such a massive overhaul.
Viado said Securiport would provide the entire ₱10.7-billion investment, maintain and upgrade the system every four years for 20 years, and train BI personnel at no cost to taxpayers.

"Ang (The) private proponent proposes to put a capitalization in the amount of P10.74 billion for the next 5 years, and with a constant upgrade of the system every 4 years for the next 20-year period — at no cost to the government," he said.

The BI chief clarified that the proposed ₱240 one-way charge is a service fee, not a tax. A round trip would cost ₱480, which he said is significantly lower than the fees collected in Australia, Singapore, Thailand, Hong Kong, and Japan.

"Compared to other countries, this is way below. This is actually the practice in other countries already, " Viado told Mamayang Liberal Party-list Rep Leila de Lima and Caloocan 2nd District Rep. Edgar Erice.
“The U.S., Australia, Singapore, Hong Kong, and Japan have been doing this at costs which are much higher than what we are proposing,” he added.
Delima and Erice raised concerns that the proposed user fee could impose an additional burden on overseas Filipino workers (OFWs).
Viado, however, clarified that OFWs would be exempted from paying the fee.

"Ang gastusin pagdating sa ticket, hindi po sinasagot po yan ng OFWs. Sagot po yan ng mga employers nila (The cost of the ticket is not shouldered by OFWs. It is covered by their employers),” he said.
BI noted that under existing executive orders and bilateral agreements, employers are responsible for ticket costs, including any service fees.

"So, hindi OFWs natin ang sasagot — ito po yung mgakumpanyang kukuha sa kanila ang magbabayad (So, our OFWs will not shoulder the cost—the companies hiring them will pay for it), Viado said, referring to Section 53 of the Revised POEA Rules and Regulations Governing the Recruitment and Employment of Land-Based Overseas Filipino Workers of 2016 (Governing Board Resolution No. 07-16, issued February 26, 2016.

articles.title: Alex Eala bows to close friend Jovic in US Open exhibition
articles.summary: No doubt, Alex Eala was a star after lighting up the U.S. Open even in an exhibition game. The 21-year-old Eala drew cheers from the rapturous crowd in her Stars of the Open appearance, where she…

blocks.text: No doubt, Alex Eala was a star after lighting up the U.S. Open even in an exhibition game.

The 21-year-old Eala drew cheers from the rapturous crowd in her Stars of the Open appearance, where she battled and eventually bowed to her American friend Iva Jovic, 3-6, at the fabled Arthur Ashe Stadium in New York Friday, Aug. 28 (Philippine time).

Before springing into action in the women's singles field, Eala and the 18-year-old Jovic delighted the crowd with their showdown which got more fun after their dads Mike and Bojan joined them on the center court in the latter part of the match.
The two young guns also exchanged sweet pleasantries in each other’s native languages, with Jovic speaking in Tagalog while Eala delivering her lines in Croatian.
“Alex, ang galing mo,” said Jovic.
“Iva, ti si najbolja [you’re the best],” Eala replied.

Aside from Eala and Jovic, Americans Amanda Anisimova, Alex Michelsen, and Learner Tien, Ukrainian Marta Kostyuk, Brazilian Joao Fonseca, and Frenchman Arthur Fils also competed in the annual charity event of the U.S. Open.
Ranked No. 18, the charming Filipina lefty is seeded as 17th and set to face a qualifier in the opening round of the meet.
World No. 14 Jovic, on the other hand, is 14th seed and also takes on an entry from the qualifiers.

articles.title: EJ Obiena punches World Championships ticket with 5.90-meter effort in Zurich
articles.summary: Despite finishing fifth overall in Diamond League’s Zurich leg, two-time Olympian EJ Obiena still punched his ticket to the 2027 World Athletics Championships after clearing the 5.90-meter mark in…

blocks.text: At A Glance

items: Despite finishing fifth overall in Diamond League's Zurich leg, two-time Olympian EJ Obiena still punched his ticket to the 2027 World Athletics Championships after clearing the 5.90-meter mark in Switzerland Friday, Aug. 28.

blocks.caption: (EJ Obiena / Facebook)

blocks.text: (EJ Obiena / Facebook)

Despite finishing fifth overall in Diamond League’s Zurich leg, two-time Olympian EJ Obiena still punched his ticket to the 2027 World Athletics Championships after clearing the 5.90-meter mark in Switzerland Friday, Aug. 28.

The 30-year-old Obiena cleared 5.90 meters on his first attempt before a packed crowd on Swiss soil which was enough to earn himself a slot in the biennial meet to be hosted by Beijing, China next year.
It will be his fifth appearance in the world championships where he once bagged a silver and bronze in the 2023 Budapest and 2022 Eugene
“5.90m here in Zurich. Thank you @weltklassezurich for always hosting such a wonderful competition. [Para sa bayan],” Obiena wrote.
“PS: With this I also qualified for next year’s World Championship,” he added.
Obiena finished fifth overall in Zurich where he sailed over 5.50 and 5.65 meters in one try. He failed two of his attempts in 5.80m before clearing 5.90m in his final effort.

As expected, world No. 1 Armand Duplantis topped the leg with a 6.25-meter outing which was another meet record for the Swedish vaulter. He was followed by Greek Emmanouil Karalis (6.20m) and Norwegian Sondre Guttormsen (6.00m) for silver and bronze honors, respectively.

articles.title: DA creates dedicated office to strengthen rice industry
articles.summary: The Department of Agriculture (DA) has created a dedicated office to promote the development of the rice industry and formulate policies to address persistent challenges. Agriculture Secretary…

blocks.text: The Department of Agriculture (DA) has created a dedicated office to promote the development of the rice industry and formulate policies to address persistent challenges.
Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel issued Department Order (DO) No. 26, dated Aug. 26, to establish the interim rice industry development office, also referred to as the RICE office.

Despite the role of rice as the country’s main staple, the DA noted that several challenges continue to plague the local sector, including high production costs and inadequate post-harvest facilities.

“The establishment of a specialized office shall strengthen coordination, monitoring, and strategic implementation of rice development initiatives; maximize the growth potential of the industry; and respond to ongoing and anticipated executive and legislative actions and priorities,” the order read.
Under DO 26, the RICE office is tasked with implementing and overseeing rice-related programs and projects at both the national and regional levels.
Specifically, the new unit is responsible for initiating rice and rice-related programs and projects under the National Rice Program (NRP) and the Rice Competitiveness Enhancement Fund (RCEF).
It will also formulate and recommend guidelines to establish a unified monitoring and evaluation framework for all rice industry programs implemented across concerned government agencies.
Furthermore, the RICE office will facilitate digitalization initiatives and lead the consolidation of a rice industry database to support planning, monitoring, and decision-making.
The office is headed by the undersecretary for rice industry development and supported by an assistant secretary and two directors.
The formation of a dedicated office to oversee the development of the rice industry comes as the country continues to rely on foreign purchases to help plug the shortfall in local production.

The latest Bureau of Plant Industry (BPI) data showed that the country’s rice imports rose by more than a quarter to 3.27 million metric tons (MT) in the first seven months of the year, up from 2.58 million MT in the same period last year.
Vietnam was the top supplier by the end of July with 2.53 million MT, or 77 percent of total volume, BPI data showed.
Tiu Laurel earlier said that rice imports this year will help the country secure enough buffer stocks and prevent a supply shortfall before the next harvest.
The country’s rice output is on track to decline by around 750,000 MT this year due to the potential impact of an extreme El Niño during the fourth quarter.

articles.title: R1MC chief appeals for infrastructure support, cites Pangasinan leaders’ backing
articles.summary: DAGUPAN CITY---The director of the Region 1 Medical Center (R1MC) Center here appealed for stronger government support to address its infrastructure needs as the hospital continues to serve a growing…

blocks.text: DAGUPAN CITY---The director of the Region 1 Medical Center (R1MC) Center here appealed for stronger government support to address its infrastructure needs as the hospital continues to serve a growing number of patients in Pangasinan and neighboring provinces.

R1MC Center Chief Dr. Joseph Roland Mejia said the lack of adequate infrastructure remains to be one of the medical center’s biggest challenges, citing that the hospital’s physical facilities have not kept pace with its achievements in governance, management, and healthcare delivery.

“The challenge we are facing is infrastructure because R1MC is being left behind,” Mejia told Manila Bulletin, emphasizing the need for additional facilities and improvements to strengthen the hospital’s capacity.

An unfinished seven-storey building stands at the Region 1 Medical Center in Dagupan City, highlighting the need for the continued development of the hospital’s facilities. R1MC chief Dr. Joseph Roland O. Mejia has called for the continuation of infrastructure projects to help support the hospital’s target of a 1,500-bed capacity and meet the growing healthcare needs of patients.

Despite the infrastructure concerns, Mejia pointed to R1MC’s track record in governance and compliance with healthcare standards. He cited the hospital’s ISO recognition and its previous Presidential recognition received at Malacañang during the administration of former President Benigno Aquino III.

Mejia also highlighted R1MC’s accomplishment under the Performance Governance System (PGS), saying the medical center ranked second nationwide among participating hospitals, next to the Philippine Heart Center.
He said the recognition reflects the hospital’s commitment to sound management and good governance.
However, Mejia said these accomplishments need to be matched with adequate infrastructure support.
He claimed that medical center has not received sufficient infrastructure assistance in recent years despite the growing demand for its services.
Mejia appealed to Malacañang to give greater attention to R1MC’s infrastructure requirements, saying Pangasinan deserves healthcare facilities capable of meeting the needs of its residents.
He expressed confidence that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. recognizes the importance of supporting the province, citing what he described as the President’s love for the people of Pangasinan.
The R1MC chief also said all congressmen in Pangasinan have been supportive of the medical center’s efforts and infrastructure needs.
Still optimistic that the province’s political leaders and the national government would continue working together to secure the resources needed by the hospital.

Mejia said additional infrastructure would allow R1MC to expand its services, improve patient care, and better respond to the increasing healthcare needs of Pangasinan and the wider Region 1 community.

articles.title: Derrick Rose embraces Filipino culture at ArenaPlus VIP night in Cebu
articles.summary: CEBU, Philippines — Basketball has long shaped Derrick Rose’s connection with the Philippines, but on Tuesday night, Aug. 25, in Cebu, Filipino culture took center stage. The former NBA Most Valuable…

blocks.text: CEBU, Philippines — Basketball has long shaped Derrick Rose’s connection with the Philippines, but on Tuesday night, Aug. 25, in Cebu, Filipino culture took center stage.

The former NBA Most Valuable Player and ArenaPlus ambassador got a closer look at the traditions behind that connection during the Champion’s Circle Appreciation Dinner on Aug. 25 at Kasadya Buffet Buko Bar, Shangri-La Mactan here.
Rose spent the evening watching the Kasadya Cultural Show alongside ArenaPlus VIPs, content creators, and members of the media.

Kasadya, a Cebuano word that captures a sense of joy and celebration, lived up to its name as the evening showcased a vibrant mix of Filipino culture through traditional dances, colorful costumes, and fiery performances.

“It’s been nothing but love—the traditional dances, the people,” Rose said when host Mark Zambrano asked what had stood out about Cebu’s welcome, with the former MVP applauding throughout the performances and appearing especially impressed as one performer sent flames into the air.
But watching eventually gave way to participation as Rose was invited onstage to try Tinikling, putting the former MVP in the middle of one of the Philippines’ best-known folk dances.
“Yeah, that’s rhythm,” Rose said after making his way through the bamboo poles, before laughing as Zambrano jokingly suggested adding Tinikling to offseason training.

The lighthearted moment offered another kind of connection with Filipino fans for Rose, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2008 NBA Draft who went on to become the youngest MVP in league history three years later.

“That’s why I retired, to be able to have these types of moments, being able to see people face to face, be intimate, and to grow a connection through life,” said Rose, now on his fifth visit to the Philippines and his third as an ArenaPlus ambassador in less than a year.
“I feel like that’s life, the journey, being able to travel, and travel with a good experience and travel with great company,” he added.

The Champion’s Circle Appreciation Dinner provided that kind of setting, bringing Rose within conversational distance of guests through a Q&A, photo opportunities with ArenaPlus' most loyal players from Cebu, and an evening that eventually saw him become part of the cultural celebration himself.

“I’m gonna keep speaking on the experience. This is something that I am taking, I am cherishing,” Rose said. “Energy is the only thing that we get in this life, and this memory here will last forever.”
After years of Filipino fans following Rose through the triumphs, adversity, and resilience that shaped his basketball journey, the evening allowed that exchange to go the other way.
For one night in Cebu, it was Rose’s turn to learn a little more about the people who had been waiting to welcome him.

articles.title: Marcoleta defends Guteza, claims threats forced recanted statement
articles.summary: Detained Senator Rodante Marcoleta said his respect for Master Sergeant Orly Guteza remains intact despite the soldier’s release of a statement on Aug. 19 that contradicted his earlier testimony…

blocks.text: Detained Senator Rodante Marcoleta said his respect for Master Sergeant Orly Guteza remains intact despite the soldier’s release of a statement on Aug. 19 that contradicted his earlier testimony before the Senate Blue Ribbon Committee.

blocks.caption: Senator Rodante Marcoleta and Orly Guteza (MB file photos)

blocks.text: Senator Rodante Marcoleta and Orly Guteza (MB file photos)
Marcoleta said Guteza’s latest statement was not surprising to him, saying it was understandable given the ordeal the soldier allegedly went through.
“My respect for MSgt Guteza has not been diminished by the release of his completely different statement on August 19, 2026,” Marcoleta said.
“It was unsurprisingly expected as it was obviously understandable given the ordeal he was subjected to,” he added.

Guteza previously testified before the Blue Ribbon Committee on Sept. 25, 2025, where he provided allegations concerning the supposed involvement of then-Speaker Martin Romualdez, former Rep. Zaldy Co and others in the alleged misuse of billions of pesos intended for flood control projects.
In his latest statement, Marcoleta maintained that the change in Guteza’s account should not diminish his view of the soldier’s character.
He said the circumstances surrounding Guteza’s later statement should instead be taken into consideration, particularly allegations that the soldier and his family were subjected to threats.

Marcoleta also pointed to a previously circulated video of a phone call between Guteza and his wife, which he said showed that the soldier had been effectively isolated after his Senate testimony and later made to sign and read a different statement.
According to Marcoleta, Guteza repeatedly told his wife that the new statement was not his, but that he had signed it to protect his family from possible danger.
The senator said he was raising these circumstances without attacking Guteza’s “honor, sense of duty and valor.”
Instead, Marcoleta maintained that Guteza’s latest statement should be viewed in light of the alleged pressure placed on him and his family.
He argued that Guteza’s original testimony before the BRC was a detailed account of his purported personal knowledge, while the later statement merely contained a general denial.

Citing the Supreme Court case People v. Manlapaz (G.R. No. 254747, July 13, 2022), Marcoleta argued that the latter statement carries little evidentiary value when weighed against the witness’ earlier detailed account.
Allegation vs him, Defensor
Marcoleta also questioned the plausibility of the allegations against him and former lawmaker Mike Defensor.
He said it was unlikely for him to have conspired with Guteza, whom he described as a complete stranger at the time.
He likewise rejected as implausible the claim that he and Defensor could have fabricated a detailed account involving the transport of money in luggage within an hour at a restaurant.

Marcoleta said it would have been physically improbable for him, upon arriving at the restaurant and being introduced to Guteza, to assess his character, establish trust, learn the details of his account, rewrite it, give him instructions on subsequent steps, and return to the Senate within minutes.
Instead, Marcoleta maintained that it was more believable that threats against Guteza’s wife and children had compelled the soldier to sign what he called an “outrageous statement.”
Despite the latest development, Marcoleta said he would not be deterred from pursuing accountability over the alleged misuse of public funds.

“Rather than feel dismay and defeat by the situation of Guteza, and the millions of our countrymen who suffer repression for seeking accountability and justice, we must strengthen our resolve,” he said.

articles.title: History beckons as Alex Eala, Janice Tjen clash at PH Arena
articles.summary: A fitting homecoming for the toast of Philippine sports. Alex Eala battles her fellow Southeast Asian tennis star Janice Tjen of Indonesia in Tatler's “Alex Eala Live: Game. Set. Celebrate.” at the…

blocks.text: A fitting homecoming for the toast of Philippine sports.
Alex Eala battles her fellow Southeast Asian tennis star Janice Tjen of Indonesia in Tatler's “Alex Eala Live: Game. Set. Celebrate.” at the Philippine Arena in Bocaue, Bulacan on Dec. 8.
The 21-year-old Eala is expected to give her Filipino fans an unforgettable experience with an exhibition showdown against Tjen at the world’s largest indoor arena.
The event will also feature local tennis talents and celebrity games.
If things fall into place, it could become one of the biggest tennis spectacles on local soil, with the 99,000-square-meter Philippine Arena capable of accommodating up to 55,000 guests.

It can be remembered that the largest crowd for a tennis game was recorded on Feb. 7, 2020, at the Cape Town Stadium in South Africa, where tennis icons Roger Federer of Switzerland and Rafael Nadal of Spain duked it out in a friendly contest before the 51,954 spectators.
Federer won the “Match in Africa” charity contest over longtime rival Nadal, 6-4, 3-6, 6-3.

“I’ll be playing against Indonesia’s Janice Tjen. Get ready for an unforgettable day of world class tennis and the celebration of national pride, designed to inspire the next generation of Filipino tennis players,” said Eala in her interview with event organizer Tatler.
“I can’t wait to share this moment with you and celebrate our culture together,” she added. “Thank you so much for all the support going into the U.S. Open. Manila, magkita-kita tayo.”
Eala, sporting her career-best world ranking of No. 18, is set for a stern test in the women’s singles event where she is seeded as 17th. She will battle a qualifier in the opening round.

articles.title: DILG flags grooming, extremist content targeting minors on Roblox
articles.summary: The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) on Friday raised alarm over alleged online grooming and extremist conversations targeting minors on Roblox.

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 2:08pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.
The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) on Friday raised alarm over alleged online grooming and extremist conversations targeting minors on Roblox.

“The Roblox games are played by millions of teenagers here in the Philippines. So that should be stopped. Sa Roblox namin nakita ang extremist conversations,” DILG Secretary Jonvic Remulla said during a press conference.

“Yun sa ibang first person shooters game, hindi pa namin nakikita as extensive as what you see in Roblox. At saka international ‘yan. International ang scale ng groomers na nangyayari dito,” he added.

Authorities have observed chat groups on the gaming platform and found some of the language used in these online conversations was allegedly criminal in nature and involved incitement of teenagers to violence.
Other Stories
Remulla earlier expressed his support to impose a total ban against Roblox following the fatal shooting at Ateneo de Zamboanga University on August 18.
In March, Roblox expressed its commitment to maintaining the safety of children, including its Filipino users, on the platform.
The company emphasized that "advanced safeguards and robust safety policies" are already in place to protect its players.

“We have filters designed to block the sharing of personal information, our chat features don’t allow user-to-user image or video sharing, and age checks are required before anyone has access to chat," Roblox said.

"Those same checks are also used to limit kids and teens to only chatting with others of similar age by default. Our approach includes multiple layers of protection: advanced AI detection systems, dedicated teams who constantly monitor for critical harms, user reporting tools, and ongoing collaboration with law enforcement and safety organizations,” the company added. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: DFA still awaiting confirmation on Filipino reportedly missing after Nepal floods
articles.summary: The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) said Friday, Aug. 28, that Philippine officials are still awaiting confirmation from Nepali authorities regarding a Filipino national reportedly missing…

blocks.text: The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) said Friday, Aug. 28, that Philippine officials are still awaiting confirmation from Nepali authorities regarding a Filipino national reportedly missing following massive flash floods in northern Nepal.

DFA spokesperson Analyn Ratonel said the Philippine Embassy in New Delhi and the Philippine Honorary Consulate General in Kathmandu, Nepal, are in “active coordination with local authorities and stand ready” to extend assistance to affected Filipinos.
“They are awaiting confirmation from Nepali authorities on a Filipino national who is reported missing,” Ratonel said.
Philippine officials are verifying reports that a Filipino traveler was among those reported missing after deadly flash floods struck areas near the Nepal-China border.

In an earlier statement, the DFA said the Philippine Embassy in New Delhi, which is mandated to represent the Philippines in Nepal, and the Philippine Honorary Consulate General in Kathmandu were actively monitoring the situation in affected areas to determine whether Filipinos were among those affected by the disaster and to provide emergency rescue or assistance, if needed.
“The Embassy and the Consulate General are coordinating with Nepali authorities to determine whether there are affected Philippine nationals and provide emergency rescue or assistance,” the DFA said.

Latest data released by the Nepal Tourism Board on Aug. 27 showed that a Filipino traveler was among those listed as “missing” after flash floods swept through parts of the Himalayan region near the Nepal-China border.

The disaster unleashed torrents of mud, debris, and water across affected communities, prompting rescue and assessment operations as authorities worked to determine the full extent of the damage and casualties.
Approximately 128 Filipinos reside in Nepal, with the Filipino community in the country largely composed of women married to Nepali nationals, according to the DFA.
The DFA said Philippine authorities will continue to closely monitor developments and coordinate with Nepali officials as rescue and assessment efforts continue.
