articles.title: DILG probes BFP officials over alleged ‘slots for sale’ scheme
articles.summary: DILG chief Jonvic Remulla warned all BFP officials involved in the 'slots for sale' scheme to come out and confess as crack down begins.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — All former and current regional directors of the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) are under investigation as the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) cracks down on the alleged widespread "slots for sale" extortion scheme within the fire agency.

Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said in a press briefing at Camp Crame, Quezon City, on Friday, August 28, that more than 200 fire personnel nationwide are under investigation for alleged involvement in what he described as a long-standing “cancer” in the BFP.
“The BFP has become a criminal syndicate instead of a law enforcement and a first responder,” Remulla said.
Remulla’s warning

The "slots for sale" scheme was previously uncovered by the DILG in February this year, in which some officials allegedly required BFP applicants to pay hundreds of thousands of pesos in exchange for guaranteed promotion or acceptance.
Remulla said those involved typically require payments ranging from P100,000 to P800,000.
“Binabalaan ko na ang lahat ng opisyal ng BFP. Lumabas na kayo ngayon at umamin kayo o hahabulin namin kayo hanggang matapos ang career n’yo,” Remulla warned.
(I am warning all the BFP officials. Come out and confess or we will come after you until the end of your careers.)
Remulla stressed that not all regional directors are restricted from their duties during the investigation, but only those who are proven to have links to corruption.
Crackdown

Remulla’s warning came following the arrest of a female BFP personnel earlier this week during an entrapment operation in San Fernando City, Pampanga, after an applicant made a report to the authorities.

The suspect, who was identified as a 32-year-old active Senior Fire Officer 1, allegedly used a dummy account to contact an aspiring Fire Officer 1 and demanded P500,000 in exchange for a guaranteed slot.

She was arrested by the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) on August 24 while receiving the partial payment of P300,000 from the complainant. She is currently under the custody of the CIDG.

The CIDG said a criminal complaint for robbery-extortion in relation to Republic Act 10175, or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, was filed against the suspect before the San Fernando City prosecutors on August 26.
The involved senior officer, who was identified as Deputy Regional Director for Administration in Region 4A, has also been relieved of his post.
“Hindi lang po matatapos ito dito. We are going after the entire institution, all the rotten eggs,” Remulla said.
(This will not end here, we are going after the entire institution, all the rotten eggs)
BFP Officer-in-Charge Wilberto Kwan Tiu stressed in the same press briefing that the BFP will not require any payment from its applicants.
“Inuulit ko po, walang bayad ang pagpasok sa aming ahensya. Libre po ito,” Kwan Tiu said.
(I repeat, there’s no payment required to join our agency. This is free)
‘Syndicates’
Kwan Tiu said they have since implemented electronic hiring systems to address the slots for sale scheme.
He, however, admitted that as the agency’s systems evolve, the modus of those involved in the scheme also adapts.
Remulla, meanwhile, said the CIDG has already subpoenaed the fire officers who were identified as beneficiaries of the slots for sale scheme as part of the further investigation.
“They can either testify kung ano ang nangyari, or we can charge them because we already saw conclusive links na nagbayad sila,” Remulla said.
Remulla added that those who testify may be given clemency and can continue their service, as long as they will “spill all the beans”. Otherwise, they will be dismissed.
When asked if he can eradicate the corruption issue in the BFP under his term, Remulla said the DILG will remove the "syndicates" within six months.
“Sa PNP tinanggal na natin lahat ng sindikato. Within the BFP matatanggal ko rin lahat ng sindikatong ito,” Remulla said.
(We have already removed all the syndicates from the PNP. I will also remove all these syndicates from the BFP.)

articles.title: 'One-strike lang': DPWH continues to carry out lifestyle checks, Dizon tells House
articles.summary: Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon has assured the House of Representatives on continued lifestyle checks in the agency as an antii-corruption measure. Dizon made…

blocks.text: Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon has assured the House of Representatives on continued lifestyle checks in the agency as an antii-corruption measure.
Dizon made the pronouncement during the DPWH's recent budget hearing before the House Committee on Appropriations.
During the DPWH budget hearing, Akbayan Party-list Rep. Chel Diokno asked how regularly the department conducts lifestyle checks and stressed the need for stronger accountability mechanisms.
Dizon says lifestyle checks are conducted continuously in coordination with the Office of the Ombudsman.
He also said the DPWH has adopted a “one-strike policy” under which verified reports of wrongdoing may lead to show-cause orders, suspension, or termination.
“Tuluy-tuloy po ang...aming lifestyle checks (Our lifestyle checks are continuous). In fact, we are working very very closely with the Office of the Ombudsman on this,” he said.

“In some cases, we have even terminated people just based on reports on social media that have been properly verified and validated. So, tuluy-tuloy po tayo diyan (So, we are continuing with that)," noted the DPWH head honcho.
Dizon also said the DPWH was working on additional waiver and disclosure requirements beyond existing statements of assets and liabilities, including stronger conflict-of-interest disclosures.
He added that the department is working with the SEC on stricter disclosure standards for private contractors handling public funds.
Meanwhile, Diokno urged the DPWH to develop a national flood control and drainage plan after Dizon said the agency was shifting toward interventions at the major river-basin level.

“Kung wala tayong national plan at hindi nakasaad doon kung ano 'yung mga general principles that should apply anywhere in the country…para rin tayo…by analogy, wala tayong national land use plan,” the solon said
(If we don't have a national plan and it doesn't state the general principles that should apply anywhere in the country…then, by analogy, it's as if we don't have a national land use plan.)
“How can we expect to develop rationally in the coming five, 10 or 15 years without this kind of comprehensive approach?” he asked.
Diokno says a national master plan is needed to coordinate flood control efforts and provide a long-term strategy, particularly after seeing firsthand the impact of flooding in Pampanga.

“Just the other day nakapunta po ako ng ilang bahagi ng Pampanga (I visited some parts of Pampanga), where flooding has not just been a recurring, but appears to be a perennial problem…Everything comes to a standstill when an area is flooded and the water doesn't go down,” he shared.

“Iyong estudyante natin, hindi nakakapasok sa eskuwelahan, 'yung mga manggagawa natin, hindi rin nakakapasok sa kanilang mga opisina. Mismo 'yung buong ekonomiya ay wala nang gagalaw. And in the areas that I visited, they were telling me that this has been happening to them not just for weeks and for months, but halos taon-taon, umaabot na daw sa dekada na ganito nga,” he said.

(Our students cannot go to school, our workers cannot get to their offices, and the entire economy comes to a standstill. In the areas I visited, they told me this has been happening not just for weeks or months, but almost every year, and has supposedly been going on like this for decades.)

According to Diokno, the recurring impact of flooding on communities and the economy underscored the need for a comprehensive, long-term national flood control and drainage plan to guide government interventions.

articles.title: Overstaying Chinese with alleged POGO ties caught in Bacolod
articles.summary: BACOLOD CITY – A 34-year-old Chinese national with suspected links to previous operations of a Philippine Offshore Gaming Operator (POGO) was recently arrested by the Bureau of Immigration (BI)…

blocks.text: BACOLOD CITY – A 34-year-old Chinese national with suspected links to previous operations of a Philippine Offshore Gaming Operator (POGO) was recently arrested by the Bureau of Immigration (BI) operatives in Barangay 16 here, following information from government intelligence sources.

In a report posted on BI’s website on Thursday, August 27, the suspect identified as Xie failed to present any identification and was later found to have not extended his visa, making him an overstaying alien.

The BI also tagged him as an undesirable alien, given his alleged links to online gaming operations. Before traveling to this city, the suspect, according to the BI, admitted to have previously worked in Manila as a fruit vendor.

Police Major Eugene Tolentino, head of Police Station 1, said that BI coordinated with them regarding the operation, but they have no idea regarding the suspect’s background and other information, including why he was in the city, as it is confidential.
The suspect was immediately transferred to the BI’s holding facility in Bicutan, where he will remain while facing deportation charges filed against him.

The BI’s operation here was also in coordination with the Negros Occidental Police Provincial Office in line with the directive of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to ensure that the country is protected from illegal aliens abusing the hospitality of the country.

In a statement, BI Commissioner Joel Anthony Viado emphasized that the agency’s strong coordination with the intelligence community allows the BI to multiply its forces and monitor movements of foreign nationals nationwide.

articles.title: PH, UK open talks on proposed visiting forces pact – DND
articles.summary: The Department of National Defense (DND) said it started discussions on a proposed agreement that could pave the way for greater defense cooperation and military interoperability with the United…

blocks.text: The Department of National Defense (DND) said it started discussions on a proposed agreement that could pave the way for greater defense cooperation and military interoperability with the United Kingdom (UK).

The first round of formal negotiations on the proposed Status of Visiting Forces Agreement (SOVFA) was held on Thursday, Aug. 27, with DND Undersecretary for Acquisition and Resource Management Salvador Melchor B. Mison Jr. leading the Philippine negotiating panel while Amy Senior, head of Indo-Pacific at the UK Ministry of Defence, led the British side.
The arrangement will provide a legal framework for military personnel to conduct exercises, training, and other activities in each other's territory.
Mison said the Philippines valued Britain’s support as the two countries work to strengthen their defense partnership.

“We appreciate UK’s unqualified support as a like-minded partner in upholding the rules-based international order and preserving freedoms ensured by the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS),” Mison said.
The negotiations covered ways to strengthen strategic defense initiatives and improve interoperability between the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and their British counterparts.
The discussions also highlighted the two countries’ shared commitment to the rule of law, regional and international security, and the rules-based international order.
Manila and London seek to expand defense cooperation across regions and address increasingly complex security challenges in the Indo-Pacific.
The DND said the proposed SOVFA is another step in strengthening bilateral defense and military ties, and is also expected to support greater cooperation between the two countries’ armed forces.
The first round of negotiations was attended by key officials from the DND and other Philippine government agencies, along with members of the UK negotiating panel.

As of writing, Manila has six countries covered by a VFA, SOVFA, or a similar military access arrangement, namely the United States, Australia, Japan (Reciprocal Access Agreement), New Zealand, Canada, and France.

articles.title: Delivery rider surrenders package of marijuana he was hired to deliver to Laguna
articles.summary: STA. CRUZ, Laguna- A delivery rider voluntarily surrendered suspected illegal drugs worth P220,000 to police here on Aug. 27, here. Santa Cruz Municipal Police Station (MPS) in Poblacion 3, Santa…

blocks.text: STA. CRUZ, Laguna- A delivery rider voluntarily surrendered suspected illegal drugs worth P220,000 to police here on Aug. 27, here.
Santa Cruz Municipal Police Station (MPS) in Poblacion 3, Santa Cruz, Laguna.

According to the rider, he picked up the parcels in front of Tanza Doctors Hospital in Tanza, Cavite, and was instructed him to deliver it to Barangay Sto. Angel Sur, Santa Cruz, Laguna at about 2:30 a.m.
Upon arriving at the designated delivery location, the intended recipient reportedly fled before the transaction could be completed.
He suspected that the parcels contained illegal substances, and he proceeded to the Sta. Cruz MPS and voluntarily turned over the items to authorities.
The items were turned over

eight unsealed paper boxes, each containing a plastic pouch and avape pen labeled “Tiny,” containing a liquid substance suspected to be marijuana. The items have an estimated value of P20,000 a bundle of suspected dried marijuana leaves, weighing approximately one kilogram, with an estimated value of P200,000.
Police Lt. Col. Jojo Sabeniano, Sta. Cruz police chief commended the rider for his integrity and cooperation with law enforcement.

“This is a clear example of community partnership. The driver did the right thing—he refused to participate in illegal activity and helped prevent prohibited substances from circulating in our community. We encourage everyone to follow his lead and report suspicious items or transactions to the nearest police station.” Sabeniano added.

The Sta. Cruz MPS continues to encourage members of the community to remain vigilant and immediately report suspicious packages, transactions, or other activities that may be connected to illegal drugs.

articles.title: US, South Korea and Japan to hold trilateral drill as North Korea ramps up pressure on US
articles.summary: SEOUL, South Korea (AP) — South Korea, the U.S. and Japan will go ahead with a trilateral military drill next month to better deal with North Korean nuclear threats, officials in Seoul said Friday, a…

blocks.text: In this photo provided by South Korea Defense Ministry, warships of South Korea, the United States and Japan including the USS George Washington aircraft carrier, bottom center, take part in the trilateral Freedom Edge exercise in international waters off South Korea's southern island of Jeju, on Nov. 13, 2024. (South Korea Defense Ministry via AP, File)

SEOUL, South Korea (AP) — South Korea, the U.S. and Japan will go ahead with a trilateral military drill next month to better deal with North Korean nuclear threats, officials in Seoul said Friday, a day after North Korea vowed to retaliate against what it called U.S. hostilities.

The development further dims prospects for an early resumption of diplomacy between North Korea and the U.S., despite President Donald Trump’s recent decision to scale back a major bilateral military drill with South Korea in an apparent goodwill gesture toward the North.
South Korea's military said in a statement the Freedom Edge exercise will start on Sept. 7 for a five-day run in the waters off South Korea's southern Jeju Island.
It said the exercise is defensive in nature and meant to respond to North Korean nuclear and missile threats as well as promote regional peace and stability.

North Korea has previously slammed the trilateral drill as a “reckless show of strength" that showed its adversaries' confrontational stance against it. Pyongyang has also said the drill contained a U.S. intention to lay siege to China and exert pressure on Russia.

The Freedom Edge drill, a U.S.-South Korea-Japan exercise, was launched in 2024. It's designed to increase the sophistication of previous exercises with simultaneous air and naval drills geared toward improving joint ballistic missile defense, anti-submarine warfare, surveillance and other skills and capabilities.

Last week, the U.S. and South Korean militaries ended their annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise six days earlier than originally planned, after Trump said he had ordered the Pentagon to “substantially reduce” the drill that North Korea views as an invasion rehearsal. Trump cited what he described as a good relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

But North Korea rebuffed Trump's overture, saying just shortening the drill won’t change its “provocative, aggressive nature.” North Korea launched about 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward the sea, apparently delivering on its previous threat to respond to the U.S.-South Korean drill.
Pyongyang has previously said it won’t resume diplomacy with the U.S. unless it drops its demand for a North Korean denuclearization as a precondition for talks.

Since his earlier diplomacy with Trump collapsed in 2019, Kim has boosted his military and diplomatic credentials by enlarging his nuclear arsenal and aligning with Russia over its war against Ukraine. With greater leverage now, experts say Kim would likely aim to win big U.S. concessions like an international recognition of North Korea as a nuclear state and sweeping sanctions relief in return for a partial surrender of his nuclear arsenal.

On Thursday, North Korea's Foreign Ministry accused the U.S. of engaging in “a series of hostile moves” targeting the North, including a possible sale of air-to-air missiles and related equipment to South Korea. It said North Korea “will make a serious, immediate and powerful response to the hostile acts in different spheres.”

articles.title: 'High risk' of lake breaching and causing second flood, warns China
articles.summary: China says a lake formed after a recent landslide near the Nepal-Tibet border may burst in the coming days.

blocks.text: China has warned there is a "high risk" that a lake which formed after the recent landslide near the Nepal-Tibet border may breach its banks, causing a second flood downstream.
The warning comes after Wednesday's deadly flash flood in the same area which scientists say was triggered by the collapse of a mountain glacier into a river.

As of Friday morning, an estimated 2.5 million cubic metres of water had accumulated at the barrier lake, according to state broadcaster CCTV. A barrier lake is a body of water formed when debris dams up a river.
Officials said that three million cubic metres of water is expected to flow into the lake between Thursday and the weekend, posing a "high risk of breach".

The barrier lake, which formed at the confluence of the Chhochen Khola and Purepu Tsangpo rivers, has already started to overflow, according to China's Ministry of Water Resources. The area has also seen heavy rain.
Authorities have sent engineering teams to monitor the lake's water levels and the atmospheric conditions.

A CCTV report on Friday morning said that most of the Chinese emergency services were stuck at a village about 7km (4 miles) from Gyirong Port, the major land crossing linking Nepal and China which was hit by Wednesday's massive flood.
This was because the barrier lake was "overflowing non-stop" which could lead to fresh floods or debris flows.
Due to the risks, search and rescue operations had to be suspended near the Nepal-Tibet border, according to the report.

articles.title: White House construction contributed to radio problems that let Trump copter come close to jet
articles.summary: The ongoing White House construction contributed to radio problems that kept air traffic controllers from hearing calls warning that President Donald Trump's helicopter was getting ready to take off,…

blocks.text: President Donald Trump, left, walks from Marine One to board Air Force One, Friday, Aug. 21, 2026, at Joint Base Andrews, Md., en route to South Carolina. (AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin)

The ongoing White House construction contributed to radio problems that kept air traffic controllers from hearing calls warning that President Donald Trump's helicopter was getting ready to take off, so they cleared an airline jet to take off just as Marine One took to the air earlier this month, federal investigators said Thursday.

The week before the president's helicopter got too close to that Envoy Air jet near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, air traffic controllers and Marine One pilots met to discuss controllers not receiving the standard three-minute warning call ahead of Marine One flights, according to a preliminary report from the National Transportation Safety Board. They made plans to relay radio calls through someone else if there were future problems but that was also unsuccessful on the day of the Aug. 4 incident.
Communication issues came up again on Thursday, when air traffic controllers at the Reagan airport weren't able to hear Marine One and had to ask a support helicopter for help just before takeoff.
“I can’t hear Marine One," an air traffic controller says to the support helicopter. "If you hear Marine One, can you let me know?”

A little over a minute later, communication was functioning normally again for the afternoon flight to Joint Base Andrews outside Washington, according to recordings posted by ATC.com. It was not immediately clear what caused the brief issue.

Since mid-July, Trump’s helicopter has been lifting off from the Ellipse, the park south of the White House, while construction has been going on for a new helipad behind the White House. Trump on Thursday was leaving the White House to head to Texas for a Republican National Committee event and present an award to the Artemis II astronauts.

After the incident earlier this month, technicians discovered that the reason Marine One was having trouble talking to the tower at times was because the helicopter shifted to a new location during the construction. So the Federal Aviation Administration moved the radio receiver out of a neighborhood near the airport and to the top of the tower at Reagan to fix the problem.
“Even though they were aware of some previous communications issues, they never got at the root cause,” aviation safety expert Jeff Guzzetti said.
The FAA said in a statement that it took immediate action after the incident by moving that antenna “to improve communications” between the airport and Marine One pilots.
The White House didn't immediately respond to the preliminary report, although the ongoing NTSB investigation does limit what it can say about the incident.
A deadly crash in 2025 prompted new safety procedures

Having both the jet and helicopter in the air at the same time also seemed to violate safety procedures put in place after last year’s midair collision near the busy airport that killed 67 people, but officials stressed that the president was never in danger. The Pentagon also has a longstanding agreement with the FAA to provide controllers with a three-minute warning before the president’s helicopter takes off that predates last year’s crash.

The NTSB said recordings from the tower showed that the controllers never heard the calls from Marine One's pilot that day warning that the helicopter was getting ready to take off, but separate recordings posted by ATC.com show the helicopter did make those calls.
The helicopter pilots tried to relay their three-minute call through the helicopter facility at Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling, but that was also unsuccessful.

The FAA decided after an airliner collided with an Army Black Hawk helicopter on Jan. 29, 2025, that all takeoffs and landings at the airport would be halted anytime a helicopter passes by on a conflicting route. The airspace near the White House and Reagan is heavily congested with military and commercial aircraft.

The FAA has acknowledged that the helicopter and airliner briefly got too close before the two aircraft started to move away from each other. The airplane quickly climbed above the helicopter after Marine One’s pilots saw the plane and paused until it safely left the area.

The NTSB said preliminary estimates show the helicopter and plane were just over 0.8 mile (1.3 kilometers) apart laterally and about 700 feet (215 meters) apart vertically at their closest. The crew of the Envoy Air flight told investigators they received a traffic warning from their collision avoidance system right after they took off, but they never saw the helicopter.
The controllers didn't hear Marine One's warnings
The official FAA recordings from the tower at Reagan did not include the warnings that Marine One was getting ready to head to Andrews Air Force Base with the president aboard that day.

A recording posted by ATC.com showed the Marine One pilot telling the tower that the helicopter was “three minutes to lift” just like the 2013 agreement between the FAA and the military calls for. But the controller seemed surprised a few minutes later when the helicopter took off.
“Uh, Marine One, you said, uh, you’re proceeding as briefed?” the controller asked before giving the helicopter directions and commenting, “OK, no three minutes, roger, proceed as briefed.”
After the controller warned the helicopter about the plane taking off, the Marine One pilot said he saw the traffic and declared, “We’ll be doing a momentary delay.”

Guzzetti, who is a former crash investigator for both the NTSB and FAA, said he doesn't fault the controllers because they never heard Marine One's warnings. And once they did realize the helicopter was taking off, they quickly warned the pilots and ordered another plane coming in to Reagan to abort landing and circle around.

“In this case, the controller did absolutely nothing wrong. He did not receive the transmission saying that they were three minutes away from taking off. So, he had no reason to hold the airplane that was lining up and waiting,” Guzzetti said.

After last year’s midair collision, it became clear that poor communication between air traffic controllers and the military had been a longstanding issue. During a congressional hearing, it came out that a hotline connecting the Pentagon to the tower at Reagan hadn’t been working for more than three years, and the FAA hadn’t even realized it.

The NTSB said that after this incident involving Marine One, FAA technicians determined that there wasn't adequate line of sight between the radio receiver at the airport and the location where the helicopter takes off at the White House. So those radios were moved from the neighborhood where they had been located to the top of the tower at Reagan. Subsequent tests showed the radios working well after that change.

articles.title: 3 family members critical after LPG tank blast in Valenzuela
articles.summary: Three family members were critically injured after an LPG tank exploded inside their apartment in Barangay Bagbaguin, Valenzuela City, on Thursday morning, Aug. 27. The victims were identified as…

blocks.text: An LPG tank exploded in an apartment in Barangay Bagbaguin, Valenzuela City, on Thursday, Aug. 27. (Screengrab from Facebook)
Three family members were critically injured after an LPG tank exploded inside their apartment in Barangay Bagbaguin, Valenzuela City, on Thursday morning, Aug. 27.
The victims were identified as aliases “Rodolfo,” a senior citizen, and his two children, “Roderick” and “Lodivina,” who sustained burns and suffered smoke inhalation during the explosion.
Authorities said the three were rushed to a hospital.
The explosion also damaged nearby properties.
Closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage showed a parked motorcycle being knocked off balance as several items were scattered by the force of the blast.
The explosion dislodged the window grills of a nearby house and sparked a fire that gutted the apartment unit.
Residents, barangay personnel, Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) members, and fire volunteers worked together to put out the blaze.
Authorities are looking into a possible LPG leak as the cause of the explosion.
Responding fire volunteers said gas may have accumulated inside the enclosed apartment before igniting.
The BFP is continuing its investigation into the incident.
The Valenzuela City government, meanwhile, assured the victims’ family of assistance as they recover.

articles.title: Search, retrieval Operations in Mapanuepe Lake drowning incident suspended due to bad weather
articles.summary: SAN MARCELINO, Zambales — Search, rescue and retrieval operations for the victims of the drowning incident at Mapanuepe Lake in Barangay Buhawen here remained suspended Friday, August 28, due to…

blocks.text: SAN MARCELINO, Zambales — Search, rescue and retrieval operations for the victims of the drowning incident at Mapanuepe Lake in Barangay Buhawen here remained suspended Friday, August 28, due to inclement weather conditions in the area.

Three passengers remain missing after the motorized banca they were riding while they were headed home to Sitio Lumibao capsized in the waters off Barangay Buhawen. Six others, all members of an Aeta community, were earlier reported to have drowned in the incident.

A report from the office of Col.Benjamin Ariola, Zambales PPO ditrector said that, as of 10:30 a.m., personnel from the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) Station Zambales, San Marcelino Municipal Police Station, Second Provincial Mobile Force Company of the Zambales Police Provincial Office, Olongapo Maritime, Bureau of Fire Protection, and municipal disaster risk reduction and management offices of San Marcelino and San Antonio were involved in the operation.
PCG Station Zambales conducted an initial assessment of the area at around 6 a.m. Friday but operating units were unable to proceed with the search, rescue and retrieval activities.
It was learned that prevailing weather conditions posed safety risks to responders.
Authorities said operations will resume once weather and safety conditions permit.
The Incident Command System (ICS) has also been activated, with an Incident Command Post (ICP) established at the Barangay Hall of Buhawen to coordinate the ongoing response.
The operation is being supervise by Police Maj. Exodus Rodriguez, who serves as the designated point of contact for the incident.

articles.title: Serendipity, your name is Nicholas: 'The Notebook: The Musical'
articles.summary: If you count yourself among the millions who have picked up and read the Nicholas Sparks novel "The Notebook," published in 1996, or have watched and swooned over the 2004 film adaptation that…

blocks.text: The cast of The Notebook, with director Nicholas Polonio seated in the center.

If you count yourself among the millions who have picked up and read the Nicholas Sparks novel "The Notebook," published in 1996, or have watched and swooned over the 2004 film adaptation that starred Ryan Gosling and Rachel McAdams, alongside James Garner and Gena Rowlands as the older iterations of Noah and Allie; then you’ll be more than ready to support Theatre Group Asia’s (TGA) mounting of "The Notebook: The Musical," with songs by Ingrid Michaelson, and Bekah Brunstetter providing the book.

To be directed by Filipino-American Nicholas Polonio - and that’s the serendipity of my title, the two Nicholas - Polonio emphasizes that this will not be a carbon copy of the Broadway staging; as it will be stamped by his own sense of stage, storytelling, and inspiration. Plus there is a personal connection, as Polonio spent his High School years in North Carolina, the setting for Sparks’ novel, the musical’s source material.

I must be one of the very few at the media event that had never read the book, or watched the film. At the time it came out, I was a snob about tearjerker romance novels; and didn’t have any interest in watching the film eight years later. Produced for a lowly $29 million, the film grossed over $118 million, a certified box office hit; and spawned an astounding second life as a cult classic for romance enthusiasts. So my real connection to this musical would have to be singer-songwriter Ingrid Michaelson, who provides the music and lyrics - I have CD’s of her "Everybody" (2009) and "Lights Out" (2014) albums.

blocks.caption: From top left, clockwise; Sheena Belarmino, Morissette, and Celeste Legaspi.

blocks.text: From top left, clockwise; Sheena Belarmino, Morissette, and Celeste Legaspi.

I really enjoy her songs, so I was curious to hear what she had come up with for this musical that opened on Broadway in March of 2024. For me, some of the curiosity stemmed from wanting to hear how different it would be from the efforts of another singer-songwriter I admire, Sara Bareilles, and her work on "Waitress: The Musical."

Running from September 3 to the 20th at the Samsung Performing Arts Theater in Circuit Makati, this opener of the TGA’s 2026-2027 season, this "The Notebook: The Musical" is actually the first international production of the Broadway musical.

With a story that moves between youth and old age, there are three sets of actors portraying the central pair of Allie and Noah. The Older Allie and Noah who actually open the musical are tackled by Celeste Legaspi and Rody Vera. Morissette and Laurence Mossman take on Middle Allie and Noah; and Young Allie and Noah are Sheena Belarmino and Benedix Ramos. The strong support cast include the likes of Carla Guevara-Laforteza, Floyd Tena, Markki Stroem, Felicity Napuli, Omar Uddin, Kathleen Francisco, Shaun Ocrisma, and Jillian Ita-as.

blocks.caption: Benedix Ramos, Rody Vera, and Laurence Mossman.

blocks.text: Benedix Ramos, Rody Vera, and Laurence Mossman.

A story about love, grief, fidelity, fate, and longing - the musical is guaranteed to produce tears that the audience will either be holding back, or allow to freely flow. So if you plan to watch this, make sure you’re brining your own hankie or tissues. It’s highly doubtful that there will be many dry eyes by the time the musical has its curtain call. And no, I’m not going to spoil you by revealing anything about the plot. And that’s because I don’t have any idea, welcoming the fact that I’ll be watching this ‘blind’.

The musical numbers that I heard during the media event were great. Emotional, filled with depth, and allowing the singers to reach notes that should be placing the audience on the edge of their seats, and spontaneously breaking into rapturous applause. And for Morissette, this musical marks her return to the stage after 14 years. In 2012, she was in the cast of Disney’s "Camp Rock."
Three weekends in September mark the run of "The Notebook: The Musical"; so best to book your seats now, and not wait for word of mouth to get you scrambling for tickets.

articles.title: Tokyo toy show kicks off
articles.summary: TOKYO (Jiji Press) -- More than 180 toy makers are exhibiting new products and flagship items, including those targeting so-called kidults, or adults who enjoy playing with toys, and inbound…

blocks.text: Tokyo Toy Show opens at Tokyo Big Sight on Thursday, Aug. 27.

TOKYO (Jiji Press) -- More than 180 toy makers are exhibiting new products and flagship items, including those targeting so-called kidults, or adults who enjoy playing with toys, and inbound tourists, as an annual Japanese toy show kicked off in Tokyo on Thursday.

Bandai Co. is displaying the Tamagotchi ring, a 2.8-centimeter device that commemorates the 30th anniversary of the debut of its iconic Tamagotchi virtual pet series. It allows users to raise 30 different characters.

The company has a section dedicated to the popular manga and anime franchise "Chiikawa." Among the products on display is the Chiikawa Phone Smart, a toy equipped with a camera and apps that allows children to enjoy a realistic smartphone experience.
Tomy Co. is exhibiting a model of Plarail railway toys designed after the iconic Doctor Yellow high-speed test train. Its 47-centimeter length allows it to run powerfully on the track.
Some toys reflect recent social trends, such as MegaHouse Corp.'s Investment Ranking, a board game in which players grow their wealth by investing in stocks and cryptocurrencies.

Amid rising electricity fees, Bandai's power generator-like toy, designed with a character from the children's picture book and anime series "Anpanman," teaches children about the importance of electricity as they enjoy sounds and lights generated by power produced through a hand crank.
The Tokyo Toy Show will run through Sunday at the Tokyo Big Sight convention center.
The Japanese toy market hit a record high of 1,166.4 billion yen in fiscal 2025, which ended last March, according to the Japan Toy Association, which organizes the show.

articles.title: 2,500 people remain in evacuation centers a month after Kumamoto quake
articles.summary: KUMAMOTO (Jiji Press) -- Nearly 2,500 people are still staying in evacuation centers amid scorching heat one month after a powerful earthquake hit the southwestern Japan prefecture of Kumamoto. While…

blocks.text: KUMAMOTO (Jiji Press) -- Nearly 2,500 people are still staying in evacuation centers amid scorching heat one month after a powerful earthquake hit the southwestern Japan prefecture of Kumamoto.
While efforts toward recovery and reconstruction are underway, challenges remain numerous, with water supply still disrupted in some areas.

According to the Kumamoto prefectural government's disaster response headquarters, 38 people were confirmed dead as a result of the July 28 quake, and 33 remained seriously injured, as of 2 p.m. Thursday. Two of the deaths are believed to have been disaster-related, stemming from factors such as heatstroke.
The number of evacuees has fallen to 2,460 at 61 shelters in 11 municipalities, down sharply from 10,467 at 415 shelters as of July 30.
Each municipality is also working to identify people sheltering at home or in their vehicles through door-to-door visits and other efforts.

The 7.1-magnitude earthquake damaged 42,222 houses, including 4,940 that were destroyed or severely damaged and 27,248 that sustained some damage. The extent of damage to 10,034 homes has yet to be determined.
The construction of temporary housing has begun, with residents expected to start moving in on Sept. 5.
However, water supply disruptions remain a major obstacle to rebuilding lives.

Although water supply and sewer service disruptions are expected to be resolved by the end of the month, about 4,400 households in the city of Yatsushiro, where the maximum seismic intensity reached 7, the highest on the Japanese scale, had wells used for daily water supplies damaged.

blocks.caption: Messages and drinks are left at a flower stand at the Aeon Mall Kumamoto shopping complex, where seven people were killed in an explosion following the July 28 earthquake, in Kashima, Kumamoto Prefecture, on Thursday.

blocks.text: Messages and drinks are left at a flower stand at the Aeon Mall Kumamoto shopping complex, where seven people were killed in an explosion following the July 28 earthquake, in Kashima, Kumamoto Prefecture, on Thursday.
The prefectural government is working with the central government to address the problem, but there is no timetable for a full recovery.

Economic damage to businesses and industries totaled about 155.9 billion yen as of Tuesday, while damage to agriculture, forestry and fisheries businesses reached about 110.2 billion yen. Both figures are expected to increase further.
A survey found that cancellations at accommodations across the prefecture totaled about 190,000 people, representing roughly 2.7 billion yen in lost revenue.
A total of some 140,000 volunteers had taken part in relief efforts across 11 municipalities as of Tuesday.

Buses for disaster relief volunteers departing from the city of Kumamoto to the cities of Uki and Yatsushiro and the town of Hikawa, which were devastated by the earthquake, are scheduled to begin operating in stages from Saturday.

articles.title: 2 women caught in entrapment for robbery with intimidation in Lipa City
articles.summary: CAMP MIGUEL MALVAR, Batangas City — Police arrested two women were arrested in an entrapment operation for alleged robbery with intimidation on Thursday afternoon, Aug. 27 at a convenience store in…

blocks.text: CAMP MIGUEL MALVAR, Batangas City — Police arrested two women were arrested in an entrapment operation for alleged robbery with intimidation on Thursday afternoon, Aug. 27 at a convenience store in Bigben Complex, Barangay Mataas na Lupa, Lipa City, Batangas.
The Batangas Police Provincial Office (BPPO), director Col. Oliver Ebora identified the suspects as Marjorie, 32, jobless, and Kaye, 28, a laundry attendant, both residents of Lipa City, Batangas.

At about 12:15 p.m. Lipa City police conducted operation after a 50-year-old victim filed a complaint that Marjorie was extorting money from him for the supposed settlement of a rape complaint that was earlier filed against him.
The victim had previously given the suspects P100,000 after which they allegedly demanded an additional
According to the victim, the suspects sent him a purported subpoena allegedly issued by the Office of the City Prosecutor of Lipa, indicating that a rape complaint had been filed against him.
Upon verification, the subpoena and the purported complaint were found to be fraudulent and non-existent.

The suspects also allegedly sent the victim a text message in which the sender misrepresented herself as Police Lt. Col.Aleli Buaquen, Lipa City police chief and instructed him to coordinate and settle the matter amicably.
Following the successful completion of the transaction and after the suspects received the marked money from the victim, the operating police immediately effected their arrest.
Police recovered the marked money used in the operation , a Settlement Agreement containing the signatures of the victim and one of the suspects, and acellular phone.
“We will not tolerate individuals who exploit fear, impersonate government officials, and use fabricated documents to extort money from our citizens, said Ebora.
The Batangas PPO remains committed to protecting the public and holding accountable those who abuse the name and authority of the police,” Ebora added.
An appropriate charges are being prepared for filing before the Lipa City Prosecutor’s Office.

articles.title: Okinawa governor race opens; LDP seeks comeback after 12 years
articles.summary: NAHA, Okinawa Pref. (Jiji Press) -- The official campaign period began on Thursday for the Sept. 13 gubernatorial election for Japan's southernmost prefecture of Okinawa. The focus is whether the…

blocks.text: Okinawa Governor Denny Tamaki (right) and Genta Koja, former vice mayor of Naha, Okinawa Prefecture, make their first campaign speeches Thursday after filing candidacies in the Sept. 13 Okinawa gubernatorial election.
NAHA, Okinawa Pref. (Jiji Press) -- The official campaign period began on Thursday for the Sept. 13 gubernatorial election for Japan's southernmost prefecture of Okinawa.

The focus is whether the Liberal Democratic Party will be able to retake the helm of the prefecture after a break of about 12 years. The outcome is likely to affect the administration of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, the party's president.

On Thursday, six people filed their candidacies, including LDP-backed Genta Koja, 42, former vice mayor of Naha, Okinawa's capital, and incumbent Governor Denny Tamaki, 66, who seeks a third four-year term.

Key election issues include a project to relocate the U.S. Marine Corps' Futenma air station in the Okinawa city of Ginowan to the Henoko coastal district in Nago, another Okinawa city, as well as Okinawa's economic development.

Delivering his first campaign speech in Naha, Koja said that high prices and traffic congestion are major problems the prefecture needs to tackle, pledging to "change a stagnant prefectural government into one that moves ahead."
Tamaki, speaking in the town of Motobu, stressed: "Everything is for the people of the prefecture and for the future. I will devote myself wholeheartedly to serving the people of the prefecture."
Tamaki, who opposes the U.S. base relocation, again receives the backing of the All Okinawa camp, which brings together progressive forces and some conservatives.

But the camp has suffered a string of defeats in recent mayoral elections. Tamaki therefore prioritizes unaffiliated voters. He did not seek recommendations from the Constitutional Democratic Party of Japan, the Japanese Communist Party or the Social Democratic Party, all of which are members of the camp.
Koja, who accepts the base relocation, is backed by the LDP, the Japan Innovation Party, the Democratic Party for the People, Sanseito and the Conservative Party of Japan.

His campaign team expects to gain additional votes from conservatives after Mikio Shimoji, a former lawmaker of the House of Representatives, the lower chamber of the Diet, the country's parliament, concluded a policy agreement with the LDP and scrapped his plan to run.

Meanwhile, Koja lacks name recognition. Another concern is that Komeito, which left the LDP-led coalition last year, has limited the scope of its backing to a recommendation from its Okinawa prefectural chapter.
The Centrist Reform Alliance, formed by Lower House lawmakers from the CDP and Komeito, has left its members free to vote independently.
The base relocation issue has long been central to Okinawa's gubernatorial elections.

Tamaki, however, came under criticism after a 17-year-old high school girl died in a March boat accident during a peace education program organized by a group supporting Tamaki. The girl was visiting Henoko on a school trip to see the planned U.S. base relocation site.
He plans to emphasize his track record over the past eight years in office, including strong performance of the tourism sector.
Koja has pledged to double per capita prefectural income.
The other four candidates are company head Shun Kaneshima, 48, medical corporation leader Masahiro Sueyoshi, 73, company representative Takashi Higa, 49, and political group leader Chosuke Yara, 74.
The upcoming gubernatorial election, the 15th of its kind since Okinawa's reversion to Japan in 1972, has the largest number of candidates among the races.

articles.title: DOE, PNOC fast-track offshore wind infra ahead of clean energy auction
articles.summary: The government moved to resolve regulatory bottlenecks hanging over its nascent offshore wind (OSW) market, securing land and coastal access rights for support infrastructure ahead of the landmark…

blocks.text: The government moved to resolve regulatory bottlenecks hanging over its nascent offshore wind (OSW) market, securing land and coastal access rights for support infrastructure ahead of the landmark capacity auction.

On Aug. 28, the Department of Energy (DOE) and state-run Philippine National Oil Co. (PNOC) signed a memorandum of agreement to acquire tenurial instruments across auxiliary onshore and coastal zones.
Under the agreement, the two agencies will secure coastal and land access rights for all upcoming OSW infrastructure prior to the tender.
“The partnership strengthens inter-agency collaboration in streamlining project requirements and advancing the country’s offshore wind potential,” PNOC said in a statement.

As developers prepare to roll out offshore wind projects, Energy Secretary Sharon Garin highlighted European firms on Thursday as key drivers of the country's clean energy transition. She noted that their expertise in offshore wind, grid modernization, and project financing can convert local energy ambitions into viable, operational developments.
“Offshore wind represents a major part of this opportunity, with our upcoming auction targeting 3.3 gigawatts (GW) of capacity,” Garin said.

“Beyond electricity generation, offshore wind can mobilize investment across ports, supply chains, engineering, manufacturing, and local employment—areas where European technology, financing, and expertise can play a significant role,” sge added.

With tenurial rights secured, the DOE is set to launch the fifth round of the Green Energy Auction (GEA-5) on Dec. 1. The agency expects to issue early contract awards by Dec. 2, with the final bidding phase running through June 30, 2027.

The bidding program comes after significant delays. Energy Undersecretary Rowena Guevara previously noted that the recalibrated framework addresses logistical, administrative, and operational bottlenecks. Specifically, it establishes clear administrative structures for environmental fees, performance bonds, monitoring funds, and auxiliary onshore arrangements.
The DOE is expected to release formal authorization to proceed with GEA-5 by Oct. 2, alongside finalized guidelines for developers and prospective bidders.

articles.title: Trump orders Lake Ontario to be renamed ‘Lake America’
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, United States — US President Donald Trump stepped up an escalating feud with Canada on Thursday, ordering that Lake Ontario — a body of water shared by both countries — be renamed…

blocks.caption: A Canadian flag flies along the waterfront of Lake Ontario, in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, on August 27, 2026. (Photo by Cole Burston / AFP)

blocks.text: WASHINGTON, United States — US President Donald Trump stepped up an escalating feud with Canada on Thursday, ordering that Lake Ontario — a body of water shared by both countries — be renamed “Lake America.”
Trump signed an executive order on the name change at the White House, further trolling Canada as the North American neighbors plunge deeper into a trade war.
“We’re going to be changing the name of Lake Ontario effective immediately to Lake America,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.
Behind Trump’s desk were two maps of the US-Canada border — one with the words “Lake America” in red over the lake, and the other with the header “Making the Great Lakes Even Greater.”
Asked why he was targeting an ally for punishment instead of America’s adversaries, Trump replied: “The Canadian officials have treated us very badly. They’re nasty people.”
“People, oftentimes, they’ll ask me who’s the worst to deal with on trade? And I said that’s easy. Canada. They are the worst to trade with,” the 80-year-old Republican added.

Canada did not immediately comment but is unlikely to accept the renaming of Lake Ontario, the smallest of the five Great Lakes by surface area, which borders Canada’s Ontario province and New York state.
US-Canada trade talks collapsed at the eleventh hour last week, with Trump’s tariffs taking effect on Saturday.
Canada responded with tit-for-tat tariffs on Tuesday, with Prime Minister Mark Carney saying: “You’re at war when you get attacked. We got attacked.”
The same day, Trump announced that he was giving “serious consideration” to changing the name to Lake America.
He then posted a TikTok video late Wednesday saying that he intended to do so after all.
‘Now all we need is an ocean’
The name change mirrors Trump’s unilateral altering of the name of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America on his first day back in office in January 2025.
That change obliged the US federal government to refer to the gulf by the new designation, although Mexico has rejected any move to rename it and it lacks international recognition.

Trump said the name change was “something I’ve been thinking about for a long time, actually. As you know, we took something called the Gulf of Mexico, we changed it, and now it’s very routinely the Gulf of America.”
Trump also hinted at renaming oceans that border the United States.

“So, if you think about it, we have a gulf, and we have a lake. Now all we need is an ocean. So, maybe we’ll have to change the name of the Atlantic and/or the Pacific. Maybe we’ll change them both,” he said.

While Lake Ontario shares its name with the Canadian province, the name itself is derived from the indigenous Huron word “Ontari’io,” which means “great lake” or “beautiful water,” according to the National Museum of the Great Lakes.
Toronto, Canada’s largest city, sits on its northwestern shore.
During his second presidential term, Trump has irked a series of allies with his outlandish territorial claims, including that Canada should become the 51st US state.
Trump has also laid claim to Greenland, an autonomous territory of NATO ally Denmark, and talked about making Venezuela a state following the US capture of its leader Nicolas Maduro.

articles.title: Norway holds its breath as King Harald’s health deteriorates
articles.summary: OSLO, Norway – Norway’s royal family gathered Thursday at King Harald V’s bedside in hospital, while hundreds paid respects outside the palace, after the court announced that the…

blocks.text: OSLO, Norway – Norway’s royal family gathered Thursday at King Harald V’s bedside in hospital, while hundreds paid respects outside the palace, after the court announced that the 89-year-old monarch’s health condition was “extremely serious”.

Queen Sonja and Harald’s 53-year-old son Crown Prince Haakon, who is acting as regent, have cancelled all royal engagements and spent much of Thursday at his side at Oslo University Hospital along with other family members.
The palace said late Thursday afternoon the king’s condition was “unchanged”, shortly after Haakon, his wife Mette-Marit and their two adult children were seen leaving the hospital.
Norwegian broadcaster NRK then on Thursday evening reported that Haakon and Mette-Marit had returned to the hospital a second time.

Europe’s oldest reigning monarch has been in hospital in Oslo since August 17 suffering from haemolytic anaemia, a condition caused by an abnormally rapid destruction of red blood cells which leads to fatigue and shortness of breath.
“His Majesty the King’s health condition is extremely serious,” the palace said, providing no specific details.

Mette-Marit’s son from a previous relationship, Marius Borg Hoiby, who is under house arrest and wearing an ankle bracelet after a rape conviction in June that he has appealed, was also seen leaving the hospital after a more than four-hour visit, as was the king’s sister.
Hundreds of people gathered outside the palace in central Oslo, with many laying down bouquets of flowers for the broadly popular king in front while staying for hours.
“He is Norway’s grandfather,” 57-year-old Trine Bakke Jord told AFP, adding that she appreciated that he was so “down-to-earth” while wiping away tears.
Kaspara Bolstad, 24, told AFP Harald had been “a very steady and warm king”.

“I think the entire Norwegian people see him as a role model and as someone who brings people together. Whether you’re for or against the monarchy, I think he’s well-liked across the board,” she said.
Magnus Skaugseth, 27, agreed, lauding the king’s “inclusive” side.
“When there is so much division and polarization, he was a pillar pointing in the opposite direction.”

Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, who cancelled a work trip to Germany on Thursday following the update on the king’s health, told AFP he was “deeply affected” by the news of the king’s health condition.
“I stand together with the entire country as we now send our warmest thoughts to the king and the rest of the royal family,” he said.
Church of Norway bishops also cut short a study visit to Rome where they had met Pope Leo and were to return to Norway Thursday, according to Christian newspaper Vart Land.

Caroline Vagle, a royal reporter for the Se og Hor magazine, called Thursday’s statement from the palace “dramatic”, noting that it was usually “very restrained in its communication about the King’s health, even when he has been hospitalised or undergone treatment.”
“There is also an entire nation that is deeply concerned and saddened. King Harald is a much-loved king,” she told AFP.
The monarch was admitted to Oslo University Hospital due to fluid retention from cortisone treatment he was receiving.

articles.title: About 90 Americans unaccounted for in Nepal-Tibet catastrophic floods
articles.summary: McMINNVILLE, Tenn — US officials said about 90 American citizens remained unaccounted for Thursday, a day after catastrophic flash floods engulfed a border area of China and Nepal, killing hundreds…

blocks.caption: A government helicopter conducts a rescue mission amidst the devastation left by flash flooding in Nepal’s Nuwakot district, Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026. (AP Photo/Rajesh Kumar Singh)

blocks.text: McMINNVILLE, Tenn — US officials said about 90 American citizens remained unaccounted for Thursday, a day after catastrophic flash floods engulfed a border area of China and Nepal, killing hundreds of people. A spiritual organization said that 22 Americans associated with it were unaccounted for.
In a statement, the US State Department said it is not aware of any US deaths, but three Americans have been rescued.
Many of the missing were on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a sacred site for Hindus, Buddhists and others.

Social media posts were surfacing Thursday from loved ones pleading for people to provide updates or circulate information about Americans they had lost contact with — a Virginia woman traveling with a tour group, a Texas couple on a birthday trip and a mother accompanying her 14-year-old daughter.
Among those on a guided tour was Venus Rajnikant Patel, a 45-year-old Indian-born US citizen who recently moved from St. Louis to Cincinnati to help his family.

Patel’s brother, Dennis, said Venus called him and their parents a few hours before the floods, showing them his hotel room on the Nepalese side of the border and talking about how excited he was to cross into Tibet. He had been planning the pilgrimage for two years, his brother said.

Another American who is missing is 72-year-old Jitendra Patel, a Long Island resident who was with a tour group on a Hindu pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, according to his son, Sunny Patel. Jitendra last called Wednesday morning local time on WhatsApp to say that he had crossed the border into Tibet.

When Sunny first saw video of the flooding he thought no one could survive it, Sunny said. He then contacted his mother to ask about his father’s whereabouts. His mother said Jitendra was in the exact same area as the flooding.
“My heart sank,” Sunny said, adding that he “didn’t think it was possible that my dad would be there at ground zero.”
“It gets worse by every hour, obviously,” he added.

Indian spiritual guru Jaggi Vasudev, also known as Sadhguru, said in a post on X that 77 people returning from Mount Kailash with groups organized by his Isha Foundation were at an immigration center in Gyirong, Tibet, when the floods struck.

Leslie Crespi, a community liaison for the foundation’s US campus, said that 22 of them were Americans affiliated with the foundation and that three volunteers supporting the trekkers were also at the immigration center when the floods hit.
“We had communication with the coordinator of the group at about 9:05 Nepalese time saying that they had arrived there. And then by 9:14 is when this flash flood hit,” Crespi said.

The Isha Foundation is a spiritual organization based in India and its US campus, the Isha Institute of Inner-sciences, is a yoga and meditation retreat center located in the mountains near McMinnville, Tennessee.

At a candlelight vigil in New York City on Thursday, Tak Ruwali, a Long Island resident who is from one of the Nepalese districts affected by the flooding, said that he is talking with people in Nepal and many regional tourist guides are “out of contact now.”
“It means they are probably gone,” Ruwali added.

articles.title: Trump once saw quick end to Iran war, now says he’s in no hurry
articles.summary: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump arrives at an awkward moment for his presidency on Friday as the U.S.-Israel war against Iran reaches the six-month mark, a notable milestone for a conflict that…

blocks.caption: President Donald Trump gestures as he walks to board Marine One on the Ellipse, Friday, Aug. 14, 2026, near the White House in Washington. — Photo by Associated Press

blocks.text: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump arrives at an awkward moment for his presidency on Friday as the U.S.-Israel war against Iran reaches the six-month mark, a notable milestone for a conflict that the Republican leader repeatedly assured Americans would be a “little excursion” lasting a matter of weeks.
The war isn’t over, though Trump claims that through bombs and blockade, he has already devastated Iran’s leadership, military and economy.

And this week his administration said it would turn its focus to increasing economic pressure — rather than military action — to try to finish off Iran. The shifting strategy centers on threats to punish any country or entity that continues to conduct business with Tehran.

The turn to using sanctions as the cudgel of choice comes as the administration weighs diminished munitions stockpiles after months of war, sparking concerns that the prolonged conflict could undermine U.S. military readiness in other parts of the globe.

As the conflict grinds on, Trump’s talk of finding a quick end to the war also appears to be fading. He stressed this week that he’s “not in a hurry” to get Iran back to the negotiating table, and he continues making the case that the Islamic Republic’s leadership is on the ropes.

“They’re not paying their troops. They’re in deep trouble. They have very little capacity,” Trump told reporters Thursday. “We don’t want to speak to them. We’re not looking to meet or anything,” he said.

It’s unclear how — or if — Trump will address the six-month anniversary of a conflict that has already cost the United States more than $37.5 billion and done damage to his popularity ahead of critical November elections for his party. The president is spending Friday in Houston, where he’ll honor the Artemis II NASA crew for their 10-day mission around the moon earlier this year.
Trump is declaring ‘mission accomplished’ — a phrase that hurt a Republican predecessor

On its face, the moment is complicated for the “America First” leader who fiercely criticized his White House predecessors for wasting American taxpayer money and U.S. troops’ lives in Middle East conflicts and vowed on the campaign trail to keep the military out of “endless wars.”

But Trump has bristled at suggestions that this war — in which no American troops have deployed into Iran — can be compared to the yearslong wars in Iraq and Afghanistan in which more than 7,000 Americans were killed.

His Republican predecessor, President George W. Bush, was widely mocked for a 2003 speech aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln beneath a White House-produced banner that read “Mission Accomplished.” It came to symbolize a premature declaration of victory for the Iraq War, which would go on for nearly nine more years. More than two decades later, there are still U.S. troops stationed in Iraq.

Trump’s war has stretched on far longer than he told Americans it would. It didn’t stop him from sharing a social media post this week declaring “MISSION ACCOMPLISHED 2026.” The AI-generated image features Trump against a backdrop of U.S. fighter jets, a warship and American flags above smaller images of Bush and former Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in an Israeli strike in the opening salvos of the war.

Trump has consistently emphasized that the U.S. and Israel campaign has been devastating for Iran’s navy and air force. Iranian officials have said the country has suffered $270 billion in direct and indirect damage. Israeli military strikes in the first weeks of the war wiped out much of the theocratic government’s leadership structure, including Khamenei.

But Iran has found leverage through its own strikes in the critical Strait of Hormuz, where relatively few vessels carrying oil and liquefied natural gas are risking passage. Trump again declared Thursday that the “Strait of Hormuz is open,” saying 24 vessels passed through a day earlier. That’s a fraction of the roughly 130 vessels that passed through the vital waterway daily before the war began.
Trump is showing little interest in talks

Mediators Qatar and Pakistan continue to press for a diplomatic off-ramp from the two sides. Qatar’s prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, was in Tehran on Thursday to discuss a proposed plan between Iran and Oman to boost traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

But in Washington, Trump has shown little interest in getting back to the preliminary deal reached in June that aimed to reopen the strait and launch talks about Iran’s nuclear program. That deal fell apart within weeks after Iran started attacking ships.

At the same time, Trump says the U.S. effort to economically choke off Tehran is working, with a U.S. naval blockade preventing Iranian oil from making it to market as the trickle of vessels carrying oil from other Gulf nations pass through.
“We have control and we have the blockade,” Trump said. “Iran is not getting anything. Nothing is going through.”
Iran is badly battered, but has a history of showing resilience
There’s no doubt that the strikes combined with decades of international sanctions have battered Iran, said Aarathi Krishnan, a geopolitical risk analyst at RAKSHA Intelligence Future.

But as Trump tries to turn to a new chapter in the war, Krishnan argues the Republican may be misguided in concluding that more pressure on Tehran — which has spent decades adapting to international economic sanctions — will produce the political outcome he wants.

Indeed, Iran’s economy in the run-up to the start of the war was mired in surging inflation, according to the International Monetary Fund. National income per person had fallen from about $8,000 in 2012 to $5,000 in 2024, according to World Bank data.
But Tehran has also shown resilience, selling discounted oil and establishing opaque shipping and financial networks, Krishnan said.
“This administration has completely underestimated the Iranian resolve,” Krishnan said. “This is not new to the Iranian regime.”
Trump must decide how far he’s willing to go with sanctions

Richard Goldberg, who served as a senior adviser on Iran at the National Security Council during Trump’s first White House term, argues that Iran now finds itself in “uncharted waters” if the administration follows through with a truly biting campaign to pressure Iranian trade partners.

“What we should be seeing is an attempt to seal off every escape hatch the regime has left,” said Goldberg, who is now at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, a hawkish Washington think tank. “Use the economic power of the United States to layer a naval blockade with an air and land embargo while dropping the hammer on anyone who gives the regime access to hard currency — whether that’s in the Middle East, China or even Europe.”
But it remains to be seen how far the administration is willing to go.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent this week unveiled a campaign the White House calls “Operation Economic Outcast,” but only issued warnings to nations to cut trade and has yet to announce any secondary sanctions. Bessent told reporters the administration wanted countries to have a chance to shift away from Iran before it was too late — and acknowledged there was economic risk to the U.S., too, in moving ahead.
China, which is Iran’s biggest trade partner and oil buyer, responded by expressing its opposition to “illegal unilateral sanctions.”
Pressed Thursday about why he wasn’t already sanctioning Chinese banks, Trump offered a cryptic response.

articles.title: Death toll rises in Nepal-China border disaster as lake poses new flood threat
articles.summary: KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — Rescuers were racing to find hundreds of people still missing two days after a catastrophic flash flood struck the Himalayan border between Nepal and China, as the death toll…

blocks.text: In this photo released by Xinhua News Agency, a drone photo shows a flood-hit area in Nuwakot, Nepal on Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026. (Sulav Shrestha/Xinhua via AP)

KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — Rescuers were racing to find hundreds of people still missing two days after a catastrophic flash flood struck the Himalayan border between Nepal and China, as the death toll rose Friday and authorities warned that an overflowing lake formed after the disaster could trigger further flooding.

Nepal police said Friday morning that the country’s death toll had risen to 469 from 390 a day earlier, while China had not updated its report of just three deaths in Tibet. Together, the two countries have said that more than 1,500 people are missing.

Nepali and Chinese authorities warned of further flooding from a lake that formed upstream after Wednesday’s disaster and was already overflowing. They urged people in potentially affected areas to move to safer ground. China’s Ministry of Water Resources said Thursday that the lake held around 2 million cubic meters (70 million cubic feet) of water and was expected to receive another 3 million cubic meters (106 million cubic feet) over the next three days.

Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported Friday morning that the lake’s barrier was more than 10 kilometers (6 miles) from Gyirong Port, the border crossing with Nepal that was engulfed by mud and floodwater.
CCTV said the lake was at an elevation of 2,950 meters (9,680 feet), about 1,000 meters (3,280 feet) above Gyirong Port.
Nepal Army said that a team was sent to the border point to inspect the Bhotekoshi River amid the potential of more floods.
Thousands of people have been evacuated
Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said Friday that 3,253 people had been airlifted by helicopter from the country’s disaster area.
Flood survivors, including injured people, were taken to Kathmandu and other locations. Foreigners from multiple countries were among the missing, many of them trekkers and pilgrims.

Nepali Army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet told The Associated Press that a team had been deployed Friday to the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project near the Nepal-China border following reports that people were trapped inside a tunnel.
“It is complicated to find the entry and exit points of the tunnel because everything has been covered by mud,” Basnet said. “Our first priority is rescuing the stranded people.”

Videos of the disaster showed floodwaters destroying buildings, bridges and vehicles as people ran in front of the stories-high torrent. In the aftermath, broken concrete lay upended in expanses of brown mud that also caked buildings and buried streets.
Families around the world hear the news of missing loved ones

Rajan Tamang, a restaurant owner in New York City, said he learned from family in Kathmandu that his mother and sister were among those who died, while many other relatives and friends remained missing.

“My family was just waking up, and they didn’t even get any information, and suddenly this flood came. Some of them are missing, some of them lost their life and only a few is alive,” he told The Associated Press after a vigil in New York.
U.S. President Donald Trump said the flooding was terrible to see, describing how “strong, well-built buildings were wiped out like they were toothpicks.”
Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, Trump said the U.S. spoke with Nepalese leaders and offered to provide “anything they want.”

Scientists who've studied satellite images said bedrock underneath a glacier high in the Himalayan region had collapsed, taking part of the glacier with it. The rocks and melted water swelled the rivers in the valleys below, causing a torrent of water that swept buildings, bridges and earth downstream.

articles.title: Himalayan ‘tsunami’: Over 350 dead, 1,400 missing
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A Filipino was reported to be among the more than a thousand people missing in the flash floods and landslides that occurred on the Nepal-Tibet border, where the confirmed death…

blocks.caption: ENGULFED Surveillance video at a Nepal-China border crossing shows a massive wall of water, mud and debris crashing over a building several stories high on Wednesday morning, engulfing the structure and the entire complex as dozens of people run for their lives below. — CCTV SCREENSHOT VIA AFP

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A Filipino was reported to be among the more than a thousand people missing in the flash floods and landslides that occurred on the Nepal-Tibet border, where the confirmed death toll had reached at least 359 people as of Thursday.
The lone Filipino was on the initial record cited by the Nepal Tourism Board, though it was yet to be confirmed by the Philippine government at press time.
The tsunami-like rumble of water and mud struck villages and towns on the path of two rivers—Bhote Koshi and Trishuli—on Wednesday night.

A terrifying clip of surveillance video from the Chinese side of the frontier shows a massive wall of mud and debris crashing over a building several stories high on Wednesday morning, engulfing it as dozens of people ran for their lives below.
The surge swept away buses and cars like they were toys.
The US Geological Survey believes the disaster was caused by a glacial collapse that sent a flow of debris engulfing homes along the way.

blocks.caption: SWAMPED Local residents watch as a helicopter flies above houses lying deluged in sludge after flash floods at Devighat, Bidur municipality in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on Aug. 27 —AFP PHOTOS

blocks.text: According to the Nepal Tourism Board, its preliminary record as of 2:45 p.m. on Thursday (Philippine time) showed 644 travelers reported missing in the affected areas, including one Filipino.
The agency gave no further details about the missing Filipino, saying the information was still being verified and crosschecked with travel agencies and other local authorities.

In Manila, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) and the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (Owwa) have started coordinating with officials in Nepal, as well as with the Filipino community, to determine the extent of the disaster’s impact on Filipinos, Palace press officer Claire Castro said.
Based on information from the DFA and Owwa, there are 128 Filipinos in Nepal, mostly women married to Nepalis. Among them are 18 overseas workers.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Thursday expressed his condolences to the victims of the disaster.
“The Philippines extends its deepest condolences to our friends in Nepal and to all those affected by the deadly flash flood yesterday,” Mr. Marcos said in a social media post.
“Our deepest sympathies go out to those who lost family, loved ones, and friends. Please accept our most heartfelt prayers for strength in this difficult time,” he added.
Wall of mud, debris

blocks.caption: Aerial views show houses inundated by mud and water in Nuwakot district—AFP PHOTOS

blocks.text: The Nepali police on Thursday said they had recovered 162 bodies, as rescue teams rushed to find more than 1,400 people still missing.
Another 823 people, including 579 Nepali and foreign tourists, remained out of contact in Nepal, according to the country’s disaster agency.
Across the border, Chinese state media said the “mudslide disaster” at the Gyirong Port in Tibet claimed three lives while 558 people, including 260 foreigners, were still missing.
Raju Bhadel, 56, a businessman in Nepal’s Nuwakot district, recounted receiving a call from his brother-in-law in distress.
“They were crying and said their entire house had been swept away. Three family members were rescued, but his brother is still missing,” he said.
Also at Nuwakot, teacher Manok Mishra witnessed “nine trucks being swept away by the floods, including people.”

blocks.caption: Aerial views show houses inundated by mud and water in Nuwakot district—AFP PHOTOS

blocks.text: ‘Inland tsunami’
Rescuers waded through mud and sludge to look for survivors after floodwaters buried the lower floors of multistory buildings.
The foreigners out of contact included Indians, and others from Australia, Britain, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Portugal, South Africa, South Korea, and the United States, Nepal’s tourism board said.
Hiking company Himalayan Glacier told Agence France-Presse (AFP) 47 people from a group including two children were missing in Nepal.

The sudden rush of mud and debris was “like an inland tsunami, traveling nearly 170 kilometers down the Bhote Koshi valley into Central Nepal,” said environmental historian Ruth Gamble of La Trobe University in Australia.
“It is a popular route for international tourists traveling from Kathmandu to Lhasa,” she added.

blocks.caption: GRIEF A girl cries as she waits for news of relatives missing after flash floods in Bidur, Nepal, on Aug. 27. —AP

blocks.text: Rasuwa, in the north of Nepal, was the first district to be affected. But deaths have been reported from seven Nepali districts in total as the floodwaters raged through to Chitwan in the south, on the border with India.
The Nepali Army was carrying out flights and had rescued scores of people, while others living near the river in danger zones had been told to relocate.
Tibet government officials mobilized nearly 800 emergency workers and 150 vehicles as well as sniffer dogs and speed boats to help the rescue efforts, China’s state-run news agency Xinhua said.
The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said it was dispatching emergency supplies including blankets, first aid kits, stretchers, and body bags.
Seismic event

blocks.caption: Himalayan ‘tsunami’: Over 350 dead, 1.4K missing

blocks.text: The cause of the disaster was not immediately clear in the hours after it occurred early Wednesday, but the US Geological Survey said it was a glacial collapse that caused seismic activity and the “catastrophic” downstream impacts in Nepal and Tibet.
“This event was initially reported as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake,” it said.

“Additional analysis of nearby seismic stations, long period seismic waves, and satellite imagery led to the determination that the seismic event was instead a glacial collapse and debris flow, and that no earthquake had occurred.”
Climate change is causing glaciers to melt worldwide, increasing the risks of glacial lake floods and glacial collapses.
Qianggong Zhang, head of climate and environmental risks at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development, warned of the potential for a second flood.
