articles.title: PRU POP Run brings running to the next level
articles.summary: Thirty years calls for 30 kilometers. Pru Life UK is marking three decades in the Philippines with PRU POP (Promise of Protection) Run, highlighted by a special 30K race that challenges runners to go…

blocks.text: Thirty years calls for 30 kilometers. Pru Life UK is marking three decades in the Philippines with PRU POP (Promise of Protection) Run, highlighted by a special 30K race that challenges runners to go beyond the usual fun-run distances.

Set Sunday, Aug. 30, at Ayala Triangle Gardens in Makati, the event will feature five race categories – 3K, 5K, 10K, 21K and the centerpiece 30K. The lineup is designed to accommodate a wide range of participants, from beginners taking their first steps into running to seasoned athletes looking for a demanding new milestone.

The 30K is particularly significant because distances of this length are relatively uncommon in local running events. Rather than simply adding another category, Pru Life UK created the race as a physical representation of its 30-year journey in the country – 30 kilometers for 30 years of serving Filipino policyholders and communities.
But the company sees the run as more than an anniversary gimmick. It celebrates its long-standing commitment to helping Filipinos build healthier and more secure futures.

Pru Life UK Vice President and Head of Brand and Integrated Marketing Communications Kathryn Cajucom said the event reflects the idea that preparing for a stronger future involves more than financial security – it also requires healthier habits, discipline and the willingness to make responsible choices every day.

That message gives the 30K a deeper meaning: endurance is not only measured by how far a runner can go, but by the habits built along the way. Through PRU POP Run, Pru Life UK hopes to turn its 30th anniversary into a reminder that securing one's future is itself a long-distance journey – one that requires preparation, resilience and consistency.

Each race category caters to different fitness levels. Beginners can kick-start their running journey through the 3K and 5K distances, while more experienced runners can challenge themselves in the 10K and 21K events. Those seeking their next big milestone can take on the exclusive 30K race, a distance rarely featured in local running events.
Registration is still open at www.prupoprun.com.

As it marks three decades of serving Filipinos, Pru Life UK continues its commitment to being the most trusted partner of every life and protector of every future. Through PRU POP Run, the company reinforces its mission of helping Filipinos build healthy habits, stronger financial futures and lasting well-being – one step at a time.

The race categories are structured to welcome every fitness level. Beginners can ease into the lifestyle with the 3K or 5K distance, while seasoned weekend runners can test their stamina in the 10K category. Regular runners and marathon trainees can take on the 21K route or the highly anticipated 30K challenge, a special distance in local running events.

Beyond the physical challenge, PRU POP Run serves as a timely call for a more active living. In a digital age, it invites young Filipinos and families to step away from screens, step onto the pavement, and experience the real-world joy of movement, community, and personal achievement.

articles.title: Iloilo officials thank Marcos administration for distribution of various aid programs
articles.summary: ILOILO CITY—Local officials expressed appreciation to the Marcos administration after Executive Secretary Ralph Recto led distribution of various aid programs earlier this week. “Nagpapasalamat kami…

blocks.text: ILOILO CITY—Local officials expressed appreciation to the Marcos administration after Executive Secretary Ralph Recto led distribution of various aid programs earlier this week.

“Nagpapasalamat kami sa Pangulo sa mga tulong na ibinigay niya rito sa Iloilo. I’ve been telling our people in the province that we are truly being prioritized,” said Iloilo Governor Arthur “Toto” Defensor Jr.
During the August 25 distribution program, Recto assured the people of Iloilo they are part of the social aid programs under the administration of President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr.
Recto distributed the P200,000 aid for each of the 1,721 barangays in the 42 towns and component city of Passi.

As part of the Bawat Bayan Makikinabang for Iloilo, Recto reiterated that it is the first time that each barangay in the country has been given aid directly by Malacañang under the Socio-Civic Projects Fund (SCPF).
“We extend our sincere gratitude to the Office of the President and Executive Secretary Ralph Recto for his presence and support,” said Barangay Provincial Federation President Amalia Debuque.
Of the P200,000 allocated for each barangay, half of it will be for Presidential Scholars of five graduating college students.
In Iloilo province alone, there are more than 8,000 graduating students who are going to be beneficiaries of the P20,000 each aid per barangay.

In the town of Pavia, Recto also distributed 10 kilos of rice each to an initial 1,500 family beneficiaries. As part of the Bagong Pilipinas Rice Distribution Program, it will benefit a total of 8,000 families in Pavia with P5 million from the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF).

Also present during the ceremonial distribution were 1st District Rep. Janette Loreto-Garin, League of the Municipalities of the Philippines (LMP) Iloilo President Mayor Suzette Mamon, municipal mayors, and barangay officials.

articles.title: UN body calls for release of Cumpio, activists from arbitrary detention
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Human rights group Karapatan on Wednesday welcomed the findings of the United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention (UN WGAD), which declared as arbitrary the detention…

blocks.caption: JAIL VISIT Frenchie Mae Cumpio (right) is visited at Tacloban City Jail by UN Special Rapporteur Irene Khan, who was in the Philippines in January on an official trip. — PHOTO FROM IRENE KHAN’S OFFICIAL X ACCOUNT

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Human rights group Karapatan on Wednesday welcomed the findings of the United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention (UN WGAD), which declared as arbitrary the detention of Tacloban community journalist Frenchie Mae Cumpio, humanitarian worker Marielle Domequil and human rights worker Alexander Abinguña.
The UN WGAD stated its findings in its opinion report, which was released only recently and first adopted during its 105th session held from March 23 to April 1.

“The UN WGAD opinions reaffirm our position that the charges against Cumpio, Domequil and Abinguña are baseless and trumped-up, that their rights under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights were violated, and that their release from prison is long overdue,” Karapatan secretary general Cristina Palabay said in a statement.
The rights groups called for the release of the three, noting that they have been detained for more than six years following their arrest on Feb. 7, 2020.
Terrorism financing

Cumpio and Domequil were convicted in January by the Tacloban City Regional Trial Court for “terrorism financing” and sentenced to 12 to 18 years in prison. From the Tacloban City Jail, they were transferred in April to the Correctional Institute for Women in Mandaluyong City where they remain detained after their petition for bail was denied by the court. They have appealed their conviction before the Court of Appeals.

“The inordinate delay of the court proceedings that has prolonged their detention is an additional layer of injustice against the three. Their release should immediately be given due course,” Palabay said.
The UN WGAD found a lack of factual and legal basis for the criminal charges against the three, concluding that their deprivation of liberty was arbitrary.
It also determined that their detention stemmed from the exercise of their rights to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and association.
Based on the UN body’s report, the three have been targets of Red-tagging and accused of associating with the Communist Party of the Philippines and its armed wing, the New People’s Army.
It said the appropriate remedy would be the immediate release of Cumpio, Domequil and Abinguña, along with an enforceable right to compensation and other forms of reparation under international law.
Probe pushed

The UN WGAD also called for a full and independent investigation into the circumstances surrounding their arbitrary detention as it urged authorities to hold accountable those responsible for violating their rights.

articles.title: DILG backs proposed internet restrictions for children 14 and below
articles.summary: The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) on Friday expressed support for a proposal to restrict internet use among children aged 14 and below.

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 1:26pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.
The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) on Friday expressed support for a proposal to restrict internet use among children aged 14 and below.
At a press conference, DILG Secretary Jonvic Remulla said the proposal has already been taken up in Congress and received support during a recent budget hearing.
“We gave our opinion. Dapat 14 years and below ay restricted na ang use of the internet,” Remulla said.

“But it is not our call. Congress na lang ‘yan.So it was taken up yesterday during the budget hearing and they were in support of it. But we will see how the legal process goes, how the process of the lawmakers does that will result in this,” he added.
Other Stories
The proposal comes amid growing concerns over the exposure of minors to harmful content and individuals who allegedly seek to manipulate or recruit children online.
These concerns were also linked to the fatal shootings in Ateneo de Zamboanga University in Zamboanga City on August 18 and San Jose National High School in Tacloban City on June 22.

Pasig Representative Roman Romulo, House Committee on Basic Education and Culture chair, earlier said the lower chamber is drafting a measure that would impose a total social media and online gaming platform ban on children aged 13 and below, while regulating social media use among those 14 to 17 years old.
Meanwhile, Senator Robin Padilla also sponsored a bill seeking to set 16 as the minimum age for creating and maintaining a social media account. —VAL, GMA News

blocks.text: A data learning center for humanoid robots run by a consortium, including Tsumura & Co., in Narashino, Chiba Prefecture, east of Tokyo, photographed on Wednesday

Narashino, Chiba Pref., Aug. 27 -- A consortium of Japanese companies has launched a data center to train physical artificial intelligence on human tasks for deploying humanoid robots in factories and logistics operations.

The facility in Narashino, Chiba Prefecture, east of Tokyo, is operated by J-HRTI, a consortium of five companies, including Tsumura & Co., a maker of Chinese herbal medicine, and Yamazen Corp., a machinery trading company.
The partners will pool resources to collect vast amounts of work data and train AI, an undertaking difficult for a single company, to put humanoid robots to practical use in industrial settings.

The data center can accommodate up to 40 Chinese-made humanoid robots, with operators stationed there. Wearing virtual reality headsets, the operators control the robots and collect data. The facility also includes areas that replicate actual work environments to test potential applications.
J-HRTI aims to deploy the robots for simple tasks such as material transport within fiscal 2026, which ends next March.

Shoichi Kumagai, an executive officer at Tsumura, said on Wednesday, "Automation and unmanned operations will be necessary to maintain stable supplies (of products) as falling population makes it increasingly difficult to secure workers."

articles.title: Janus Del Prado weighs in on Bea Alonzo-Shirley Kuan issue, suggests NDA for actors and managers
articles.summary: Actor Janus Del Prado has weighed in on the controversy involving Bea Alonzo and her former manager Shirley Kuan, saying the public should hear the actress’s side before making conclusions about…

blocks.text: Actor Janus Del Prado (IMDB)

Actor Janus Del Prado has weighed in on the controversy involving Bea Alonzo and her former manager Shirley Kuan, saying the public should hear the actress’s side before making conclusions about their falling-out.

Janus shared his thoughts on Facebook as the issue continued to generate discussion following Shirley’s public revelation about the alleged reasons behind her decision to end her professional relationship with Bea.
“Before you judge Bea, let’s wait to hear her side of the story first. I’m not dismissing what her former manager claimed just yet, but that’s only one side of the story,” Janus wrote.
The actor also raised a bigger issue about the relationship between celebrities and their talent managers, suggesting that both sides should consider signing a non-disclosure agreement, or NDA.
For Janus, such an agreement could help protect sensitive information shared during a professional relationship—and provide legal protection if that relationship eventually falls apart.

“Actors should really consider having an NDA with their managers, and vice versa, to legally protect both parties’ confidential information and reputations. Para when the sh** hits the fan, everyone involved is legally protected,” he said.
Janus’ comments come after Shirley’s revelations about her split from Bea became a talking point online.
Shirley has also denied allegations that she interfered in Bea’s relationship with her husband, Vincent Co.

articles.title: Iran, Qatar hold Hormuz talks as US blockade chokes Iran’s oil imports
articles.summary: TEHRAN, Iran — Iran’s top diplomat met his Qatari counterpart on Thursday in Tehran for talks on the strategic Strait of Hormuz, as a US naval blockade squeezes oil supplies to Iran amid a…

blocks.caption: Before the Iran war, the Strait of Hormuz carried around 20% of global crude exports from the Persian Gulf. Image: REUTERS

blocks.text: TEHRAN, Iran — Iran’s top diplomat met his Qatari counterpart on Thursday in Tehran for talks on the strategic Strait of Hormuz, as a US naval blockade squeezes oil supplies to Iran amid a domestic shortfall.

The visit by Qatar’s Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani follows a week of intense diplomacy in Iran involving separate meetings with Oman’s top diplomat and senior Pakistani officials seeking ways to end the Middle East war and reopen Hormuz.

It also comes as Washington threatens wider secondary sanctions against countries, banks and companies that continue doing business with Iran, part of a broader campaign it has called “economic asphyxiation.”
Iranian state television said Al Thani, who is also Qatar’s prime minister, had met with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, without providing details.
In a statement after the talks, Al Thani said they focused on efforts to de-escalate tensions and boost security in the region.
“Qatar believes that dialogue and diplomacy remain the best way to overcome crises,” he wrote on X.
Qatar’s foreign ministry said they discussed the proposed framework for Hormuz between Iran and Oman.
“Talks stressed the importance of respecting freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz in accordance with international law,” Al Thani added.
Alongside mediator Pakistan, Qatar had played a key role in securing an April ceasefire and June deal between Iran and the United States, but those deals have since collapsed.
Fuel shortage

Since war with the United States broke out on February 28, Iran has maintained tight control over Hormuz, a vital global energy conduit, with Washington imposing a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports.
On Wednesday, Iran’s Vice President Mohammad Jafar Ghaempanah said the blockade had prevented his country from importing enough gasoline to cover a shortfall in domestic production.
“Gasoline production is insufficient, and because of the US naval blockade, we cannot import it,” he was quoted by the official IRNA news agency as saying.
In recent days, many Iranians have been seen queuing outside gas stations. Presidential chief of staff Mohsen Haji-Mirzaei said gasoline quotas would be reviewed, without elaborating.
Iran, a major oil producer with some of the world’s cheapest fuel, has for years heavily subsidized gasoline, making changes to pricing politically sensitive.
As the US seeks to strangle Iran’s economy, Iranian officials have dismissed the measures as “failed policies” that will not force Tehran to change course.
“The country is in an all-out economic war,” said Iran’s top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf in a statement carried by local media.
“We will see that the government … will defeat the enemy on this ground as well,” he added.
Even before the war, Iran’s economy was battered by decades of international sanctions and has long suffered from chronic inflation and a weakening currency.
Talks on Hormuz

Iran has for weeks been in talks with Oman, which also overlooks the Strait of Hormuz, over a framework agreement that would establish a “temporary corridor” for shipping and provide for clearing mines Tehran says were laid during the war.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards on Wednesday said the two countries had agreed on each country’s share of the waters and any revenues collected from managing the waterway.

Tehran has nonetheless insisted that the strait will not be reopened unless Washington meets its demands, including lifting its naval blockade, unfreezing Iranian assets abroad and removing oil sanctions.
Since the war broke out, Iranian forces have required vessels to obtain permission to transit the waterway and struck ships that failed to comply.
Tehran has also sought to impose service fees on ships using the strait — a move strongly opposed by Washington and regional countries.

articles.title: Meta vows to share user data in case Philippine authorities see ‘imminent threat’—Hontiveros
articles.summary: Tech giant Meta has agreed to share user data with Philippine law enforcement authorities, especially when there is an imminent threat of violence, Senator Risa Hontiveros said on Friday, August 28.…

blocks.text: Tech giant Meta has agreed to share user data with Philippine law enforcement authorities, especially when there is an imminent threat of violence, Senator Risa Hontiveros said on Friday, August 28.

This comes after Meta’s top Asia-Pacific region policy officers held a roundtable meeting at its headquarters in Singapore to discuss the responsibilities of it platforms—particularly Facebook—on the spread of nihilistic violent extremism (NVE).
Hontiveros said she sent representatives to join the Philippine delegation of key government officials to Meta’s meeting.

As their meeting was drawing to a close without agreement among the parties, Hontiveros’ camp pushed Meta to commit to sharing subscriber information and traffic data to Philippine authorities when there are indications of imminent attacks, to which the social media giant agreed to.
“Now that high-ranking Meta officials themselves have pledged to be more proactive regarding potential threats of violence, action against such threats must be swifter,” Hontiveros said.

“This is crucial, especially as we are currently pushing for the Child Online Safety and Protection Act, a priority measure of the government. Meta appears ready to tighten its safeguards, as we have already informed them that the bill is nearing passage,” the senator said.

Hontiveros is optimistic the agreement will come to play once Congress pass the Child Online Safety and Protection Act, which builds on the safeguards under Republic Act No. 11930 or the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse and Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act authored by Hontiveros.
“I gave strict instructions to the staff who met with Meta: It must be made clear to them that they cannot profit from Filipinos on Facebook without taking responsibility for the content,” she said.
“We will hold them to their word," Hontiveros vowed.

articles.title: Seven films, seven worlds: A visual feast of what’s coming to CinePanalo 2026
articles.summary: A farmer and his carabao on an unlikely journey to Manila. A romance that reaches into the netherworld. A young boy trying to make sense of growing up. An elderly widower, a kodokushi cleaner and a…

blocks.text: A farmer and his carabao on an unlikely journey to Manila. A romance that reaches into the netherworld. A young boy trying to make sense of growing up. An elderly widower, a kodokushi cleaner and a promise about grief.
These are just some of the stories waiting for moviegoers at this year’s CinePanalo, and the newly released posters offer the first visual taste of what’s to come.
The posters for the festival’s seven full-length films introduce not only their titles but the different moods and worlds that audiences can expect when the films screen in September.

There is magic and adventure in Lawrence Fajardo’s “Beast,” which follows an old farmer and his loyal carabao as they travel to Manila. The poster, designed by writer Jim Flores, hints at the film’s unusual journey and emotional core.

Then there’s Carl Joseph E. Papa’s “Patay Gutom,” starring Ian Pangilinan, which takes romance and family drama into supernatural territory. Filipino illustrator and film poster artist Denver Balbaboco gives the film a colorful, playful look that seems appropriate for a story involving the netherworld.
Balbaboco recently created the new cover art for The Criterion Collection’s release of Guillermo del Toro’s “Frankenstein.”
Mikko Baldoza’s “Stuck On You” goes in another direction, mixing romance, danger and comedy. Its poster, designed by Liam Casimiro, reflects that collision with a bold and energetic visual treatment.
Thop Nazareno’s “Apol of My Ai” brings things down to a more intimate, coming-of-age story about a young boy dealing with the complications of growing up.

The poster by Jermaine Tulbo brings together the people, relationships and music that shape Apol’s world. Tulbo previously designed the poster for “Olsen’s Day,” one of the entries in the 2025 CinePanalo lineup.

In “Wantawsan,” Joseph Abello turns an ordinary errand into what appears to be anything but an ordinary day. Abello also designed the poster, giving the film an offbeat visual personality that matches its comic adventure.
The more contemplative side of the lineup comes through in BC Amparado’s “Mono No Aware.”

The film follows a Filipino kodokushi cleaner and an elderly widower whose promise to one another leads to a story about grief, family and the fleeting nature of life. Davao-based graphic designer and filmmaker Wowa Medroso created its restrained, evocative poster.
Medroso’s debut feature, “Kantil,” premiered at Cinemalaya.
Then there’s “Multwoh (Patay na Patay Sa’yo),” written and directed by Rodina Singh, which promises a romance with a rather unusual complication: one of the lovers is dead.

Multidisciplinary visual creative EA Rosana designed the poster, blending the haunting, funny and tender elements of the story. Rosana previously worked with Singh on the poster for “Dreamboi” and has also worked on projects involving girl group BINI.
Taken together, the seven posters make for quite a visual feast and a useful primer for the films themselves.

There’s the strange and surreal, the funny and romantic, the supernatural and the deeply human. If the posters are any indication, this year’s CinePanalo lineup isn’t interested in looking like seven versions of the same movie.
The seven filmmakers each received a ₱5 million production grant for their respective films.
CinePanalo 2026 runs from Sept. 23 to Oct. 4 at Gateway Cineplex 18, Trinoma, Fairview Terraces, Ayala Malls Feliz, Ayala Malls Circuit, Ayala Malls Manila Bay and Market! Market!

The STAR / Miguel de Guzman

MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang announced the suspension of government work and classes at all levels in public and private schools in Metro Manila and 16 provinces starting 1 p.m. Friday, Aug. 28, as heavy rains from the southwest monsoon persist.

In a news release, the Presidential Communications Office said Executive Secretary Ralph Recto issued Memorandum Circular No. 132 upon the recommendation of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council.
The suspension covers:

The suspension was ordered due to the expected further enhancement of the southwest monsoon, or habagat, by a low pressure area that has entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility, Malacañang said.
Government agencies providing basic and health services, disaster preparedness and response, and other vital services will continue to operate, it added.
It also directs local chief executives to suspend classes or government work in their respective areas depending on local conditions.
For the private sector, the suspension of work or adoption of alternative work arrangements will be left to management.
Heavy rains over Luzon. The suspension comes as the southwest monsoon, or habagat, continues to bring heavy rain over large parts of Luzon.
PAGASA earlier said Metro Manila, the Ilocos Region, parts of Central Luzon, Calabarzon and Occidental Mindoro may experience heavy rain Friday.
La Union, Benguet, Bataan, Zambales and Occidental Mindoro may receive 100 to 200 millimeters of rain, while Metro Manila and several other provinces could receive 50 to 100 mm.
PAGASA warned that rainfall could be heavier in mountainous and elevated areas, while flooding and landslide risks may be worsened in places already saturated by previous rains.

articles.title: Turning 'flood control' to 'flood management'
articles.summary: The UP Resilience Institute-NOAH Center believe that it is important to predict floods. You may ask, why make such predictions when most Filipinos already know where it floods? Why not just focus on…

blocks.text: The UP Resilience Institute-NOAH Center believe that it is important to predict floods. You may ask, why make such predictions when most Filipinos already know where it floods? Why not just focus on making solutions? According to the institute, prediction is understanding the problem. If solutions are applied without fully understanding the problem, it is possible the said problems will be underestimated, and the solutions produced are not suited in handling the problem.

With the P1 billion allocation, the UP Resilience Institute-NOAH Center will strengthen the country’s capacity to generate, manage, communicate, and apply scientific information for disaster risk reduction, flood management, environmental protection, and climate resilience.

The allocation builds on existing accomplishments in hazard mapping, flood intelligence, resilience education, technical assistance, government partnerships, and open access to disaster-risk data and information.

Rather than a stand-alone project fund, the budget will expand systems that translate research into practical information for better public investment decisions. This approach recognizes that resilience requires the integration of natural systems, scientific data, and evidence-based governance.

blocks.caption: Alfredo Mahar Lagmay, executive director, University of the Philippines Resilience Institute (UPRI), Diliman

blocks.text: Alfredo Mahar Lagmay, executive director, University of the Philippines Resilience Institute (UPRI), Diliman

The appropriation is consistent with Republic Act No. 9500, or the UP Charter of 2008, which mandates the University to provide scholarly and technical assistance to government, the private sector, and civil society. The funding therefore rests on UP’s legal mandate to advance research, public service, and national development.
Areas for Budget Utilization

High-resolution mapping of major river basins. UPRI-NOAH will update major river-basin maps using advanced geospatial technologies, producing hazard maps with up to one-by-one-meter pixel resolution. Detailed information on waterways, floodplains, land use, watersheds, infrastructure, and exposed communities will support hazard assessments, land-use planning, and preparedness.

blocks.caption: Atty. Angelo Jimenez, president of the University of the Philippines

blocks.text: Atty. Angelo Jimenez, president of the University of the Philippines

Support for Oplan Kontra Baha. In cooperation with the Department of Public Works and Highways, the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority, local governments, and the private sector, UPRI-NOAH will integrate watershed science, flood modeling, terrain, infrastructure, and local knowledge to identify appropriate structural and non-structural solutions.

Simulation of major detention basins. Simulations will integrate surface and subsurface flow of water to assess storage capacity of detention basins, drainage connectivity, downstream effects, and performance under extreme rainfall and future climate conditions, guiding flood-control planning, operations, maintenance, and investment.

LiDAR drone surveys with state colleges and universities. Knowledge co-creation with state colleges and universities will include topographic surveys using LiDAR-equipped drones. There will be capacity building programs to train faculty, researchers, and students, while strengthening regional geospatial and resilience-planning capabilities.

Native-tree mapping and tree inventory. Mapping and inventories will document native trees and their environmental value, supporting carbon-credit development, carbon accounting, biodiversity conservation, watershed protection, ecological restoration, urban greening, and flood management.

Sediment erosion and delivery assessment. Watershed assessments will estimate soil loss, sediment delivery, and sediment yield using rainfall, soil, topography, land cover, and conservation factors. Results will identify rehabilitation priorities and potential impacts on waterways, detention basins, drainage, and flood-management infrastructure.

Mapping hidden waterways and undocumented drainage paths. Identifying buried, altered, diverted, or undocumented waterways will improve flood modeling and guide urban planning, drainage improvement, infrastructure design, restoration, and emergency response.

Nature-based solutions. Watershed rehabilitation, wetland and floodplain restoration, urban green spaces, permeable surfaces, and tree planting will complement necessary structural measures while supporting biodiversity, carbon sequestration, water quality, erosion control, and stormwater retention.

Artificial Intelligence for Disaster Management. The Institute will harness artificial intelligence and advanced analytics to develop decision-support tools that generate actionable information for land-use and infrastructure planning, environmental management, and risk analysis. These will be integrated and analyzed alongside historical disaster data to identify patterns useful for the assessment of risk.

These systems may support identification of vulnerable communities, forecasting, early warning, exposure assessment, and prioritization of interventions. AI-assisted benefit-cost assessment will help decision-makers compare projects and identify interventions that are effective, sustainable, financially justified, and capable of protecting the greatest number of people.
Transparency and Accountability

Every major expenditure will be connected to a defined program, public purpose, implementation plan, technical outputs, measurable indicators, and monitoring and evaluation. Budget implementation will follow applicable procurement and auditing requirements. The UP System will document and monitor fund disbursements.
Building on UPRI-NOAH Accomplishments

UPRI-NOAH provides nationwide hazard information covering floods, landslides, storm surges, tsunamis, and coastal hazards. A United Nations Development Programme study found that approximately 59.7 percent of local government units utilize NOAH datasets and analytical tools. The NOAH platform has served more than 3.2 million users, recorded approximately 12.9 million location searches in 2025, and reached as many as 2.3 million engagements in a single day.

With the UP Open University, the Institute developed free Basics of Resilience online courses, reaching approximately 117,000 enrollees since program inception and 45,000 finishers over the span of two years. Microcredentials, advanced courses, professional training, master’s programs, and partnerships with state colleges and universities strengthen resilience education and regional technical capacity.

Partnerships with government agencies, local governments, universities, and communities support forecasting, risk assessment, drainage and flood studies, and operational flood intelligence. Multidisciplinary Quick Response Teams conduct field investigations, drone mapping, geospatial analysis, and engineering assessments to support disaster response, recovery, and rehabilitation.
Looking Ahead

UPRI-NOAH will expand the coverage, resolution, accuracy, and usefulness of its services; strengthen public education and graduate programs; develop innovative technologies; and connect research more closely with government planning and investment decisions. Long-term collaboration among universities, government, civil society, industry, international organizations, and communities will combine scientific expertise, local knowledge, sound governance, and public participation.

The ₱1 billion allocation will be measured by better information, transparency, evidence-based decisions, effective flood management, and reduced disaster risks and losses. Through innovation, education, partnerships, and public service, UPRI-NOAH will continue to transform scientific knowledge into practical action that protects lives and helps build safer, more resilient, and sustainable communities.

articles.title: Nepal flash flood 'unlikely' in PH --weather specialist
articles.summary: A weather specialist of weather bureau PAGASA on Friday said he believed that the landslide and flash flood that occurred along the Nepal-Tibet border is unlikely to occur in the Philippines.

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 1:00pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.
A weather specialist from PAGASA believes that the flash flood that occurred along the Nepal-Tibet border is unlikely to occur in the Philippines.

“Based on ‘yung ating construction ng mga kailugan po sa ngayon is somehow hindi naman ganoon ka-drastic talaga, hindi comparable doon sa nangyari sa may area ng Himalayas kasi sobrang lawak naman po atsaka ang tataas talaga ng mga bundok nila doon,” PAGASA weather specialist Benison Estareja said in an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Friday.

(Based on the current construction of our rivers, it is somehow not that drastic and is not comparable to what happened in the Himalayan region, which is much more extensive and has much higher mountains.)

“‘Yung potential energy coming from ‘yung pinakamataas papunta sa ibaba, talagang sobra ‘yung impact. Unlike dito na, yes may tendency na talagang dumami ‘yung tubig, pero ‘yung ragasa po hindi naman siya nakikita halos maladelubyo,” he added.
Other Stories

(The potential energy from the highest point moving down to the lower areas has a tremendous impact. Unlike here, where there is a tendency for the volume of water to increase, but we are not really seeing a massive surge that would cause a catastrophe.)
The flash floods and landslides killed at least 165 people and swept away entire villages.
Rivers, dams
When asked about possible landslides from mountains falling into dams, Estareja said that the country has no glaciers.
He also assured that the the government has a warning system in place.

“Kung magkaroon man ng ganoong instance na sobrang lakas ng ulan sa taas and then nagkaroon ng pagkasira ng gates and then nag burst open ‘yung ating mga rivers. At least po meron tayong mga warnings,” he said.

(If such an instance were to occur where there is extremely heavy rainfall in the upper areas, followed by damage to the gates and the rivers suddenly bursting open, at least we have warnings in place.)

According to Maki Pulido’s report on Saksi, though experts are still looking into the cause of the incident, University of the Philippines (UP) Resillience Institute Executive Director Mahar Lagmay said what occured may be a “debris flow.”
“Parang baha pero may laman na mga bato, graba, buhangin na pagka umagos ay parang wet concrete. Debris flow ang tawag diyan. Boulders na tangay-tangay nung baha na more than 50% ang bato,” he said.

(It is like a flood, but it carries rocks, gravel, and sand, and when it flows, it behaves like wet concrete. That is called a debris flow. Boulders are carried along by the flood, with more than 50% of the flow consisting of rocks.)
Lagmay said a debris flow occurred at Compostela Valley in 2012, where more than 500 people died, while several barangays in Oriental Mindoro were burried in 2015 by rocks from a debris flow.
“Marami tayong bundok. Kapag nagkaroon ng landslide because of a storm, thousands of landslides doon sa mountains, meron tayong source material,” he said.
(We have many mountains. When a storm causes landslides, potentially resulting in thousands of landslides in the mountains, we have a source of material.)
He said that the UP Resillience Institute has identified more than 1,000 places that has communities along the river. —Joahna Casilao/ VAL, GMA News

articles.byline: JON VIKTOR D. CABUENAS, GMA News

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 12:56pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.

More than 200 personnel of the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) are being investigated over an alleged “slot-for-sale” recruitment scheme, the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) said Friday.
At a press conference, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said the investigation covers personnel nationwide and is part of a broader effort to eliminate corruption within the BFP.
“Binabalaan ko na ang lahat ng opisyal ng BFP. Lumabas na kayo ngayon at umamin kayo o hahabulin namin kayo hanggang matapos ang career niyo,” Remulla said.
“Ang iniimbestigahan namin ngayon ay lumagpas ng 200 tao na tungkol sa slots for sale,” he added.
Other Stories

(We are warning all (involved) BFP officials. You better come out and admit your fault or we will go after you until your career ends. We are investigating over 200 people over the slots for sale [scheme].)
The investigation followed an entrapment operation conducted by the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) Region 3 in San Fernando City, Pampanga on August 24.
The operation resulted in the arrest of a 32-year-old BFP personnel who was caught accepting P300,000 from the complainant in exchange for securing a position in the bureau.
Other applicants allegedly paid between P100,000 and P800,000 for BFP slots under the illegal scheme.
“It's a P15 billion a year industry,” Remulla said.
A senior BFP officer in Calabarzon allegedly linked to the recruitment scheme was also relieved from their post and placed under restrictive duty pending investigation.
Remulla vowed to clean the BFP and resolve the matter within six months. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: PH batters bow to Venezuela, miss World Cup final berth
articles.summary: The Philippines missed a chance to qualify in the finals of next year’s Women’s Baseball World Cup after falling short against Venezuela, 0-10, in the final match of its group stage in Tainan, Taiwan…

blocks.text: At A Glance

items: A few hours after absorbing a painful 2-8 defeat at the hands of host Chinese Taipei, the Nationals continued their struggle against the more experienced Venezuelans to finish the group stage with a 2-3 win-loss record.

blocks.caption: (Photo from PABA)

blocks.text: (Photo from PABA)

The Philippines missed a chance to qualify in the finals of next year’s Women’s Baseball World Cup after falling short against Venezuela, 0-10, in the final match of its group stage in Tainan, Taiwan on Thursday, Aug. 29.

A few hours after absorbing a painful 2-8 defeat at the hands of host Chinese Taipei, the Nationals continued their struggle against the more experienced Venezuelans to finish the group stage with a 2-3 win-loss record.
They finished fourth behind unbeaten Japan (5-0), Venezuela (4-1) and Chinese Taipei (3-2), who claimed the top 3 slots allocated for next year’s finals in Rockford, Illinois.
The three qualified teams joined the United States, Australia and Canada, who clinched spots by finishing in the top 3 of their group stage held in Rockford last July.
Despite falling short of their goal, the Nationals still showed promise with victories over world No. 7 Cuba, 6-0, and Great Britain, 6-2, last Wednesday, Aug. 26.
They also lost to Japan, 0-3, and Cuba, 0-6.

items: The Trump administration issued a memo restricting internship work authorizations for international students, warning universities of potential loss of certification for non-compliance.
Some universities, including UCLA and UC Berkeley, have paused certain work authorization applications while reviewing the new federal guidance, which is seen as more restrictive.

The administration has also targeted universities over various issues, including diversity initiatives and protests, leading to allegations of bias in admissions practices and revocation of visas for student protesters.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

WASHINGTON, USA — President Donald Trump‘s administration has issued a memo for universities that seeks to restrict issuance of certain internship work authorizations for international students as the federal government warned that colleges not complying with the regulations may lose certification to enroll foreign students.

The federal memo dated August 24 said the Student and Exchange Visitor Program, which is part of the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency, has “observed a rise in Curricular Practical Training (CPT) authorizations that appear to violate regulatory requirements which permit CPT only where the training is an integral part of an established curriculum.”
“Failure to comply with SEVP regulations may result in an institution losing certification to enroll foreign students,” the memo said.

It resulted in some schools, including the University of California, Los Angeles and the University of California, Berkeley, pausing certain applications for work authorizations for international students.
“UCLA has paused certain Curricular Practical Training authorizations while it reviews recent federal guidance and determines next steps,” a UCLA spokesperson said.

UC Berkeley’s international office said the August 24 memo was “more narrow in focus, more direct, and includes content that is more restrictive in nature.” The federal government had also issued an earlier memo in mid-August.
UC Berkeley’s international office said it is unlikely that it will process certain work authorization applications “in the near future” and urged those international students to plan accordingly.

It said it will continue processing “degree-requirement” CPT as normal and would resume processing “Doctoral Dissertation and Master’s Thesis Research CPT.” The office said it would consult legal experts to develop new processes aligning with new federal requirements.

“Nothing about these regulations has changed,” the Department of Homeland Security, ICE’s parent, said in a statement. “However, schools and employers should consider themselves on notice: under President Trump, abuse of this generous system will no longer be tolerated.”

Trump has targeted universities with probes and funding threats over issues like pro-Palestinian protests against US ally Israel’s assault on Gaza, diversity initiatives, climate programs, and transgender policies. Rights advocates have raised free speech, academic freedom, and due process concerns.

Separately, the US Justice Department alleged on Thursday admissions practices at the George Washington University School of Medicine and Health Services favored Black and Hispanic applicants, citing findings of a probe as the Trump administration continued its diversity crackdown.
“We are disappointed by the DOJ’s conclusions, which we believe are incorrect,” the university said, saying the admissions policies were in compliance with law and not discriminatory.
The Justice Department has alleged similar bias at other schools, saying the department aims for settlement talks. If those efforts fail, the department will file suit, it said.
Trump’s administration has also revoked visas of student protesters over pro-Palestinian protests that it casts as antisemitic and sympathetic to extremists.

Protesters, including some Jewish groups, say opposition to Israel’s assault on Gaza and its occupation of Palestinian territories is not antisemitic and advocacy for Palestinian rights is not the same as supporting extremism. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Filipino at Tsino Magkaibigan Foundation donates 1,000 sacks of rice to Baguio, Benguet LGUs
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY – The Filipino at Tsino Magkaibigan Foundation distributed 1,000 sacks of 5 kilos of rice to three local government units for residents affected by the previous typhoon and the southwest…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY – The Filipino at Tsino Magkaibigan Foundation distributed 1,000 sacks of 5 kilos of rice to three local government units for residents affected by the previous typhoon and the southwest monsoon.

The donation, spearheaded by the Federation of Filipino Chinese Chambers of Commerce & Industry, Inc.-Baguio Chapter led by Peter Ng, together with its members, delivered 300 sacks of rice (5 kilos each) to the Benguet provincial government, on August 27, which were received by Governor Melchor Diclas.
Diclas expressed his deep gratitude to the Baguio Filipino-Chinese community for its continuing support, particularly during times of calamity.
In the capital town of La Trinidad, officials also received 200 sacks (5 kilos each) of rice provided by the group for the disaster victims.

Another 500 sacks of rice (5 kilos each) were personally delivered by Ng and his group to the Office of the City Social Welfare and Development Office in Baguio City, which were received by City Administrator Vittorio Jericho Cawis and OCWD Officer Liza Balungayan.

“On behalf of Mayor Benjamin Magalong, thank you very much for the tireless support to the city government of the Filipino-Chinese community, not only during the disaster, but also for their continued support for the city’s tourism development programs,” said Cawis.
He said that based on ODSWDO data, more than 1,000 families were severely affected by the southwest monsoon.
It can be recalled that last year, the foundation also donated 1,000 bags of five kilos of rice to these LGUs to be distributed to those affected by the typhoon.

“In our groups, and with the support of the foundation, this is our traditional work to deliver aid to disaster victims. On these occasions, we want to show that we are Filipinos who will continue to help the community,” said Ng.

articles.title: Muntinlupa’s Doctor of Medicine Program now CHED-certified
articles.summary: The Commission on Higher Education (CHED) has awarded a Certificate of Program Compliance (COPC) to the Doctor of Medicine program in Muntinlupa. The program is offered by the Pamantasan ng Lungsod…

blocks.text: The Commission on Higher Education (CHED) has awarded a Certificate of Program Compliance (COPC) to the Doctor of Medicine program in Muntinlupa.
The program is offered by the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Muntinlupa (PLMun)–Ospital ng Muntinlupa (OsMun) College of Medicine.
“We can now say that our very own PLMun–OsMun College of Medicine fully meets CHED’s official policies, standards, and guidelines,” said Muntinlupa Mayor Ruffy Biazon.

Under Joint CHED–Professional Regulation Commission Circular No. 1 issued in 2025, the PRC will not admit applicants for licensure exams from state and local universities and colleges without COPC or government recognition.
PLMun, funded by the city government, is the first local university in the country to offer a Doctor of Medicine program among 140 local colleges and universities.

With the granting of the COPC, the Muntinlupa City government said CHED has confirmed that the program meets standards, including qualified faculty, adequate resources, and suitable facilities for medical education.
“Isa ulit itong milestone (This is another milestone) towards our goal of producing more homegrown healthcare professionals,” the mayor added.
Last July, the first batch of PLMun–OsMun College of Medicine graduates completed their studies and are now undergoing internship at OsMun.
The graduates are Princess Garcia, Aileen Mae Arban, Maxine Barlaw, Tricia Guevarra, Sophia Laranan, Ana Marie Ramos, and Jaycee Mae Rufino.

articles.title: How policy choices left Philippines behind Taiwan in global chip race
articles.summary: Foreign factories aren't enough. What UP researchers say Pax Silica needs:

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines risks repeating the failures of the 1970s Bataan export zone if the vaunted Pax Silica site in New Clark City draws foreign investors without a government-led push into chip design and fabrication, a University of the Philippines study said.

Beyond the manufacturing side, the study points out how the government's historic "paltry" budget for science and technology, an unfocused education system, and decades of brain drain hollowed out the country’s pool of experts, while Taiwan heavily bankrolled its own research and development and aligned its schools with industrial goals.

The study, published last month as a discussion paper by the UP Center for Integrative and Development Studies, compares how Taiwan and the Philippines developed their semiconductor industries after both entered the business in the late 1960s as low-cost sites for the assembly, testing and packaging of chips made elsewhere.

Taiwan spent the three decades that followed building an industry that now spans design, fabrication and advanced packaging — investment that led it to become today's source of about 90% of the world's most advanced chips.
The Philippines, however, is still constrained to back-end assembly and testing, and has yet to build a single wafer fabrication plant, the paper said.

The paper's authors, Lianne Angelico Depante of the National Graduate Institute for Policy Studies in Japan and Kirsten Lianne Mae Dedase of the UP National College of Public Administration and Governance, argue that the vast difference between Taipei and Manila's chip industries was more a product of policy decisions between the 1970s and the 1990s than market forces.
The researchers examined the policies Taipei and Manila governments adopted between the 1970s and the 1990s, when the foundations of both chip industries were laid.

Without domestic fabrication, or the ability to manufacture microchips locally, the Philippines will continue to be "a processor of upstream foreign value rather than a producer of its own," the paper read.
Pax Silica

The research noted that the Philippines is now betting much of its chip industry outlook around the planned 1,619-hectare economic security zone in New Clark City, which President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. touted in his most recent State of the Nation Address.

The zone sits within the larger Luzon Economic Corridor, a logistics network linking Subic, Clark, Manila and Batangas that is being developed with United States backing under the Pax Silica initiative.
The paper argues that this has essentially been done before, the paper contends, with the creation of the Bataan Export Processing Zone (BEPZ) in 1972.

The study notes that the BEPZ was designed "primarily to attract foreign investment and generate employment" through "a combination of fiscal and non-fiscal incentives, including the provision of physical infrastructure and government-guaranteed financing and policies permitting full foreign ownership and duty-free production."
This drew large manufacturers, including Intel and Texas Instruments. Buoyed by this success, the government eventually pursued more economic zones in Baguio, Cavite, and Cebu.
However, the BEPZ itself did not lead to more advanced manufacturing and failed to bring about local technology transfer due to several factors.

Among others, the Bataan zone was far from major academic and commercial centers, as well as remote from Metro Manila. Because of its remote location, its potential to generate knowledge spillovers and facilitate technology transfer among firms was limited, the study read.

"Site selection was not solely determined by economic or logistical factors but also by political considerations, which influenced the placement of several zones and, in some cases, reinforced their spatial disconnect from key hubs of industry and knowledge," the paper read.
The government eventually decided, with the 1995 PEZA law, to largely turn ecozone development over to the private sector.

While the hands-off approach allowed more foreign investors in, the researchers say it turned the nation's industrial parks into isolated "enclaves with minimal integration into the domestic economy."

Unlike Taiwan, which tightly linked its tech zones to national innovation systems, Philippine zones suffer from a "paucity of deliberate policies" to build local supply chains or spur local technology transfer.

Taiwan's own cluster, the Hsinchu Science Park, opened in 1980 next to two engineering schools, National Tsing Hua University and National Chiao Tung University, and within reach of the state research institutes that would later spin off its largest chipmakers.

The study is careful not to present the planned economic zone in New Clark City as doomed. The project under Pax Silica could still anchor a genuine cluster of assembly firms, startups, universities, public research bodies and prospective fabrication and design companies, the study read, but only alongside industrial and fiscal policies that go beyond building roads and ports.
Those would include shared fabrication, design and testing facilities, research consortia for joint work and technology transfer, and dedicated funding for spinoffs and university research.

Without them, the paper warned, the site "risks repeating history and becoming yet another primarily logistics-oriented initiative, while exposing the country to geopolitical risks without commensurate gains in development."
Paltry budget for science and technology
The study also noted that while Taiwan aggressively funded its chip ambitions, the Philippines starved its primary science agency of funding.

Over the years, the Department of Science and Technology has received a "paltry budget" of less than 1% of total national spending. The researchers argued this limited support and funding, especially for research and development, kept back the country's industry from moving beyond low-value assembly lines.

In contrast, Taiwan used public capital to back risky, unproven technologies. The Taiwanese government directly funded up to 49% of the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company's initial capital — spinning the global chip giant off from its state research institute, ITRI — and empowered public labs to co-invest alongside private enterprise.
Tech-voc gap and brain drain

Among many differences in both economies' approach to education, the study noted that technical and vocational education and training (TVET) formed the backbone of Taiwan's strategy, while the Philippines left higher education largely to market forces.

Taiwan aligned its school system directly with its industrial goals. By 1980, TVET students in Taiwan "outnumbered their university counterparts by more than 50 percent," providing the necessary backbone of technicians and engineers for its "burgeoning electronics and semiconductor industry."

The Philippines meanwhile was largely hands off and left universities to offer programs based on what it argues was short-term market demand. As a result, students historically "gravitated toward law, business administration, education, and the humanities, leaving science and engineering underrepresented."
TVET in the Philippines is also mostly privately run and tailored toward the service sector rather than manufacturing, the study noted.
This is further compounded by "longstanding cultural norms" where technical and vocational fields were "commonly viewed as less prestigious" than white-collar professions.

The two economies also diverged sharply in how they supported their engineers and scientists. While Taiwan brought back overseas engineers and executives to build domestic tech giants, the Philippines to this day experiences a persistent "brain drain" where professionals would move overseas for better career opportunities.

Manila's efforts to bring its scientists back struggled to gain ground because the domestic economy lacked the commensurate high-tech jobs. The government's Balik (Return) Scientist Program — modeled directly after Taiwan's — has achieved limited success, the paper noted.

Of the 320 scientists who joined the program in the early 2010s, more than half eventually decided to again move overseas because talent retention was severely "constrained by the country's limited industrial base."
What the study recommends
The study lists seven recommendations for developing countries trying to build chip industries.

Among others, it said public research agencies should be given mandates that allow "calculated risk-taking," including the power to incubate spinoff firms and run applied research in design, advanced packaging and lab-scale wafer fabrication.
That "does not imply indiscriminate spending but a willingness to tolerate failure as an inherent part of learning," the paper said.
Governments must also fund capital-intensive segments that private firms avoid "in the absence of state commitment and risk-sharing mechanisms," it said.
For the Philippines, the study proposed a dedicated semiconductor development fund offering equity, matching grants, concessional financing or research subsidies to local firms and startups.
Support should be conditioned on "technology transfer, workforce upgrading, local supplier development, patent generation" and not on profit alone, it said.

articles.title: Japanese Ambassador Endo bids farewell, thanks Filipinos for support and friendship
articles.summary: Outgoing Japanese Ambassador to the Philippines Endo Kazuya bade farewell to Filipinos on Friday, Aug. 28, as he ended his two-and-a-half-year tour of duty, describing his time in the country as…

blocks.text: Outgoing Japanese Ambassador to the Philippines Endo Kazuya bade farewell to Filipinos on Friday, Aug. 28, as he ended his two-and-a-half-year tour of duty, describing his time in the country as "truly unforgettable."
In an X post, Endo thanked Filipinos for their "unwavering" support and friendship, saying he was deeply humbled to have served as ambassador "at the height of our two countries’ partnership."
"Taos-pusong pasasalamat, Pilipinas (My sincerest thanks, Philippines)!” he wrote.
“These two and a half years have been truly unforgettable, and I am deeply humbled to have served as Japanese Ambassador to the Philippines at the height of our two countries’ partnership," he added.
In a video accompanying the post, Endo also thanked Filipinos for their friendship and support.
"Maraming salamat sa walang humpay ninyong suporta at pagkakaibigan (Thank you very much for your unwavering support and friendship),” he said.
“Hanggang sa muli! Mata ne (Until we meet again. See you)!” he added.

Endo’s farewell message came a day after President Marcos honored him during a farewell call at Malacañang, where the President conferred on him the Order of Sikatuna, Grand Cross with Distinction, for his contributions to strengthening Philippine-Japan relations.

According to the Presidential Communications Office (PCO), Endo was recognized for promoting bilateral exchanges and deepening cooperation in defense, security, and development cooperation, as well as supporting Philippine priorities in infrastructure, education, transportation, maritime domain awareness, and human resource development.

The PCO also cited Endo's efforts to advance Japan's longstanding commitment to peace and development in Mindanao, including support for the peace process, grassroots development, and the transition of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.

The award likewise recognized his efforts to mobilize Japanese humanitarian and development assistance during natural disasters and recent regional crises, as well as initiatives that fostered friendship, mutual understanding, and goodwill between Filipinos and Japanese.
The Order of Sikatuna is conferred on individuals who have rendered exceptional and meritorious service to the Philippines or made outstanding contributions to Philippine-Japan relations.

The Philippines and Japan are marking 70 years of normalized relations this year, with 15 years of Strengthened Strategic Partnership since 2011, and bilateral ties having expanded across economic, development, security, and people-to-people cooperation.

articles.title: Danielle Smith takes questions at virtual town hall on data centres in Alberta, NDP calls for pause
articles.summary: Premier Danielle Smith and three of her ministers spent an hour Thursday fielding calls and online questions from Albertans who say they are concerned about artificial intelligence data centres being…

image.caption: Premier Danielle Smith said her government is considering feedback from Albertans who attended town halls to express concerns around data centres. Smith is seen in this photo speaking to media in Calgary on Feb. 1, 2024. (Emilio Avalos/Radio-Canada)

blocks.text: Premier Danielle Smith and three of her ministers spent an hour Thursday fielding calls and online questions from Albertans who say they are concerned about artificial intelligence data centres being built in the province.

The virtual town hall was tame compared to the two in-person events held earlier this month, where Technology Minister Nate Glubish was repeatedly hit with criticism, profanity and demands for additional safeguards.
For Thursday's call, Albertans could either submit questions online or, if they registered in advance, over the phone.
Moderator Justin Wright, the province's primary care minister, said over 12,500 people had tuned in.
Smith's government has been trying to position Alberta as an ideal destination for data centres, saying they could generate new jobs and billions in royalties and taxes for the province.
The premier has said the town halls are about finding "blind spots" in the government's regulatory framework.
Alberta Ministers face barrage of opposition to data centres

But, as with the previous events, nobody who spoke Thursday expressed any excitement about having the major computing complexes built in the province in the first place. One caller did say he was excited to be on the call with "the premier and her entourage," but he didn't ask a question or mention data centres.

The event started with Smith addressing many of the concerns the government has already heard, including about water use, location selection and setbacks, and potential electricity bill hikes — all issues that callers would bring up.

Water usage was a popular topic, with many callers questioning Smith and her ministers for saying that projects to date — namely the $13-billion campus north of Edmonton being proposed by tech giant Meta — will have limited water use.
The facility is to have a closed-loop cooling system, and both the company and the government have said its annual water use would be equivalent to a golf course.

One caller, identified as David from Calgary, asked why the province wasn't also accounting for the water that will be used by the adjacent $4.6-billion natural gas power plant, built solely to power Meta's facility.
"They'll be using loads of water. I mean, enormous amounts," he said.

items: Alberta minister faces more fury at second town hall on AI data centres

blocks.text: Smith said his point was well taken, but also said other heavy industries use massive amounts of water. She specifically mentioned a pulp mill in northern Alberta that she recently toured, saying it used seven billion litres of water per year.
"We don't say that you're not allowed to use water at all," she said.
Another caller, Peggy, asked why the government was willing to risk bringing in more heavy water users when parts of the province have seen water restrictions in recent years.
"It doesn't seem like a really smart, long-term idea," she said.
The issue of jobs also came up when one caller asked whether Albertans would be prioritized.

Smith said that was the goal, adding it was also why the referendum her government has scheduled for Oct. 19 will feature questions about whether Alberta should take more control over immigration and temporary foreign worker rules.
"That's certainly what I think should be done, and I want to just make sure that Albertans agree with us on that," the premier said.
Thursday's event also saw the government poll callers and those online about whether they supported setbacks to protect communities from having data centres built too close to homes.

items: Alberta Utilities Commission rejects power plant for Olds data centre plan

blocks.text: Proximity to homes is why a provincial regulator rejected a major data centre project last week in the town of Olds, north of Calgary. Smith had said on Wednesday that her government was already considering developing guidance for setbacks.
Wright shared that 57 per cent of respondents "strongly supported" the measure.

He also conducted another poll at the end of the event, asking those on the call to identify their greatest concern about data centres, with options including electricity affordability, grid reliability, water use, or other. The results weren't shared before the call ended.
Thursday's town hall began just hours after the Opposition called for a moratorium on AI data centres until stricter rules are put in place.
NDP Leader Naheed Nenshi told reporters that Smith's government has rushed ahead and rubber-stamped projects without clear guidelines or by first hearing Albertans' concerns.
Projects should go through impact assessments to ensure significant community benefits, permanent jobs, and that life-cycle plans for when facilities run their course are in place, he said.

items: Man planning protests against data centres as Alberta government announces town hall events

blocks.text: They're the concerns he said his party heard most when it hosted its own data centre town halls over the summer.
"The UCP failed to create a process that Albertans can have confidence in," Nenshi said.
He said his party's proposal would provide certainty for residents and those behind the projects.
The rejection of the Olds proposal, which had been turned down once before for other reasons, represents a government failure for not having clear expectations for developers, Nenshi added.
"There is no framework in place, and they're making it up as they go along," he said.
"Would a company like that want to invest in Alberta again after they were treated this way by the government?"

items: Why are there suddenly so many data centres planned in Canada? Your questions answered

blocks.text: The province didn't immediately respond to questions about the NDP's call for a moratorium on Thursday.
The issue of reclamation did come up during the town hall when a caller asked who would be stuck with the infrastructure should a data centre be abandoned.
Glubish said it would fall to the province. He said he was confident another company would come in and take the warehouse for "pennies on the dollar."
He also said an abandoned power plant would be considered a new asset for the province, and that the government would look to keep it running so that power is still fed to the electricity grid.
Smith added that reclamation for data centres was different than wind turbines, which her government requires operators to have clean-up plans for before being built.
"We have a high level of confidence that those [data centre] buildings will be able to be used for something else," she said.
The government's fourth and final data centre town hall is scheduled for Sept. 11 in Grande Prairie, though the premier isn't scheduled to attend.

articles.title: WHAT WE KNOW SO FAR: 1 Filipino still missing after deadly Nepal flash flood
articles.summary: One Filipino remains missing following the deadly flash flood that struck Nepal on Wednesday, with Philippine officials continuing to coordinate with Nepalese authorities and the Filipino community…

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 12:34pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.

One Filipino remains missing following the deadly flash flood that struck Nepal on Wednesday, with Philippine officials continuing to coordinate with Nepalese authorities and the Filipino community to locate the missing national.
Philippine Embassy in India Consul General Maria Cynthia Pelayo said Friday that they have yet to receive information on the Filipino whose disappearance was reported following the disaster.
“Until now, we are still waiting for information about the missing Filipino which was reported yesterday,” Pelayo said in a Super Radyo dzBB interview.
The Filipino is among the 667 foreign nationals from 32 countries listed as still missing in the update released by Nepal’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Thursday evening.
Other Stories
Nepalese authorities said 359 bodies had been recovered at that point.
Filipino community in Nepal accounted for
Pelayo said the Philippine Embassy has maintained close communication with the Filipino community in Nepal and that those they have accounted for are safe.
“Fortunately, they are all okay. They are well accounted for,” she said.

Most members of the Filipino community are in Kathmandu, according to Pelayo. She said around 90% of the profiles they have are spouses of Nepalese nationals, while the percentage of Filipino professionals in the country is “very minimal.”

The Philippine government earlier said there were 18 overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) in Nepal based on Overseas Workers Welfare Administration records, while Department of Foreign Affairs data showed 128 Filipinos in the country.
Rescue efforts continue
Pelayo said Nepalese authorities continue rescue operations in areas affected by the flash flood, although access to some locations remains difficult.
The Philippine official also noted that getting information from the affected areas has been difficult, saying it would be challenging for her to personally reach the location.

Nepal’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has established an emergency response team to coordinate search and rescue operations, verify information concerning missing foreign nationals and provide consular assistance. It has also urged families and diplomatic missions to rely on official channels and avoid circulating unverified information.
The disaster was triggered by a glacier collapse that sent a torrent of water, rock, ice and mud through Himalayan river systems along the Nepal-China border.
A Reuters report on Thursday quoting the Nepali police said that 359 had died, with dozens of bodies swept down into the plains from where they were being recovered.

Rescuers searched for survivors in the debris-strewn valleys and hillsides of Nepal on Thursday while more than 1,000 people remained missing there and in neighboring China after a wall of ice, mud and rock collapsed into a mountain river, triggering a catastrophic flash flood.
The Philippine government has also expressed condolences to Nepal and those affected by the disaster.

articles.title: Woman dies after re‑entering burning house in QC
articles.summary: A 25‑year‑old woman died after she reportedly went back inside a burning house to search for her mother on 13th Street in Barangay Damayang Lagi, Quezon City, on Friday morning, Aug. 28.…

blocks.text: Thick smoke and flames rise from a residential area in Damayang Lagi, Quezon City, on Friday morning, Aug. 28, as the blaze rages. (Photo courtesy of Libis Fire Volunteer Group)
A 25‑year‑old woman died after she reportedly went back inside a burning house to search for her mother on 13th Street in Barangay Damayang Lagi, Quezon City, on Friday morning, Aug. 28.

Investigators from the Bureau of Fire Protection‑Quezon City’s Arson Unit said the victim was about to jump from the third floor of the three‑story house when she remembered her mother and turned back.
A companion who was with her when the fire broke out was able to escape by jumping onto the roof, but the woman was not seen again and was eventually trapped inside the burning structure.
BFP-QC rescuers later searched the house using equipment from the Quezon City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (QCDRRMC).
Her body was eventually found beneath the debris.
The blaze spread through residential structures made of light materials and was first logged for verification at 6:51 a.m.
A smoke sighting was reported at 6:55 a.m., with the BFP raising the fire to first alarm at 7 a.m. and second alarm at 7:11 a.m.
The blaze was placed under control at 7:55 a.m. and declared fire out at 8:45 a.m.
Some residents helped firefighters by fetching water to refill a fire truck battling the blaze.
The BFP is still investigating the cause of the fire and assessing the extent of the damage.
The exact number of families affected and the value of the damaged properties have yet to be determined.
Barangay Damayang Lagi officials continue to coordinate with affected residents, who are also appealing for assistance.

articles.title: Philippine exports, imports lose steam as second half begins
articles.summary: Philippine merchandise trade lost momentum at the start of the second half of 2026, as both exports and imports posted slower annual growth in July and fell in value from the previous month. The…

blocks.text: Philippine merchandise trade lost momentum at the start of the second half of 2026, as both exports and imports posted slower annual growth in July and fell in value from the previous month.

The latest preliminary Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) data released on Friday, Aug. 28, showed exports grew by 10.8 percent year-on-year to $8.15 billion in July, sharply slower than the 25-percent expansion in June. Imports likewise rose by 19.8 percent to $14.12 billion, easing from the 25-percent growth recorded a month ago.

In value terms, exports fell by $681.31 million, or 7.7 percent, from the revised monthly record high of $8.83 billion in June, while imports declined by $204.52 million, or 1.4 percent, from $14.33 billion. As a result, total external trade dropped by $885.83 million, or 3.8 percent, month-on-month to $22.27 billion from $23.16 billion.
The July export value was the lowest since May, when outbound shipments amounted to $7.95 billion, while imports were also at their lowest since May’s $14.05 billion.
The slower trade performance came despite continued strong demand for Philippine electronic products, which remained the country’s top export commodity.

Electronics exports reached $4.79 billion in July, accounting for 58.8 percent of total outbound shipments. They also recorded the biggest annual increase among commodity groups, rising by $869.72 million from $3.92 billion a year ago.

Other commodities that contributed to the annual increase in exports were gold, which rose by $79.34 million; electronic equipment and parts, up by $71.81 million; machinery and transport equipment, up by $50.06 million; and woodcrafts and furniture, up by $30.92 million.

By major type of goods, manufactured goods remained the largest source of export earnings at $6.61 billion, equivalent to 81.1 percent of total. Mineral products followed at $776.61 million, or 9.5 percent of total, while agro-based products accounted for $548.95 million, or 6.7 percent.

Despite the July slowdown, exports in the first seven months of the year climbed by 12.9 percent to $54.92 billion from $48.67 billion in the same period last year, the highest January-to-July export value since the series began in 1991.

The United States (US) remained the Philippines’ biggest export market in July, accounting for $1.68 billion, or 20.7 percent of total exports. It was followed by Hong Kong at $1.29 billion, China at $919.82 million, Japan at $856.6 million, and Singapore at $401.17 million.
On the import side, electronic products also posted the biggest annual increase, surging by $1.75 billion to $4.6 billion and accounting for 32.6 percent of total imports.

This was followed by mineral fuels, lubricants and related materials, which increased by $502.71 million to $1.95 billion, and cereals and cereal preparations, which rose by $187.36 million to $561.06 million.

Raw materials and intermediate goods comprised the biggest share of imports at $5.71 billion, or 40.4 percent, followed by capital goods at $3.84 billion, or 27.2 percent, and consumer goods at $2.58 billion, or 18.3 percent.
From January to July, imports increased by 18.9 percent to $92.26 billion from $77.58 billion a year ago, also the highest first-seven-month import value since the series began in 1991.

China remained the country’s largest source of imported goods, supplying $4.17 billion, or 29.5 percent of total imports in July. It was followed by South Korea with $1.8 billion, Japan with $1.11 billion, Indonesia with $807.75 million, and the US with $766.61 million.

With imports continuing to outpace exports, the country’s balance of trade in goods posted a deficit of $5.97 billion in July, 34.9 percent wider than the $4.43-billion shortfall a year ago and the widest since the $6.1-billion deficit recorded in May.

Total external trade nevertheless remained 16.3 percent higher than the $19.14 billion recorded in July last year, although its annual growth also slowed from 25 percent in June. Imports accounted for 63.4 percent of July trade, while exports comprised the remaining 36.6 percent. - with a report from Danielle T. Bayani
