articles.title: Red rainfall warning up over Zambales, Bataan; NCR under yellow alert
articles.summary: Zambales and parts of Bataan were placed under a red rainfall warning on Friday morning, August 28, as the southwest monsoon or habagat continues to dump heavy rains over parts of Luzon.

blocks.text: Motorists and pedestrians are drenched during a heavy downpour in Quezon City as the habagat continues to batter in Metro Manila and neighboring provinces with strong winds and heavy rainfall on Aug. 8, 2026.
The Philippine STAR / Miguel de Guzman

MANILA, Philippines — Zambales and parts of Bataan were placed under a red rainfall warning on Friday morning, August 28, as the southwest monsoon or habagat continues to dump heavy rains over parts of Luzon.
In its heavy rainfall advisory issued at 11 a.m., state weather bureau PAGASA said that serious flooding is expected in flood-prone areas under the red warning level.
The following areas are under the red warning level:
PAGASA said flooding is still threatening in areas under the orange warning level, which covers:

items: Bataan: Abucay, Bagac, Balanga, Limay, Mariveles, Orani, Orion, Pilar and Samal

Nueva Ecija: Guimba, Santo Domingo, Talavera, Llanera, Rizal, Bongabon, Gabaldon, Laur, Palayan, General Mamerto Natividad, Cabanatuan, Aliaga, Quezon, Licab, Zaragoza, Jaen, Santa Rosa, San Leonardo, San Isidro, San Antonio, Cabiao, Gapan, General Tinio and Peñaranda

blocks.text: Meanwhile, flooding is possible in flood-prone areas under the yellow warning level, including:

items: Cavite: Bacoor, Imus, Kawit, Noveleta, Cavite City, Rosario, Tanza, Naic, Ternate, Maragondon, General Trias, Magallanes, General Emilio Aguinaldo and Alfonso
Nueva Ecija: Carranglan, Cuyapo, Lupao, Nampicuan, Pantabangan, San Jose, Muñoz and Talugtug

blocks.text: PAGASA said light to moderate rains with occasional heavy rains are also expected over Laguna and parts of Batangas and Cavite within the next three hours.

The weather disturbance has a medium chance of developing into a tropical depression within the next 24 hours.

articles.title: It works! Lucena inventor creates trash-collecting robot from recycled materials
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY, Quezon - An innovative method for cleaning waterways was demonstrated at the Iyam River using an improvised garbage-collecting robot made from recycled materials in this city. The device…

blocks.text: (Photo by Isagani Inciong via Danny Estacio)
LUCENA CITY, Quezon - An innovative method for cleaning waterways was demonstrated at the Iyam River using an improvised garbage-collecting robot made from recycled materials in this city.
The device was constructed using old plastic containers, aluminum, and galvanized wire mesh.
It is equipped with a garbage lifter designed to easily gather and collect floating debris.
The robot is operated via a remote control—similar to those used in computer games—that controls a small motor attached to the unit.
According to Isagani Inciong, an electronics technician and the device's inventor, he conceived the project to help reduce floating river debris, particularly plastic waste.
Tests conducted at the Iyam River proved the robot effective at gathering and retrieving floating trash.
Inciong added that aside from being fun to operate, the robot offers significant environmental benefits.
He believes that if more people use or "play" with this type of robot, a larger volume of waste can be recovered from waterways.

He also called on local government units (LGUs) to take notice of his invention and expressed willingness to collaborate with authorities to refine the design and build a larger version of the robot to support more extensive river rehabilitation efforts.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Misamis Oriental family deaths in 2021 due to COVID-19, not vaccines
articles.summary: A viral Facebook reel recycles a report from a 2021 incident involving four family members in Misamis Oriental; the health department has clarified that the deaths were associated with COVID-19…

blocks.text: Claim: Four members of one family in Laguindingan, Misamis Oriental, died because of COVID-19 vaccines after receiving their jabs.

Why we fact-checked this: A widely shared Facebook reel claims that four members of the same family died because of COVID-19 vaccines. Posted on August 16, 2026, it garnered around 19,400 reactions, 1,700 comments, and 19,000 shares as of writing.
The reel was posted by the Facebook account Unsa Gyod Gisulti SaBibliya, which has around 60,000 followers.
The account’s biography shows an anti-vaccination position, stating: “Va666ines= Mark Of The Beast! ✓Mandated (Rev13:16) ✓Required (Rev13:17) ✓Deceit (Rev18:23,19:20).”
It also has multiple reels opposing vaccines, many of which use the phrase, “Va666$in TATAK666 ng Antikristo nililinlang at nilalason mga kabataan.”
(Vaccines are marks of the Antichrist, deceiving and poisoning the youth.)

The post presents the incident, using a news report from GMA Regional TV, as evidence that COVID-19 vaccines were responsible for the deaths and questions the Department of Health (DOH)’s explanation of the case.
The facts: The four deaths were real, occurring between August 1 and 8, 2021, but available evidence does not support the claim that COVID-19 vaccination caused them.
According to an August 21, 2021 report by the Philippine News Agency, the DOH Region 10 found that the four individuals showed COVID-19 symptoms.
About 10 family members and neighbors were also infected. Investigators identified possible exposure at a wake in Barangay Patag, Cagayan de Oro City, and at a family birthday gathering.
Jasper Kent Ola, the nurse-epidemiologist who supervised the investigation, explained that the deaths occurred successively because of the different infection and incubation periods of the virus.
The Philippine Information Agency (PIA) later reported on August 23, 2021 that the four deceased family members tested positive for COVID-19 through RT-PCR tests.

The DOH-10 Regional Adverse Effect Following Immunization Committee also conducted a causality assessment based on case-tracking reports and found that the cases were “inconsistent with causal association to immunization.”
Investigators concluded that the individuals were likely already incubating the virus around the time of immunization.

Vaccination in the Philippines: The Facebook reel surfaced amid the DOH’s rollout of its nationwide Measles-Rubella Supplementary Immunization Activity this month. In an August 27 PIA report, the DOH said false information about vaccines continues to circulate on social media and may discourage parents from having their children immunized.
To counter this, the health department is partnering with local government units to conduct health education sessions and share reliable information on vaccines through social media.
Earlier, Rappler debunked circulating posts casting doubt on the safety of the measles-rubella vaccines. – Ahyenne Neleah Estacio/Rappler.com

Ahyenne Neleah Estacio is a graduating Bachelor of Arts in Communication student and campus journalist at Holy Angel University. The current senior editor and former editor-in-chief of The Angelite, she is an Aries Rufo Fellow for 2026.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: No place for violence, bullying in Baguio - Mayor Magalong
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY -- There is no place for violence, bullying, or any form of abuse, especially against children and young people in Baguio City. This was emphasized by Mayor Benjamin Magalong as he…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY -- There is no place for violence, bullying, or any form of abuse, especially against children and young people in Baguio City.
This was emphasized by Mayor Benjamin Magalong as he assured that the two separate violent incidents involving high school students are now being handled by the Baguio City Police Office.
Magalong urged the public not to circulate a video involving one of the cases to prevent online abuse.
"While we do not condone these acts among the youth, we should also respect the dignity, privacy, and well-being of the children involved."

He asked the public not to "share, repost, or further circulate the video" as further dissemination could expose minors to public shaming, harassment, insults, threats and other forms of online abuse.
Magalong urged the public to allow police authorities, school officials, and social workers to address the two separate cases judiciously.
“Let us not amplify violence. Let us protect our children and help build a safer, kinder, and more respectful Baguio,” he said.
The police said the two cases are being handled separately with details treated confidentially because minors are involved.
The first incident involving students reportedly occurred outside the school premises of a high school at around 3 p.m. on August 26.
Investigation report said complaints were filed with Police Station 2 and the minors involved, described as Grade 9 and Grade 10 students, have been identified.
Personnel of the Women and Children Protection Desk (WCPD) coordinated with the school authorities while appropriate intervention was undertaken with the assistance of social workers.
Police Station 2 had scheduled another coordination meeting on August 28 to discuss the matter and the appropriate interventions.
The second incident reportedly involved Grade 7 and Grade 9 students from another secondary school and was reported to Police Station 5 at around 1 p.m. on August 27.
The incident allegedly happened during recess on August 24 inside a classroom causing an injury to the complainant.

Police said WCPD personnel coordinated with the school principal and class advisers and a dialogue was later held with the students and their parents or guardians with administrative sanctions expected to be imposed.

articles.title: DSWD, DDB pilot program to curb drug abuse risks among street children, out-of-school youth
articles.summary: Children in street situations and out-of-school youth will be among the first beneficiaries of a new intervention that combines drug abuse prevention education with family, community, and…

blocks.text: Children in street situations and out-of-school youth will be among the first beneficiaries of a new intervention that combines drug abuse prevention education with family, community, and psychosocial support.

The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), in partnership with the Dangerous Drugs Board (DDB), is piloting “Program Silong,” an integrated program to be implemented through Special Drug Education Centers (SDECs).
The agencies conducted a week-long training for the program’s pilot implementation from Aug. 24 to 28 in Quezon City.
DSWD Special Assistant to the Secretary for Innovations Helen Suzara said the initiative seeks to strengthen drug and substance abuse prevention efforts among children and young people.
“Silong is an important step in strengthening our collective efforts towards drug abuse prevention, particularly among children and the young people,” Suzara said during the opening of the training.
The program has four components covering drug abuse prevention education, family involvement and support, community mobilization, and psychosocial and auxiliary services.
The education component includes toolkits designed for children, early to late adolescents, and parents or caregivers.

The family component will provide interventions to help parents and caregivers support drug abuse prevention efforts, while the community component will encourage communities to develop and implement prevention activities.
The psychosocial component will use pre- and post-assessments to identify the needs of children in street situations and out-of-school youth and monitor their progress.
Suzara described Program Silong as “a pioneering initiative, the first of its kind in the Philippines and in the ASEAN region.”
The program will initially be piloted in Muntinlupa City, Occidental Mindoro, and Zamboanga del Sur.

DSWD said the initiative is in line with its mandate under the implementing rules and regulations of Republic Act No. 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, to provide drug abuse prevention and developmental services to vulnerable children and youth.
It will also involve community volunteers and local government implementers in carrying out prevention activities in the pilot areas.

articles.title: Trump administration illegally retaliated against Anthropic, judge rules
articles.summary: The AI startup has been at loggerheads with the Pentagon over the use of AI by the US military.

blocks.text: A judge has ruled the US Department of Defense acted unlawfully when it designated artificial intelligence (AI) startup Anthropic a supply chain risk, calling the move "illegal and baseless".

The company argued in the lawsuit that Defense Secretary Pete Hegeth overstepped his authority with the new designation. It followed Anthropic's refusal to allow the military to use its AI models for things that included surveillance or autonomous weapons.
US district judge Rita Lin said in the ruling that citing national security "is not a blank check to punish and retaliate against government critics".
Anthropic welcomed the ruling. The BBC has contacted the Pentagon and the White House for comment.
Anthropic is focused on "working productively with the government to harness AI for our national security so all Americans benefit from this technology," a spokesperson told the BBC.
Judge Lin said in the court filing that the Defense Department had acted unlawfully to order firms that do business with the US military to boycott Anthropic.
The Pentagon designated Anthropic as a supply-chain risk in February - a law typically reserved for companies based in countries that pose a threat to the US.
It marked the first time an American company had been publicly designated as such.
Anthropic's lawsuit said the government's actions were both "unprecedented and unlawful".
The Claude-maker said its models were not reliable enough to be safely used in weapons systems for the military. It added that it opposed its use for domestic surveillance as a violation of rights.
The Pentagon said at the time that private companies should not be able to constrain military action.

The White House had previously said Anthropic was "a radical left, woke company" attempting to control military activity" and argued the military was beholden to the US Constitution, "not any woke AI company's terms of service".
The Pentagon also argued that Anthropic's refusal to accept new contract terms raised concerns over what the company could do with its technology.
Anthropic said in its lawsuit that its business had been impacted by the government's actions and its right to freedom of speech had been violated.
Judge Lin said during an earlier round in the lawsuit that the government was trying to "cripple" the company and "chill public debate" over military use of AI.
"This appears to be classic First Amendment retaliation," the judge added.

articles.title: LIVE UPDATES: Impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte
articles.summary: Bookmark this page for Rappler's comprehensive coverage of Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial at the Senate

blocks.text: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.

There are four articles of impeachment against Duterte involving alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.

Only 21 out of 24 senator-judges are physically present. Senator Bato dela Rosa remains in hiding as he faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, Senator Jinggoy Estrada has been detained and suspended in connection with a plunder case, and Senator Rodante Marcoleta surrendered to authorities as he also faces a plunder case.
On this page, we bring you the latest updates, analyses, videos, and photos as the trial of the Vice President unfolds.

articles.title: Court rejects Tarlac lawmaker Rivera’s bid to consolidate 9 graft cases
articles.summary: 'Instead of expediting the proceedings, consolidation will merely cause delay,' the anti-graft court says

blocks.text: ANTI-GRAFT COURT. The Sandiganbayan in Quezon City.
Jansen Romero/Rappler
'Instead of expediting the proceedings, consolidation will merely cause delay,' the anti-graft court says

items: The Sandiganbayan court rejected Representative Noel Rivera's request to consolidate his graft cases, citing that they involve different public works projects.
Rivera is accused of having an unlawful interest in Tarlac 3-G Construction and Development Corporation, which secured significant government contracts during his congressional term.
The court emphasized that consolidating the cases could lead to confusion and delays, as they involve separate contracts and are spread across multiple divisions.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The anti-graft court Sandiganbayan has rejected Tarlac 3rd District Representative Noel Rivera’s bid to have his graft cases handled by just one court division, saying these involve different public works projects and that lumping them together could cause confusion and delays.

In two separate resolutions on Thursday, August 27, the Sandiganbayan’s 6th Division denied Rivera’s motion for consolidation. The ruling, made by associate justices Sarah Jane Fernandez, Kevin Narce Vivero and Lord Villanueva, rejected the congressman’s contention that the nine cases were similar and that having only one division handle them would save time and resources.

Rivera is accused of keeping an unlawful interest in the construction firm Tarlac 3-G Construction and Development Corporation, which bagged government projects worth millions of pesos while he was serving as a member of the House of Representatives.

blocks.caption: Congress, contractors, conflict, corruption: A list of Rappler exclusives

blocks.text: Rivera has been accused by Ombudsman Boying Remulla of being one of the so-called “congtractors,” or members of the House of Representatives who keep stakes in companies that bagged juicy public works contracts.
Prosecutors have also accused him of owning a 54.8% stake in Tarlac 3-G, while his wife, Evelyn, allegedly held another 45%.
An earlier Rappler report cited DPWH data showing that Tarlac 3-G had already been winning a large share of government projects in Tarlac even before Rivera became a congressman.
Since Rivera entered Congress, Tarlac 3-G has secured P671 million worth of DPWH projects. The company reported total assets of P392 million in its 2024 financial statement.
Rivera’s cases were spread across six Sandiganbayan divisions, with the 5th, 6th and 7th divisions handling two cases each, while the 1st, 2nd and 4th divisions each took on one.
The court stressed that there was little chance of conflicting rulings because the cases involved separate contracts.

The cases involve contracts that Tarlac 3-G secured while Rivera was already serving as a congressman, with eight coming from the DPWH, while the Philippine State College of Aeronautics awarded the remaining contract.
“Instead of expediting the proceedings, consolidation will merely cause delay,” read part of the Sandiganbayan ruling. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Psychologists want us to rethink what we ask about school violence
articles.summary: Rather than neatly condense all the violence and trace it to one root cause, psychologists choose to ask the difficult questions about each individual case. Each child in conflict with the law is not…

blocks.text: This is Part 1 of a two-part story.

The kids aren’t alright. Only a few months into the school year, multiple cases of school violence have been reported throughout the Philippines, where the students themselves are the perpetrators inflicting harm on their school community. The most recent incident in Zamboanga was a school shooting that resulted in the death of two students: one who was fatally shot by his schoolmate, while the other was the shooter himself, who, after live streaming his violent acts on social media, ended his own life.

These incidents have alarmed psychologists and mental health practitioners, especially those who work with minors and young Filipinos. But rather than neatly condense all the violence and attribute it to one root cause, they choose to ask the difficult questions about each individual case. They want to understand each student not just as a perpetrator, but as a highly vulnerable person.

“When I heard about the school violence, I immediately asked, ‘What was happening to the teenager’s life that made her or him to be in that position?’” said psychologist Jannah Trixie Cuevas. “What was happening at home? What was happening in the school? Why did it happen in school? What comes to their mind before they started getting the gun? Did someone influence them? Did someone try to manipulate them?”

“No student will do that if they can handle things properly,” psychologist Arnel Sarte Jr. said. “We have to ask: What are they experiencing that pushed them to do that? What are they carrying on their own, until they reach a breaking point?”

Both Cuevas and Sarte work with Sapphire Clinics East Inc., a Filipino-owned rehabilitation and psychological services network in Metro Manila. In the two years they have been operating, the clinic has already handled more than 2,700 clients with a median age of 14 years old. In their work, they respond to warning signs in children and minors who exhibit mental health issues in order to prevent any “breaking points” from happening.

As minors, children and teenagers’ brains are not yet fully developed. Their prefrontal cortex, the part of their brain which manages decision making, emotion processing and control, and impulse regulation, will only fully mature around their mid-20s. Until then, they are “like sponges,” absorbing everything around them.

“Anything that they’re experiencing at school, at home, also what they’re seeing online, they will absorb quickly. Imagine all the risks that they can absorb while they’re growing up,” Sarte said. “If they’re exposed to bullying, invalidation, pressure, that can make them do things they don’t want to. As kids, their brain isn’t fully developed. They don’t have enough ways to properly process things.”

Processing difficult experiences and complex emotions with children is crucial for parents and schools. It is what will save their children from internalizing and carrying their struggles on their own to the point where they cannot bear it anymore. Once a child reaches a breaking point, they can either implode or explode; they can hurt themselves or hurt others.

In schools, experts say teachers and administrators are becoming more observant and attuned to the mental health warning signs and calls for help their students are exhibiting. Hannah Pellejo Jara, CEO and founder of Sapphire Clinics East, says that educational institutions have been partnering with them for more mental health support for their students because there are times when the school is no longer equipped to handle them.

“What they’re saying is there’s really a shift with the mental health of children,” she shared. “In their guidance office, they have concerns. That’s why they’re partnering with us. What we have seen are suicidal cases, depression cases. A lot of it is family conflict, I would say. We’re seeing a lot of anxiety, panic, and anger management, even in kids.”

Questions that seem reasonable to ask about this situation are, “Why are they like that?” or “What’s wrong with them?” But psychologists propose more productive questions that avoid connotations of defectiveness or blaming the child for things they perhaps could not control. “What are they going through?” “What is their family history like?” or “What did they experience?” are questions that instead seek to understand the child and see them as a whole person.
Guided by the biopsychosocial model, psychologists check the different dimensions of the child to understand their mental health vulnerabilities.

First is the biological factor, specifically their genes, brain chemistry, hormones, and overall physical health. Is their family vulnerable to mental health disorders? Is there a predisposition toward violence or issues like impulse control?

blocks.caption: [OPINION] If our answer starts at the school gate, we are too late

blocks.text: Second is the psychological factor. If they’re vulnerable to certain disorders, are they prone to being sensitive and emotionally or mentally overwhelmed? Are they moody? How do they cope with struggles and conflict? Do they have triggers?

Third, the social factor. What is their environment like at home? At school? Who are their support systems? Who are their friends? Do they feel supported and validated? What is their family’s socioeconomic situation?
The answers to these questions are the puzzle pieces that form the bigger picture of what burdens a person and has built up inside them.

“For a certain person to develop a disorder, there should be an interaction with the genes, the predispositions, and the social factors or environmental factors that would really nurture the disorder,” Cuevas said. “For example, you cannot inherit gambling itself, but the problems when it comes to impulse control. And then, you get connected with people who usually have problems when it comes to impulse control. It creates more tendencies to develop, but it’s not a guarantee.”

Children with mental health vulnerabilities might not even develop disorders if they have access to adequate support systems and safe spaces at home and in their immediate community. “Sometimes what happens is that they just get worse when the environment, when the kid is repeatedly exposed to triggers,” said Sarte.
What could these triggering environments look like?

“There could be a lot of invalidations at home, a lot of unprocessed [experiences] at home, a lot of negative emotions inside the home that teenagers no longer feel safe at home, I think some part of it is when there’s a lot of violence inside the home,” Cuevas said as examples, looking back on past anxiety, depression, and trauma cases.

These environments normalize aggression and violence and elicit stress over feeling unsafe. “Even though we think that the kids don’t have any reaction to it, something is going on with their minds,” Cuevas warned. “Especially teenagers, this is the age that they are making sense of what’s happening in the world. As they’re making sense of the world, it was normalized to just shout at people, to just be aggressive to people, to just not talk when things are not going well at home. It usually starts with that.”

One effect this has on children can result in mirrored behavior, where a kid mirrors the violence at home by bullying others. Another is the child developing a persistent sense of helplessness, of feeling small and defenseless against those harming them.
Cuevas is worried, however, by how children who experience helplessness could perceive the school violence cases, especially the live streamed Zamboanga shooting.

“For some kids who feel very helpless, very small of themselves, seeing this all over the social media for two to three days, maybe one week, gives them an idea. ‘Oh, I can do it too. For them, for me to feel more powerful,’ that gives them a sense of power again.”

She echoed the calls of fellow psychologists at the Psychological Association of the Philippines for social media users and members of the media to be responsible about their coverage of the incidents, especially with the risk of copycat behavior.

“The child who feels helpless, upon seeing the social media post doing such a thing like that could unconsciously provide a hero [image]. Like holding a gun, everyone bowing their head, they could have a different way of seeing it, ‘I’m more powerful than you guys. Before you were bullying me, before you were saying that I’m small, but now, holding this weapon gives me more power than all of you guys.’”

blocks.caption: [Be The Good] Not another school shooting please

blocks.text: This is what makes the Ateneo de Zamboanga school shooting particularly troubling. According to authorities, the shooter was a “very bright student” whom no one would have expected would do such a thing.
“It’s a wake-up call,” Cuevas said, “that even though someone is still performing, that doesn’t guarantee that your child is doing well emotionally.”

Sarte said this is why we need to be attentive and not so dismissive of early warning signs of mental health issues. Children aren’t just asking for attention or being dramatic — and being depressed or anxious isn’t something they want to happen to or that they set out to do.

And maybe that is what Filipino children need the most: families, schools, and communities that refrain from quick assumptions or dismissive attitudes, and instead are attentive, curious, and concerned about the heavy burdens their young hearts carry. – Rappler.com
Part 2 to be published on Saturday, August 29.
Elise Suarez is a Rappler intern from Puerto Princesa City and a Humanities student of the University of Asia & the Pacific.

articles.title: Tate brothers blast US jail conditions as they seek bail in UK extradition fight
articles.summary: Andrew and Tristan Tate's legal team argued in a Miami court that the two were not a flight risk.

blocks.text: Andrew and Tristan Tate have told a Florida court they should be released from jail so they can fight extradition to the UK on charges of rape and trafficking.
Wearing tan jail uniforms, the brothers maintained they did not commit the alleged crimes as they slammed conditions in US custody.

Government lawyers argued that the two were a flight risk and had bragged about having multiple passports, while defence attorneys said the two social media influencers' high profile would make it almost impossible for them to flee.
US Magistrate Judge Lauren Louis will issue a written ruling at a later date on whether to grant bail to the dual British-US citizens. The two were arrested in Miami on 19 July.
During Thursday's hearing, defence lawyers said the pair had complied with the terms of their release while they battled the UK charges and another case in Romania.
US authorities took the men into custody last month after the UK's Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) unveiled dozens of new charges against them.
The British authorities have until 16 September to submit a full extradition request.
The brothers, who arrived in court in shackles, were questioned in turn by their defence attorneys and government lawyers as they took the stand.
Andrew Tate, 39, declared he has "never committed the crimes I'm accused of".
Tristan Tate, 38, described his detention conditions as small and hot, with little sunlight and exercise.
"It's beginning to grate on me because I can't partake in helping with my defence," he told the court, according to CBS News, the BBC's US partner.
"It's death by scurvy," he said, adding that he had lost 14lb (6.3kg).
The British Embassy filed court documents asking the judge to keep the Tates in custody as the UK pursues extradition.
US government lawyers pushed back against the brothers' claims that they had exaggerated their wealth to massage their online personas.
The federal attorneys said the Tates had access to resources that could help fund an escape and they had bragged about having multiple passports.
But Andrew Tate, a former professional kickboxer, testified that to support himself financially, he "had to go back to the boxing ring against heavier, younger opponents", according to CBS News.
"I've said some stupid things, but sometimes you have to shake the internet to get noticed," he testified about his online statements, according to CBS.
"This is the reality of the internet.
"I'm being treated like El Chapo," he added, referring to the Mexican drug kingpin, "but I have a perfect record in the court system".
Under questioning from his attorney, Joseph McBride, Andrew Tate denied he was a human trafficker.
The defence also called Natasha Sesay, from England, to testify in support of releasing Andrew Tate.
She described a five-year romantic relationship, saying she had had one child with him and was expecting a second.
"It's nice having him at home," she told the court, reports CBS.
Sesay also said that despite his online persona, Andrew Tate "has never ever been violent toward women", according to CBS.
The UK has brought a total of 59 criminal charges against the Tates, including rape and counts relating to sex trafficking and indecent images of a child.
The British authorities filed 21 charges last year against the brothers, then 38 additional counts last month.
The combined charges involve seven accusers, UK prosecutors said.
The brothers also faced sex-trafficking charges in Romania in 2022, and were under a travel ban until they were allowed to come to the US in 2025.
"If I go to England they will lock me up," Tristan Tate said on the stand in Miami on Thursday, "and take everything I've ever worked for".
He also said the Romanian charges had "destroyed my entire life", reports CBS.
"They took everything, even the savings accounts for their [his children's] college funds. This case is make or break for me."
The Tates built an influencer empire in the so-called manosphere, showcasing a lifestyle of conspicuous wealth and excess.
Andrew Tate accumulated millions of followers among an audience of primarily young men.
The White House has said President Donald Trump will not intervene in the extradition case of the brothers, who have been vocal supporters of him.

blocks.caption: Three out of four grizzlies in a family that was frequenting Nelson, B.C., have been killed. (The Ursa Project)

blocks.text: A third grizzly in a family of four well-known bears in the West Kootenay has been killed.
A sow and three yearlings attracted attention in the community of Nelson as they travelled throughout the community.
Wildlife officials said they had become a danger as they were habituated to humans and rummaged through yards and garbage.

The mother bear, which had previously been relocated from Nelson and returned, was killed earlier this month as was one of its yearlings, which the B.C. Conservation Officer Service said was not a suitable candidate for relocation due to its age and health. The young bear walked with a limp, either from injury or deformity.

items: More stories from the B.C. Interior
Grizzly bear family returns to Nelson, B.C., after attempted relocation

blocks.text: The two other yearlings, a male and female, were relocated but soon turned up again in the community of Christina Lake.
While the female has since moved on, officials say the male continued to frequent residential neighbourhoods and was deemed unsuitable for a second relocation attempt.
The service said Thursday that "the male yearling was dispatched, in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines."
Poor food sources
Provincial wildlife biologist Garth Mowat said the "bears were really habituated to people."

"We had lots of good indication that the bears had been eating human food for most years of their lives. We did this translocation as kind of a last effort and a hope that these bears would revert to wild food and we could save part of the family group."
Andrew Milne with the B.C. Conservation Officer Service said killing bears is only used as a last resort.

items: Young grizzly bear with limp killed in Nelson, B.C., sparks rally

blocks.text: "Killing wildlife in the name of public safety takes a toll on all these officers," he said. "We don't take these decisions lightly and we try to do as much as we can with what we have."

Mowat said with drought conditions throughout the B.C. Interior, berry crops are poor and more bears will be looking to come into communities in search of food. Officials are once again warning people to remove any possible attractants including fruit trees, garbage and bird feeders in order to prevent human-wildlife conflict.

articles.title: P1-billion fund revitalizes Project Noah. But they need more help reaching LGUs.
articles.summary: 'We can mainstream the science, the knowledge into the plans of the community,' says disaster risk management expert Mahar Lagmay

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Project Noah has been revitalized with a P1-billion fund release from the 2026 national budget, half of which will go to up-to-date equipment such as LiDAR drones and the rest to operations and its researchers.
Despite this newfound support to this long-running program, there remains the problem of reaching more local governments with knowledge and maps that scientists generate.

Project Noah is a hazard monitoring program launched in 2012, considered a landmark project in the Philippines’ disaster risk reduction and management. The Rodrigo Duterte administration pulled the plug on the program in 2017, which was then under the Department of Science and Technology. Project Noah did not completely disappear but with its termination, the program lost most of its experts and reach.
Currently, the University of the Philippines Resilience Institute (UPRI) manages Project Noah.

With the new funds, UPRI intends to prioritize using cutting-edge technology. This would allow it to generate higher resolution maps of major river basins, a huge improvement from the maps generated when Project Noah was launched 14 years ago. It will also continue promoting nature-based solutions to disaster risk reduction and management.

Mahar Lagmay, the institute’s executive director, listed down their priority areas in budget allocation such as: simulation of major detention basins, LiDAR drone surveys with educational institutions, native tree-mapping and inventory. Higher resolution is not just a quality issue; with it, UPRI researchers will be able to see where exactly flooding happens in a particular street.
Lagmay said they need help in disseminating information, including reaching more local governments so they can apply science to disaster risk management.

“We can mainstream the science, the knowledge into the plans of the community,” Lagmay said in a mix of Filipino and English on Thursday, August 27. “We want the plans of the community to be in accordance with the vision of the stakeholders.”
Lagmay said Project Noah will continue to prioritize support for the government’s flagship flood mitigation program Oplan Kontra Baha.

“The business of hazards mapping is not just to identify the hazards but more importantly to identify the safest places in the community for development and for citing evacuation centers,” Lagmay said.
According to Lagmay, UPRI has worked with at least 20 local governments on hazard and risk mapping in a span of eight years.
A notable partnership of UPRI was with the Quezon City local government. The result was a city-wide drainage master plan that relied on “science and nature-based solutions to mitigate flooding.”

All local governments UPRI has worked with “were really aggressive” and “wanted to change the system,” said Lagmay. Working with a local government to find ways to mitigate flooding and other hazards takes one to two years.
University of the Philippines President Angelo Jimenez said the university is “not an implementing arm” but only provides the knowledge and resource.
“It’s our mandate to offer this resource to the people,” Jimenez said in the same press briefing. “I believe that because of recent events, there is more appreciation of our work.”
He referred to the P1-billion funding as some sort of recognition, but it will need to be replenished if the government wants to continue Project NOAH. – Rappler.com
Quotes translated to English for brevity.

MANILA, Philippines — Several areas in Luzon, including Metro Manila, are expected to experience heavy rains on Friday, August 28, as the southwest monsoon or habagat continues to affect the country, state weather bureau PAGASA said.
As of 5 a.m. on Friday, PAGASA weather specialist Obet Badrina said that heavy rains are likely over Metro Manila, the Ilocos Region, parts of Central Luzon, Calabarzon and Occidental Mindoro.
The affected areas in Central Luzon include Bataan and Zambales.
The rest of Luzon will generally have cloudy skies with scattered rain showers and thunderstorms, particularly over the eastern portion of the island, Badrina said.
Palawan and the Visayas may likewise experience cloudy weather with chances of scattered rain showers.
Meanwhile, Mindanao will have partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rain showers.
Badrina said Mindanao is not expected to experience prolonged rainfall, with relatively warm weather prevailing over the island.

articles.title: Qatar steps in to mediate as Trump says US not talking to Iran
articles.summary: Iran's leadership expresss distrust toward the US and outlines conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz

blocks.text: CRISIS. US and Iranian flags are seen in this illustration taken March 23, 2026.
REUTERS
Iran's leadership expresss distrust toward the US and outlines conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz

items: Qatar's Prime Minister visited Tehran to promote diplomacy amid ongoing tensions and US sanctions against Iran, while President Trump stated that the US is not currently engaging in talks with Iran.
Iran's leadership emphasizes the demand for the US to lift sanctions and provide compensation.

Despite military setbacks, Iran maintains significant military capabilities and has engaged in discussions with Oman regarding traffic management in the Strait of Hormuz, while the US continues its economic campaign against Iran.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Qatar’s prime minister visited Tehran on Thursday, August 27, in an effort to revive stalled diplomacy six months into the war, as US President Donald Trump said Washington was not currently talking to Iran.

“We don’t want to speak to them. We’re not looking to meet or anything,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office after the White House said a US economic campaign against Tehran would continue until Iran decides to negotiate meaningfully.

Major combat operations have been paused for weeks but there has been little progress toward a wider peace agreement or reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route. Six months after US and Israeli forces attacked Iran, killing its supreme leader and maiming his son and successor, the Iranian government is under economic siege, but it still holds power and has shown little urgency to negotiate.

Trump, facing political pressure at home over higher energy prices ahead of November congressional elections, has opted to focus on economic sanctions, but aggressively enforcing them would require taking measures against Iranian trade partners such as China and India.

In Tehran, Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani urged a return to diplomacy during talks with Iran’s top negotiator Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf on Thursday, Qatar’s foreign ministry said.

Iran in turn called on regional neighbors to prevent the US from using their territory to carry out military or economic attacks on Iran, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on his Telegram account.

Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, told the Qatari prime minister that Tehran would strike US military and economic interests if Washington engaged in “mischief” against Iran, Iranian media reported.

Rezaei said the United States must take steps to meet Iran’s conditions before Tehran moved to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Those conditions include an end to the US blockade on Iranian ports, compensation and removal of sanctions.
“We do not trust the United States; it has repeatedly betrayed diplomacy and negotiations,” Rezaei said.

A June memorandum of understanding between Washington and Tehran collapsed in part over the future of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman through which about a fifth of global energy supplies passed before the war.
Iran has sought to exert control over the strait and charge fees to ships it authorizes, while Washington insists it should remain an open international waterway.

Al Thani said on X that he stressed the importance of freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. He and the Iranian foreign minister also discussed a proposal to establish a temporary joint Iranian-Omani shipping corridor through the strait and a joint project to clear mines, Qatar’s foreign ministry said.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Wednesday that Iran and Oman had agreed in principle on administering traffic in the strait and sharing revenues, but a senior Iranian source later said the two countries were still working on the details of an agreement.

Iran is preparing a list of conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz after mediators asked Tehran to set them out, Rezaei said. Ships would use a designated central channel if the US met Iran’s conditions, he said through an interpreter in an Al Manar TV interview.
White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said on Thursday that Trump “continues to retain all options on the table” with regard to Iran.
“We’ve had Operation Epic Fury to destroy their military. Now we have Operation Economic Outcast to destroy their economy,” Leavitt said in an interview with Fox News.
“No negotiations are happening right now, and this will continue until the president feels that maybe they come to the table in a meaningful way,” she said. “We have not seen that yet.”
Tehran has lived under various forms of US sanctions since the Islamic revolution in 1979.
Despite suffering heavy military losses, Iran retains enough missile and drone capability to strike Gulf states that host US forces and disrupt shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
The International Maritime Organization has reported 70 incidents in the strait since February 28 that have killed 19 seafarers.

Thousands of others have died, mostly in Iran and Lebanon, since the US and Israel attacked Iran with the stated goals of denying Iran a nuclear weapon, helping Iranians topple their government, and destroying Tehran’s missile program. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic dead
articles.summary: BELGRADE, Serbia — Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb military chief who was convicted of war crimes for his role in the 1995 Srebrenica massacre, died in a hospital on Thursday, according to a…

blocks.caption: Ex-Bosnian Serb military chief Ratko Mladic gestures from the defendant box during the hearing of the final verdict on appeal against his genocide conviction over the 1995 Srebrenica massacre, Europe’s worst act of bloodshed since World War II, on June 8, 2021, at the International Residual Mecha…

blocks.text: BELGRADE, Serbia — Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb military chief who was convicted of war crimes for his role in the 1995 Srebrenica massacre, died in a hospital on Thursday, according to a United Nations international tribunal.

Mladic, who had suffered several strokes in recent months, was serving a life sentence in The Hague for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity after overseeing the Srebrenica slaughter, Europe’s worst act of bloodshed since World War II.
His conviction for wartime killings as the former Yugoslavia descended into carnage following the fall of communism led the media to dub him the “Butcher of Bosnia.”
The 1992-1995 war left around 100,000 people dead and 2.2 million displaced.
Mladic was the military face of a brutal trio, led on the political side by former Yugoslav President Slobodan Milosevic and former Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic.
Serbian state officials and Mladic’s family had appealed for his release due to his failing health, but those calls were rejected by the Hague tribunal.
A representative of the Mothers of Srebrenica victims’ association, reacting to Mladic’s death, told AFP that his name would always “symbolize genocide.”
“That will never be erased from his name,” said Sehida Abdurahmanovic, who believes her missing brother was among those killed in Srebrenica.
Srebrenica
In the war’s most infamous atrocity, Serb forces under Mladic’s command executed 8,000 Bosnian Muslim men and boys who had sought shelter in Srebrenica, which was meant to be a UN-protected enclave.
Their bodies were dumped in mass graves, many of which were dug up and reburied in an attempt to hide the evidence.
The few who escaped told harrowing stories of murder, torture and rape by Bosnian Serb forces.
In November 1995, the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia (ICTY) indicted Mladic, who was dismissed from his post but evaded capture for another 16 years.
At first, he led a life of luxury, pampered by the military in Serbia, where some to this day see him as a hero.
But the pressure mounted on him after Milosevic fell from power in 2000. Mladic was finally arrested in May 2011 and transferred to The Hague.
He was convicted in 2017, with the life sentence upheld on appeal in 2021.
On the streets of Bosnia’s capital, Sarajevo, Hava Suljic told AFP she welcomed the news.
“I’m delighted to know there is one less war criminal walking around in this world,” Suljic, a Bosnian Muslim from Srebrenica, said.
But reactions in the Serb entity of divided Bosnia were in stark contrast.
Former Bosnian Serb leader Milorad Dodik said Mladic’s death had “hit hard” and that the Republika Srpska “will not forget his role,” the Serb statelet’s public broadcaster reported.
Locals who spoke with AFP in the Republika Srpska’s capital, Banja Luka, called Mladic the “greatest.”
“The greatest man has died, the greatest general of the Serbian people,” pensioner Dragan Beric said.
‘Epitome of evil’
Mladic was also found guilty of orchestrating a wider campaign of ethnic cleansing to drive Muslims and Bosnians out of key areas to create a so-called Greater Serbia.
The tribunal said at the time that the crimes committed were “among the most heinous known to humankind.” Former UN rights chief Zeid Ra’ad al Hussein described him as “the epitome of evil.”
But many Serbs continued to revere a military commander who portrayed himself as a “simple man” whom fate had chosen to protect his people.

articles.title: Philippines, UK begin talks on proposed visiting forces agreement
articles.summary: The Philippines and the United Kingdom have started formal negotiations for a proposed Status of Visiting Forces Agreement (SOVFA), the Department of National Defense (DND) said Thursday.

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 7:55am
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.
The Philippines and the United Kingdom have started formal negotiations for a proposed Status of Visiting Forces Agreement (SOVFA), the Department of National Defense (DND) said Thursday.
In a statement, the DND said the first round of negotiations was held on Thursday as Manila and London sought to strengthen defense cooperation and interoperability between their armed forces.

The Philippine panel was led by DND Undersecretary for Acquisition and Resource Management Salvador Melchor B. Mison Jr., while the UK panel was headed Ministry of Defence Indo-Pacific head Amy Senior.

"We appreciate UK’s unqualified support as a like-minded partner in upholding the rules-based international order and preserving freedoms ensured by the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)," Mison said.
Other Stories
The discussions focused on improving strategic defense initiatives and interoperability between the Philippine and British armed forces.

For the DND, the talks reflected the two countries' shared commitment to promoting regional peace and security through the rule of law, particularly amid increasingly complex security challenges in the Indo-Pacific.

Visiting forces deals provide the legal framework governing foreign troops temporarily conducting activities in Philippine territory, covering jurisdiction, entry and exit procedures, logistics support, and military cooperation.
The countries with visiting forces pact with the Philippines include the United States, Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Canada, and France.

In recent years, the Philippines has strengthened its defense agreements with other countries under President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. amid growing security concerns involving China in the West Philippine Sea. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Trump signs order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America
articles.summary: Trump's order comes after the trade talks between the US and Canada collapsed late last week.

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order seeking to change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America.

The move comes after trade talks between the US and Canada collapsed late last week, and the US imposed new 50% tariffs on $20bn (C$28bn) worth of Canadian goods. Canada will implement "dollar for dollar" counter tariffs next month.
Trump has repeatedly posted threats about renaming the lake, one of the five Great Lakes that straddle both countries, on social media amid the trade dispute.
He said on Thursday the move was "official, effective immediately" and that his administration has "filed all the necessary papers, documents" to make the change.

Text of the executive order says it gives the US Department of the Interior 30 days to update the name change with the Geographic Names Information Service - the official repository of domestic geographic names in the US.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney noted the name Lake Ontario can be traced back more than 400 years, adding in a social media post on Thursday that preceded the formation of the Canadian Confederation and the US Declaration of Independence.

"We know that the United States is changing. Their trade relations, their foreign policy, their national monuments, their hydronyms," he wrote. "Canadian women and men also know that things must be called by their name, and this lake is called Lake Ontario – today and forever."

When Trump took the White House in 2025, he signed a similar order that changed the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America. Mexico has rejected the name change, arguing a single country cannot rename a shared body of international water.
It also led to a legal dispute between Mexico and tech giant Google, which renamed the gulf in its maps application. , external
In that case, Google Maps users in the US see "Gulf of America", while those in Mexico see the "Gulf of Mexico". Those in other countries see the "Gulf of Mexico (Gulf of America)".

The White House at the time also blocked Associated Press reporters from presidential events over the news agency's refusal to adopt the name "Gulf of America" in its coverage. The AP sued the Trump administration in response, and that legal battle is ongoing.

There is no universally recognised international body setting the names of international waters. While the US president has broad discretion over how his country officially recognises landmarks, other countries do not have to follow.
Canada does not have to recognise name changes made by other countries and officials there have dismissed the idea.
Ontario Premier Doug Ford wrote on social media, "It's Lake Ontario to Canadians and the rest of the world. Now and forever."
Nova Scotia Premier Tim Houston agreed, saying "We're into some real foolishness now. It's Lake Ontario, buddy."
"We'll always call it Lake Ontario," said Industry Minister Melanie Joly on Tuesday.

The names of four of the Great Lakes - Ontario, Huron, Michigan and Erie - originate from indigenous words. Lake Superior was named after an anglicised French word. Lake Ontario, the smallest of the Great Lakes, borders both the Canadian province and the US state of New York.
As he signed the order on Thursday in the Oval Office, Trump said it wasn't a direct message to Canada, but that America's northern neighbour "has been ripping us off for a long time on trade".
Trump said he'd been thinking about renaming the lake "for a long time".
"So if you think about it, we have a gulf and we have a lake," Trump said.
"Now, all we need is an ocean. So maybe we'll have to change the name of the Atlantic and or the Pacific. Maybe we'll change them both."

The name change request comes amid a trade dispute that has seen US-Canada relations fall to new lows, with insults thrown back-and-forth between the Trump administration and Canadian officials over the past week.
There was a hint on Thursday that there was room for a return to the negotiating table sometime in the future.

Canadian US trade minister, Dominic LeBlanc, said in a post on X that the US had withdrawn some of its demands around labelling requirements in French "and is confirming that measures to promote French language and Canadian culture will not be subject to future US trade actions".
"We look forward to further constructive US clarifications on their other positions, which would create the possibility of a mutually beneficial trade agreement that respects Canadian sovereignty".
Trade talks collapsed at the last minute late on Friday night, with both sides accusing the other of demanding last-minute changes to a tentative deal.

Democratic lawmaker Debbie Dingell of Michigan, the US state that borders four of the five Great Lakes, said that she would introduce a bill in Congress to nullify the name change, calling Trump's order "idiotic".
She wrote, "The Great Lakes are a shared treasure that generations of Americans and Canadians have worked together to protect".

Other Democratic lawmakers in the US also criticised the order on social media, calling for the Trump administration to get back to negotiating on a trade deal. Some mocked Trump's idea and posted their own ideas to change the names of other landmarks.

Wisconsin's governor joked, "I just renamed Lake Michigan Lake Wisconsin," in a social media post with a video of himself signing a napkin on one of the Great Lakes. "See, I can sign napkins that say things, too," he added.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul said her state, the sole US state bordering Lake Ontario, "won't be calling it" Lake America.
Meanwhile, Trump's Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum applauded the move, writing, "We're on it, Mr. President!"

"The places and waters that border our nation and support our economy should reflect the greatness of the United States," he said, adding that the US Geological Survey "maps our country for the world to see, and we are PROUD to implement your Executive Order to rename LAKE AMERICA".

articles.title: PH may be caught in US rivals’ ‘crosshairs’ – Tinio
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Deputy Minority Leader and ACT Teachers Rep. Antonio Tinio on Thursday warned that the growing US presence in the country’s military and economic assets could put the…

blocks.caption: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., left, speaks during a meeting with Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, right, at the Pentagon, Monday, July 21, 2025, in Washington. (AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein)

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Deputy Minority Leader and ACT Teachers Rep. Antonio Tinio on Thursday warned that the growing US presence in the country’s military and economic assets could put the Philippines in the “crosshairs” of its rivals.

“In the event of a war between the US and China over the Taiwan issue, we can infer that China would target US facilities—both military and commercial—located in the Philippines. Our concern is that the US presence in the country is situated within our strategic and critical economic infrastructure,” Tinio said in a statement released on Thursday.

Tinio’s statement followed his heated exchange with Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro during the House committee on appropriations’ hearing on the proposed 2027 budget of the Department of National Defense last Tuesday, Aug. 25.

During the hearing, Tinio raised reports that US soldiers had attempted to enter the Philippine Veterans Investment Development Corporation Industrial Authority in Tagoloan, Misamis Oriental, where the new Philippine Navy dry dock is set to be established.
Teodoro dismissed claims about US interest in the dry dock, saying the presence of foreign troops was for the Balikatan loading exercise.
For Tinio, however, the incident was part of a broader pattern of Washington’s agenda in the country.
He cited the US-led Pax Silica, the US Navy’s use of Subic Bay for repairs and plans for an oil depot in Davao Gulf.

Tinio said the growing US presence in strategic military and economic facilities was particularly concerning because the Philippines lacks the capacity to defend these assets should geopolitical tensions escalate.
“How is the Philippines? The Gulf states are rich countries. They can afford high-tech missile defenses. How are we? What is the capability of the Armed Forces to defend these facilities?” he asked.
Tinio called on the public to remain vigilant against “foreign manipulation and intervention.”
“We must oppose all efforts to sell us out,” he added. /mcm

blocks.text: B.C.'s forests minister says a provincewide state of emergency due to wildfires has ended, but wildfire risk remains.
The province declared a state of emergency on Aug. 8 after the Bald Range wildfire forced the evacuation of thousands of Summerland-area residents.
The state of emergency was extended on Aug. 21, but Forests Minister Ravi Parmar told journalists in Summerland Thursday that the tools are no longer necessary.

"We are not done with this wildfire season. We still have many days and weeks ahead. We know that our fire seasons are more intense and they are longer. But we don't need these tools at this time," Parmar said.

Battling Summerland blaze 'like a jet engine coming up behind you': firefighter
He encouraged tourists to return to the Okanagan to help businesses get back on their feet.
"I think it's also equally important for me to say to a community that is struggling because of the impact of this that they need your help right now," he said.
"It's important for us to recognize the strength of Summerland, and the best way we can do that is by buying local, buying B.C., coming up and flooding their hotel rooms and spending our money here."
Offroad vehicle ban to be lifted
The B.C. Wildfire Service announced Thursday that they are lifting an offroad vehicle ban that was put in place in many parts of the province.
The ban is set to expire Friday at noon PT.

articles.title: What we know about deadly Nepal-Tibet floods
articles.summary: Hundreds have died or are missing in Wednesday's flooding and landslides on the border of Nepal and Tibet.

blocks.text: Video shows scale of flash flood hitting Nepal-Tibet border
ByOlivia Ireland and Henry Moore
Massive landslides and flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have caused widespread damage and left hundreds dead or missing.
Search and rescue operations are continuing after Wednesday's disaster. Chinese state media has said there are significant casualties, while Nepalese officials describe "huge scale loss".
There are risks of more floods: a lake of rising water has formed at a site along the China-Nepal border - prompting fears it could burst its banks.
Here is what we know so far.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Military teams were brought in to help with rescue and evacuation following the flooding on Wednesday

blocks.text: Image source, Nepal Army via EPA
Military teams were brought in to help with rescue and evacuation following the flooding on Wednesday
What caused the deadly landslide?
Initial reports of an earthquake on the Nepal-Tibet border led many to believe that a tremor had caused a landslide, which in turn caused the devastating flood.
However, the US Geological Survey has clarified that the disaster was caused by a "glacial collapse", which is when a glacier or part of a glacier disintegrates.
The impact of the collapsed glacier hitting the bottom of a valley was so powerful that it registered a magnitude of 5.2, according to USGS data and scientists who have analysed the event.
Debris flow from the collapse "caused subsequent catastrophic impacts downstream" the USGS said.

blocks.caption: Map showing the path of floodwaters along the Lende Khola, Bhote Koshi and  Trishuli rivers in northern Nepal after a glacier collapse near the Tibet border. The collapse sent ice and rock debris into the river, triggering flooding that destroyed a border checkpoint and continued downstream past…

blocks.text: Climate change is known to be driving faster glacier melt in the Hindu Kush Himalaya region and, as rescue efforts continue, scientists are trying to piece together the exact order of events.
Simon Cook, senior lecturer in energy environment and security at the University of Dundee who specialises in glaciology, said "climate change could have an impact".
Cook said his team had detected that the lower part of a glacier in Nepal near the Langtang Lirung peak - which is approximately 15km (9 miles) west of the site of the floods - had collapsed.
He estimated that the glacier collapsed in a north-westerly direction and then travelled westwards downstream.
He told the BBC "permafrost is partially holding some mountainsides together, this permafrost is warming and thawing and degrading so you are going to get more landslides".
Mike Searle, professor of Earth sciences at Oxford University, said the glacier could have collapsed "hours or days" before the flooding hit Nepal and Tibet.
He told the BBC: "I think the sheer wave of debris suggests there was a landslide first, the water built up, (which) dammed the river, and then it burst in one huge great flood."
One possibility is that water from rainfall or melting ice may have destabilised the ground or ice, triggering a chain reaction.

Scientist will be looking at satellite images of exactly where the landslide occurred, whether any glacial lakes suddenly drained, and where the river might have become blocked, as well as data on recent rainfall.

A deluge of material careered towards northern Nepalese towns, including areas popular with mountaineering tourists and pilgrims. The border is around 40 miles (64.4km) north of Nepal's capital city Kathmandu.
Footage showed a wall of mud and rock sweeping away buildings, roads and vehicles, as people fled the fast-moving wave of material in the Nuwakot region.
In one video, a towering wall of water and mud was seen rushing down a gorge along the Trishuli River and enveloping the Rasuvagadhi Border check point, a multi-storey building.
Severe flooding has been reported along the Bhote Koshi, Trishuli and Narayani rivers.
Deaths have also been reported in villages on the Tibetan side of the border.
The International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIDMOD) has warned secondary flooding could occur in the coming days as a result of the debris that washed into the river systems.

In a report, the ICIDMOD said they are in the process of assessing whether the Trishuli River has been temporarily blocked in narrow sections. If it has been blocked, it is at risk of forming a landslide dam - and a second flooding event.
Authorities and scientists are continuing to evaluate the size, location and stability of any potential blockages.
Watch: BBC Nepali's Shreejana Shrestha is at a hospital in Kathmandu, where some survivors are being flown in by helicopter
How many people are dead and missing?
The number of people killed or missing is still becoming clear.
Nepali police say at least 389 people have died. Among those killed, 64 were found in downstream areas in the Chitwan district while another 26 were found in Nawalparasi East.

In its latest update on Thursday evening, Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said 910 people were still missing. This included 517 foreign citizens, 44 members of the Nepal Army and 28 Nepal police officers.
Meanwhile, China's state broadcaster CCTV said on Thursday that the number of people missing in the mudslide disaster in Tibet's Gyirong county had risen to 558.
Among these are 260 foreign nationals, CCTV said, adding that the death toll remained at three.
The Nepal Tourism Board said on Thursday that 644 tourists were still missing, 33 of which were UK nationals, including a 13-year-old girl and 14-year-old boy.
It is not clear if any of the missing in the Nepali and Chinese figures have been counted twice.
The border at Gyirong is the main crossing point for tourists and traffic between China and Nepal.

blocks.caption: Police officers carrying an elderly woman who survived the flash flood at Trishuli in Nuwakot district of Nepal

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
How are governments responding?
Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah said "the entire nation has been left shocked and deeply distressed" and that officials would coordinate with China on the response.
China's President Xi Jinping urged an "all-out" search effort, and promised stronger monitoring and early warning systems to prevent secondary impacts.
In neighbouring India, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said his government was "prepared to provide Nepal with all possible types of humanitarian assistance".

UN Secretary General António Guterres says he is "saddened by the severe flooding", adding that UN teams and partners are mobilising supplies and personnel in Nepal to support the government-led response.
The US has promised $500,000 (£367,982) in aid which will be used to cover emergency shelter, water, sanitation and other relief items for communities affected by the floods.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the UK has offered £5m to help the Nepalese government and will do "everything we can" to support British nationals in Nepal.
Aerial footage shows flash flood on Nepal-Tibet border
What countries are the missing tourists from?
Tourists from all over the world come to Nepal for its mountains and sacred sites. Official figures suggested at least 291 foreigners are among the missing, including:

items: India - the Nepal Tourism board says 288 nationals from neighbouring India are missing
China - The Chinese foreign ministry says nearly 100 Chinese nationals are missing in Nepal
US - the latest update from Nepal's tourist board is that 65 US tourists are known to be among the missing
Ukraine - Ukraine's foreign ministry says 53 Ukrainian nationals are missing
Malaysia - 51 Malaysians travelling with Fishtail Tours and Travels are missing in the floods, officials say
Australia - Australia's foreign minister says 39 Australians are among the missing and there's an "unfortunate possibility" the number will rise
UK - Nepal's police say 33 British nationals are missing
Canada - a tourism board spokesman in Nepal says 24 Canadians are reported missing

blocks.text: Smaller numbers of travellers from South Korea, South Africa, Portugal, the Netherlands and New Zealand are also among the missing.
