articles.title: Kim Jong-un sidelines father’s legacy as his own era takes shape
articles.summary: North Korea’s muted commemoration this week of a key anniversary tied to former leader Kim Jong-il offers another glimpse into a broader transformation under his son: an effort to build a state…

blocks.caption: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un watches a commemorative march marking the 73rd anniversary of what North Korea calls its victory in the Korean War at the Pyongyang Indoor Stadium Square on July 27 in this image aired by North Korea’s state-run Korean Central Television the following day. (KCTV-Yo…

blocks.text: North Korea’s muted commemoration this week of a key anniversary tied to former leader Kim Jong-il offers another glimpse into a broader transformation under his son: an effort to build a state defined increasingly by Kim Jong-un himself, not the legacies of the two leaders who came before him.

The Rodong Sinmun, the official newspaper of North Korea’s ruling Workers’ Party, relegated its coverage of the Aug. 25 anniversary associated with Kim Jong-il’s “Songun,” or military-first, leadership to page two on Wednesday, an unusual departure from the prominent treatment the occasion received as recently as last year.

More strikingly, the article mentioned the word “Songun” only once. In previous years, Rodong Sinmun repeatedly invoked Kim Jong-il’s “Songun leadership” and “Songun journey” in commemorating the anniversary.

Instead of opening its front page with Kim Jong-il’s military legacy, the newspaper led with Premier Pak Thae-song’s economic inspection activities and efforts to fulfill the five-year national development plan adopted at the ninth Workers’ Party Congress in February.

The change appears to be the latest in a pattern that has accelerated this year: Kim Jong-un is not abandoning the legitimacy inherited from his grandfather Kim Il-sung and father Kim Jong-il, but is increasingly recasting it around a political system, national identity and personality cult that belong distinctly to his own era.

South Korea’s National Intelligence Service has gone a step further in its assessment. The spy agency told lawmakers earlier this year that Pyongyang appears to be simultaneously diluting the political imprint of Kim’s predecessors, elevating Kim’s status and reorganizing its institutions in an apparent attempt to present North Korea as a more “normal state.”
From Kim Jong-il’s military-first era to Kim Jong-un’s state

Aug. 25 marks what North Korea describes as the day Kim Jong-il began his leadership of the country’s revolutionary armed forces in 1960 with a visit to the Ryu Kyong Su 105th Tank Division, which Pyongyang says was the first North Korean unit to enter Seoul during the 1950-53 Korean War.
The date subsequently became closely associated with Songun, the military-first doctrine that came to define Kim Jong-il’s rule, particularly during the economic crisis and famine of the 1990s.
North Korea formally designated Aug. 25 as a national holiday and day of rest in 2013.

The anniversary received far more prominent treatment in previous years. Last year, the newspaper devoted extensive coverage to Aug. 25, portraying it as the anniversary of Kim Jong-il’s start of leadership over the revolutionary armed forces and recalling that the date had brought about “a historic turn” in “developing our revolutionary armed forces and implementing the cause of the Juche revolution.”
This year was different.

The Rodong Sinmun article focused on Chol Pass in Kangwon Province, a mountainous route that occupies an important place in North Korea’s mythology surrounding Kim Jong-il’s repeated visits to military units.
The article still lavished praise on the late leader and credited his arduous journeys with helping North Korea emerge as “a nuclear weapons state, a military power.”
Yet its narrative repeatedly led back to the current leader.

It recalled Kim Jong-un crossing Chol Pass in 2012, quoted his remarks on his father’s devotion and concluded by calling on North Koreans to “hasten the bright future of communism” by faithfully upholding Kim Jong-un’s leadership.
The change is notable because it reflects a much broader retreat from the governing model associated with Kim Jong-il.

“The reduction in the significance of Songun Day and similar moves can be understood as part of the process of clearing away the legacy of the military-first politics of the Kim Jong-il era,” said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University’s Institute for Far Eastern Studies.
“As time passes, the meaning and symbolism of Songun Day are likely to fade further.”
Keeping the dynasty, rewriting its hierarchy
The treatment of Kim Jong-il’s military legacy is only one part of a series of changes visible across North Korean politics and propaganda.
Kim Jong-un has reduced his appearances at commemorations dedicated to his predecessors, and state media have increasingly avoided the once-ubiquitous honorific names attached to their birthdays.

The term “Day of the Sun,” traditionally used for founder Kim Il-sung’s April 15 birthday, has largely disappeared from official coverage. Similarly, the use of “Day of the Shining Star” for Kim Jong-il’s Feb. 16 birthday has declined.

Kim skipped a customary visit to the Kumsusan Palace of the Sun on his grandfather Kim Il Sung’s birthday for the fourth consecutive year this year. He also did not visit the mausoleum for his father Kim Jong Il’s birthday in February, after making his first such visit in four years in 2025.
On Kim Jong-il’s birthday in February, the Rodong Sinmun instead prominently showcased Kim Jong-un attending the completion ceremony for Saebyeol Street with his daughter Kim Ju-ae.
That shift has now reached North Korea’s most fundamental legal document.
A revised Constitution adopted by the Supreme People’s Assembly at its March 22-23 session removed much of the lengthy account of Kim Il-sung and Kim Jong-il’s achievements from its preamble.

In their place, the Constitution put greater emphasis on governing principles associated with the current leader, including the so-called “people-first principle,” the supreme leader’s monolithic leadership system and the protection of national interests.
Aiming to be seen as ‘normal state’
For Seoul’s intelligence authorities, the changes suggest something broader than a simple effort by a third-generation ruler to build a stronger personality cult.

The NIS told the National Assembly Intelligence Committee in May that North Korea appeared to be diluting the colors of the Kim Il-sung and Kim Jong-il eras while simultaneously strengthening Kim Jong-un’s status and reorganizing the state’s institutions.

The agency assessed that the changes point to an intention to move toward the image of a “normal state” — one operating through more recognizable state institutions and national interests rather than relying as heavily on the revolutionary mythology and ideological terminology inherited from the Cold War.

Among the changes cited by the NIS was North Korea’s removal of “socialist” from the official title of its Constitution for the first time in 54 years, a move the agency interpreted as an attempt to emphasize the Constitution’s character as a more universal set of state rules.
The revised Constitution also dropped the description of North Korea as a “socialist state” from Article 1 and stripped away a range of ideologically charged expressions.

A recent report by Kim Il-ki, a senior research fellow at the Institute for National Security Strategy, similarly argued that North Korea is weakening socialist rhetoric while elevating a more state-centered form of nationalism.

The revised Constitution, Kim wrote, could be characterized as a “Kim Jong-un Constitution,” institutionalizing both his monolithic rule and North Korea’s new conception of the Korean Peninsula as consisting of two separate states.
That transition carries an apparent paradox.

Kim is presiding over a country with an expanding nuclear arsenal and an intensely personalized political system, even as the regime appears increasingly interested in presenting itself through the language and institutions of conventional statehood.
But those two objectives need not be contradictory from Pyongyang’s perspective.

North Korea’s concept of becoming a more “normal” state does not necessarily imply political liberalization or movement toward international norms. Rather, the changes suggest an effort to replace some of the inherited revolutionary symbolism of the Kim dynasty with a state identity centered on sovereignty, national power, nuclear status and Kim Jong-un’s own leadership.

Kim is therefore not erasing his grandfather and father altogether. Their legitimacy remains indispensable to the hereditary system, and this week’s Rodong Sinmun article continued to praise Kim Jong-il extensively.
What appears to be changing is the hierarchy of that legacy.

“Rather than continuing to cover the gap between socialist principles and reality with ideological rhetoric, North Korea appears to be acknowledging those realities and incorporating them into a state-centered governing framework,” Kim of INSS wrote in his report.

articles.title: Jellyfish force partial shutdown of French nuclear plant
articles.summary: It is the second consecutive year that jellyfish has forced the closure of the Gravelines power station in northern France.

blocks.text: A massive influx of jellyfish has led to the partial shutdown of a nuclear reactor in northern France.

Two of Gravelines nuclear power station's six units were shut down on Wednesday and Thursday because of the presence of jellyfish in the seawater filtration system, which is used for cooling, Électricité de France (EDF) said.
A third unit has been shut down since 10 August due to the same issue, while a fourth has been closed for an inspection.
Gravelines, one of the country's biggest nuclear power stations located between Dunkirk and Calais in the Hauts-de-France region, was also closed last August because of jellyfish in its filters.
EDF said that units three, four and six were now shut.

Unit three had only been reconnected to the grid on 18 August after the first wave of jellyfish earlier this month, the company said, while units one and two were also operating at reduced power as a preventative measure.
Gravelines' six units each produce 900 megawatts of power. The station is cooled from a canal connected to the North Sea.
Several species of jellyfish are native and can be seen around the coast when the waters are warm.
Jellyfish are at their most active in the warmer months. Hot weather increases plankton levels at the water's surface, drawing jellyfish up, experts say.
Measures have been implemented to try to prevent jellyfish infiltration, including a partnership with fishermen who capture and release them further offshore, according to French outlet Ici.
There have been similar issues at other nuclear stations, including at the Torness plant in Scotland in 2011 and Sweden's Oskarshamn plant in 2013, but such cases are rare.

articles.title: Comelec mulls leaving 2028 presidential debates to private groups
articles.summary: The Commission on Elections (Comelec) is considering leaving the 2028 presidential and other election-related debates to private entities, while taking on a "supervisory" role.

blocks.text: Published August 27, 2026 10:35pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.
COTABATO CITY — The Commission on Elections (Comelec) is considering leaving the 2028 presidential and other election-related debates to private entities, while taking on a "supervisory" role.

Speaking to the media in Cotabato City, Comelec chairperson George Garcia said that under the Fair Elections Act on lawful election propaganda, private entities must be the ones conducting debates under the supervision of a Comelec commissioner.
"Hindi po talagang kami dapat ang nagsasagawa nito [We’re really not the ones who should be handling debates]," Garcia said Thursday.

"Kami ay guest lamang dun at sinu-supervise namin but hindi kami mismo ang gagastos at walang public fund na gagamitin but we definitely encourage yung mga media entities na magkaroon ng pa debate," he added.
Other Stories

(We are only guests there, and we are only supervising it, but we will not be the ones shouldering the expenses, and no public funds will be used. However, we definitely encourage media entities to organize debates.)
Garcia urged private entities, including media organizations, to conduct the debates to show the public the candidates' stand on the issues.
"Mas maganda po yan para makita ng kababayan natin ang kahandaan ng mga tumatakbo [at] makita natin yung saloobin ng mga kanditao patungkol sa isang issue," Garcia said.
(It would be better to have debates so our fellow Filipinos can see the preparedness of those running for office and understand the candidates’ views on a particular issue.)

Comelec conducted the PiliPinas Debates of the presidential candidates for the May 2022 elections, where nine out of the 10 presidential candidates attended. The absentee was Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr., who refused to attend most of the debates; his running mate Sara Duterte also stayed away. They both won their races. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Dalai Lama prays ‘for all’ killed in Tibet-Nepal floods
articles.summary: NEW DELHI — Buddhist spiritual leader the Dalai Lama said Thursday that he was praying for all those killed in devastating floods in Nepal and Tibet. Flash floods and landslides on Wednesday…

blocks.caption: Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama attends a long-life prayer offering ceremony at the Main Tibetan Temple in McLeod Ganj, near Dharamsala on July 5, 2025. FILE PHOTO/Agence France-Presse

blocks.text: NEW DELHI — Buddhist spiritual leader the Dalai Lama said Thursday that he was praying for all those killed in devastating floods in Nepal and Tibet.
Flash floods and landslides on Wednesday killed at least 165 people and more than 1,300 remain missing on the Nepal-Tibet border.
“I pray for all those who have lost their lives, and offer my sympathy and heartfelt condolences to the bereaved and to all those affected by this tragedy,” he said in a statement.
The charismatic 91-year-old, who lives in exile in India, is lauded worldwide for his tireless campaign for greater autonomy for his Tibetan homeland, which Beijing says is an integral part of China.
“Since this region has seen calamities in the past as well, these are certainly symptoms of a deeper underlying cause — whether climate change or other factors,” he added.
“I hope that appropriate follow-up measures will be taken, wherever possible, to help ensure that such disasters do not recur.”

The Dalai Lama was just 23 when he fled the Tibetan capital Lhasa in fear for his life after Chinese troops crushed an uprising in 1959. He has never returned. Beijing condemns the Dalai Lama as a rebel and separatist.
On Wednesday, Penpa Tsering, leader of the India-based government of Tibetans in exile — the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) — called the disaster a “catastrophe”.
“The news of casualties and widespread destruction …and of the hundreds still missing, is heartbreaking,” Tsering said.
China calls the exiled Tibetans “nothing but a separatist political group”. /dl

articles.title: Board of Peace's Gaza envoy criticises Israeli strikes and Hamas actions
articles.summary: Nickolay Mladenov warns that a collapse of last October's ceasefire would be "a point of no return" for the region.

blocks.text: A senior official on US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace has criticised Israel's continuing air strikes on Gaza, as well as the actions of the Palestinian armed group Hamas.
Nickolay Mladenov warned that a collapse of last October's ceasefire would be "a point of no return" for the region.
He was speaking to the UN Security Council after Israel rejected the 15-point roadmap for Hamas's disarmament, which was announced by the Board of Peace last month.
Hamas has agreed to give up its weapons in exchange for a phased Israeli troop withdrawal. But Israel has insisted that the group must fully disarm before any pullout.

At least 1,303 Palestinians, including 300 children, have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the US-brokered ceasefire began, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
The Israeli military says four of its soldiers have been killed in Palestinian attacks in Gaza over the same period.

The Board of Peace's high representative for Gaza told the Security Council on Wednesday that he and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had agreed at their last meeting on a mechanism through which his government's remaining questions would be settled and that committees had been established for that purpose.
Mladenov said that process had not stalled but warned that risks remained, including the continued killing of Palestinian civilians in Israeli strikes.

"A ceasefire in fact under which civilians are still buried is not yet one that the people of Gaza can really feel. Every use of force that does not answer an immediate threat, and every incident that the deconfliction mechanism was not asked to resolve, costs this process something very hard to buy back," he added.
Mladenov acknowledged that Hamas too had yet to meet fully its commitment to cease all military activities.
"Every weapon carried, every tunnel still worked and every convoy still obstructed sets the process back and hands an argument to those who want to resume war," he said.

He repeated that under the new roadmap, Israeli troop withdrawal from Gaza "follows verified decommissioning" of Hamas weapons handed over to the Palestinian technocratic committee that will govern Gaza under the Board of Peace's supervision.
"It is sequenced and reciprocal," he said.
That is a key difference from comments made by President Trump's envoy, Jared Kushner, after meeting Israel's prime minister two weeks ago.
He said Israeli withdrawal would be discussed only once the demilitarisation of Gaza was "done" - appearing to change the plan in line with Israel's demands.

Israel's representative told the Security Council meeting that it was committed to last October's US-brokered plan for ending the Gaza war, but she insisted it could not succeed while Hamas still had weapons, tunnels and other military infrastructure.
"Disarmament must come first," she stated.
The Palestinian representative said Israel was killing Palestinian civilians with impunity in Gaza and called on the international community to protect them without delay.

Mladenov warned that if the ceasefire was allowed to collapse, "there will be no roadmap to return to, there will be no administration to deploy, and there will be nothing left of the ground to rebuild".
"That would not be a setback. It would be a point of no return for everyone."
The war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.
Israel responded by launching a military campaign in Gaza, during which more than 73,430 people have been killed, according to the territory's health ministry.

articles.title: CIA director warned Russia not to attack Nato members – US media
articles.summary: WASHINGTON — A highly unusual trip by the CIA director to Moscow this week was to warn Russia against any attack on Nato member states, US media reported Wednesday, after President Donald Trump…

blocks.caption: Two pedestrians, including a Ukrainian servicewoman, walk past a placard reading “Together we are unbreakable” and picturing Brigadier General of the Third Army Corps of the Ukrainian Armed Forces Andriy Biletsky (front) surrounded by militaries, in Kyiv on August 26, 2026, amid Russian invasion…

blocks.text: WASHINGTON — A highly unusual trip by the CIA director to Moscow this week was to warn Russia against any attack on Nato member states, US media reported Wednesday, after President Donald Trump sought to downplay the visit.

The Wall Street Journal and CBS News reported CIA Director John Ratcliffe aimed to dissuade Russia from attacking Nato members amid US intelligence assessments that Moscow could seek to test the alliance.
The Journal specified that Putin could test the North Atlantic Treaty Organization with a “limited assault” in the next few years.

The White House did not respond to multiple AFP requests for comment on the matter, and Trump said Ratcliffe’s visit to Moscow on Tuesday was “semi-routine,” implying that the intelligence chief was in the Russian capital to discuss the Ukraine war.
“He’s there, very sort of semi-routine. I hate to disappoint people. We would like to see the war with Ukraine end,” Trump said in an interview with conservative radio host Glenn Beck.
Ratcliffe is one of the highest-ranking US officials to visit Russia since its war with Ukraine started in 2022.
His visit came amid an escalation in Moscow’s offensive in Ukraine, with attacks this summer increasing the civilian death toll, while US-brokered peace talks have stalled.

During his visit, Ratcliffe also discussed the war with Iran, warning of additional sanctions if the Strait of Hormuz doesn’t reopen to shipping traffic, CBS News reported, citing multiple people familiar with the matter.
The Kremlin said Wednesday that Ratcliffe had “contacts” with Russia’s special services on his visit to Moscow but did not meet President Vladimir Putin.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Putin was briefed on the talks but refused to say whether the Ukraine war was raised.

“Contacts through the intelligence services are a positive development in and of themselves. It is too early to say how this will affect the process of resolving the crisis in our relations,” Peskov said.

The last time a CIA director visited Moscow was in November 2021 — when William Burns warned Russia against sending troops into Ukraine. Weeks later, the Kremlin launched its attack that turned into Europe’s worst conflict since World War II.
The CIA has also been involved in prisoner swap deals with Russia, including a major exchange in mid-2024.
The war in Ukraine has killed hundreds of thousands and the Kremlin has refused to ease its maximalist demands of seizing the rest of eastern Ukraine and keeping Crimea.
Trump dismissed suggestions that Ratcliffe was discussing other issues such as Russia testing the resolve of Nato or the US campaign to ramp up economic pressure on Iran.

articles.title: China deploys record number of ships around Taiwan as pressure grows
articles.summary: TAIPEI — China deployed a record number of coast guard, scientific research and other ships in Taiwan’s waters last month, the island’s coast guard told AFP, as Beijing dials up…

blocks.caption: A handout photo from the Taiwan Coast Guard taken and released on July 8, 2026 shows a Taiwan Coast Guard patrol vessel (R) sailing near a China Coast Guard ship in waters south of Kinmen. China deployed a record number of coast guard, scientific research and other ships in Taiwan’s waters in Jul…

blocks.text: TAIPEI — China deployed a record number of coast guard, scientific research and other ships in Taiwan’s waters last month, the island’s coast guard told AFP, as Beijing dials up pressure on Taipei.
Taiwan’s coast guard warned of an increasingly severe situation, as analysts say the increased activity is part of China’s bid to map the region for submarine warfare.

China’s Communist Party has never ruled Taiwan, but Beijing claims the island democracy is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to annex it. China also asserts jurisdiction over Taiwan’s surrounding waters.
The number of Chinese ships detected around Taiwan’s main island soared to a record 244 in July — an average of nearly eight every day, official data shared with AFP show.
That compares with 55 ships detected in June and 30 in May, and 58 in July last year.
In the first 21 days of this month, 152 vessels were detected.
About 60 percent are coast guard ships, with research vessels and other government boats making up the rest.
The figures do not include Chinese warships, which China’s military deploys around Taiwan on a near-daily basis.

China has long dispatched coast guard and research ships around the Asia-Pacific region, particularly in the hotly contested South China Sea, where Beijing and several littoral countries have competing claims.
China uses the ships to assert authority over the waters, government officials and analysts say, describing them as “grey zone” tactics — actions that fall short of an act of war.
The number of Chinese ships detected around Taiwan and several of its outer islands since May is 1,247, coast guard figures show.

“When we say the situation is becoming increasingly severe, we mean that the number of their government vessels in the waters surrounding Taiwan has increased, and there was a marked increase in July,” a senior coast guard official told AFP on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak to the media.
The Communist Party “has never ruled Taiwan for even a single day” and “without sovereignty over land, it has no right to claim economic zones at sea,” the official said.
‘Submarine warfare’

While Taiwan faces the constant threat of a Chinese invasion, China’s increasing maritime presence has also fuelled concerns about a potential quarantine or blockade to prevent ships carrying energy or other critical supplies from entering or leaving its ports.
China operates more than “120 oceanographic research vessels”, the Taiwanese coast guard said previously. It is tracking about 41 that operate in Taiwan’s waters.
They include the “Tong Ji”, which circled Taiwan in May, tracking the edge of the island’s restricted waters and refusing the coast guard’s orders to leave.
Its activities likely involved “oceanographic sampling and seabed survey operations”, which could contribute to China’s “anti-submarine warfare databases”, the coast guard said.
That was followed in June by China’s first law enforcement patrol in waters east of Taiwan.
Earlier this month, China also announced “traffic control measures” for the Taiwan Strait as Typhoon Dolphin swept towards the region.
A Taiwanese security official recently accused China of “authoritarian expansionism” and warned Beijing was “constantly pushing the limits through an incremental salami-slicing approach”.

Ryan D. Martinson, an expert on China’s maritime strategy at the US Naval War College, said Chinese research ships are owned and operated by civilian research institutes, but the data collected is shared with the military.

“That kind of data/knowledge is highly useful for Chinese naval forces, which will operate in these waters in the event of a conflict,” Martinson said in an email to AFP, noting he was speaking in a personal capacity.
“It is especially important for anti-submarine warfare and submarine warfare.”
‘Clear escalation’
In the past couple of months, Martinson said he had observed a “very large increase” in the number of Chinese research vessels operating around Taiwan, especially to the east of the island.
“This is not a new ‘play’ in its ‘playbook’. Rather, the novel aspect is that the scale of these operations around Taiwan is unprecedented,” he said.
Chinese research vessels have been seen “operating in conjunction” with coast guard ships around Taiwan, the coast guard official said.

This month, China’s “Xiang Yang Hong 03” research vessel was observed operating within Taiwan and Japan’s exclusive economic zones, moving over deep sea trenches and telecoms cables, said Jason Wang, chief operating officer of ingeniSPACE, which analyses satellite imagery and ship signals data.
The research vessel was escorted by a Chinese coast guard ship and a fishing boat that is part of China’s maritime militia, Wang said.
“This is the first time we have seen maritime militia escort a research vessel in Taiwan’s waters,” Wang said.

Wang said China’s objective was to gather “fresh hydrographic data of the Ryukyu Trench and East Taiwan Trench to conduct anti-submarine warfare” and “deny US and other allied vessels from doing the same”.

articles.title: World’s soils deteriorating while solutions go unused – UN
articles.summary: PARIS — More than half of the world’s soils are in poor condition, threatening global food supplies and biodiversity, while proven measures to improve soil health are not being…

blocks.caption: View of dry soil at La Concepcion reservoir, located about 10 kilometers south of Tegucigalpa, which water level is reduced to a 30%, on August 15, 2026. On August 19, 2026, the Honduran Secretariat of State for Risk and National Contingency Management (COPECO) raised the alert level to red in 75…

blocks.text: PARIS — More than half of the world’s soils are in poor condition, threatening global food supplies and biodiversity, while proven measures to improve soil health are not being implemented, said a UN report released on Thursday.
“Globally, we must shift from a mindset of soil exploitation to one of soil stewardship,” the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) warned.
Soils “support 95 percent of our food production, host 59 percent of global biodiversity, and serve as the planet’s second-largest carbon sink after the oceans,” said the report’s authors.
Yet “soil degradation continues to accelerate at an alarming rate”.
The report found that in 52.5 percent of regions and subregions soil management was poor or very poor. In a third, it was fair, while in only 14 percent was it good or very good.

It is the second major report by the FAO, after a pioneering effort in 2015, assessing soil health across the planet. That first study found most of the world’s soils were in fair, poor or very poor condition.

Since then, the FAO said, the world’s population has grown by 800 million people, while 80 million hectares (around 200 million acres) of additional land, nearly the combined area of France and Germany, had been turned over to major crops.
Erosion threat
By far the greatest threat to soil is from erosion, the experts said, with soil washed or blown away because of unsustainable practices.
Other threats include loss of the organic matter in soil (known as soil organic carbon), nutrient mismanagement, depleted soil biodiversity, salt build-up, pollution and urban expansion.

Climate change threatens to make most of the problems worse, while soil degradation itself can contribute to climate change. But improving soil health could also improve resilience and help fight global warming.
The authors said that most techniques for protecting and restoring soils were already well known before 2015, but they were still not being widely implemented.
Soil management improved in just 10 percent of assessed areas and deteriorating in 58 percent of them, they said.

One major technique for reducing soil degradation is reducing or abandoning tillage, such as ploughing. While as old as agriculture itself, tillage destroys organic life in the soil and, by breaking it up, leaves it prone to erosion.
Other methods for protecting and improving soil include planting cover crops, such as legumes and brassicas.
They are grown on fallow fields to lock soils in place and improve their nutrient content, and agroforestry, in which trees are integrated into farming practices.
Better use of natural and artificial fertilisers, which can themselves be a source of pollution, is also a key strategy.

The FAO said it was not a lack of knowledge, but limited access to resources and high upfront costs that were preventing farmers from implementing better soil management and called for greater financial incentives, more localised data and the use of indigenous knowledge, among other suggestions.

Ontario company Chapman’s Ice Cream says it's moving to replace more than 70 per cent of its ingredients from the U.S. by mid-2027, promising no price increases until March 2028.

blocks.caption: Chapman’s Ice Cream, based in southwestern Ontario, says it is moving to replace more than 70 per cent of its American ingredients by mid-2027, promising no price increases until March 2028. (CBC )

blocks.text: An Ontario ice cream company says it will replace more than 70 per cent of its American ingredients and won't increase prices for two years.

Chapman’s Ice Cream is shifting away from American suppliers as the trade dispute between Canada and the United States continues. The family-owned company also says it won't raise prices for its ice cream until March 2028.
It began looking for alternatives to U.S. suppliers in March 2025, when the first round of tariffs from the Trump administration was announced, CEO Ashley Chapman said.

“We made a statement at that time that we weren’t raising prices and we were going to start this journey. And here we are. We have not been sitting idle. We have been working very hard,” Chapman told CBC's London Morning on Thursday.
The company said it's on track to replace more than 70 per cent of its American ingredients and components with Canadian or non-U.S. sources by mid-2027.

items: The art of inflicting pain: How to select targets for Canada's counter-tariffs

blocks.text: The sweet move to Ontario sugar cone company
One of the biggest changes involves sugar cones.
There are no producers of industrial sugar cones in Canada, so the company partnered with Original Foods, a Dunville, Ont.-based company, to bring in a cone oven, Chapman said.
“We are going to be the only company in Canada who has a 100 per cent Canadian cone line."
Original Foods Limited will produce the sugar cones for Chapman's. The manufacturer tapped the ice cream retailer a few months ago when trade talks with Canada and the U.S. intensified.

"We knew there will be opportunities for customers who are currently buying in the U.S. to look for local manufacturing and we approached Chapman's to discuss if they would be interested to buy locally," said president Steeve Tremblay.

"It's very rewarding to keep the jobs in Canada. It makes our economy stronger and we're not being dependent outside the country, especially when there's a country that tries to make our economy and our lives more difficult. It's nice to see that we can collaborate and give somewhat of strategic response that’s good for Canada."

The two companies have already signed their agreement and equipment has been purchased in Germany. However, Tremblay said, there have been delays due to Canada's electricity registration requirements and other red tape.

"Sometimes [the requirements] are really unique to Canada and not aligned with European manufacturers, so it causes extra costs and delays and is a perfect example of something that can be reviewed," he said.
Tremblay said he plans to contact other Canadian companies to encourage more local partnerships.
Chapman's is also moving production of wafers used in its ice cream sandwiches to Canada, and is sourcing ingredients such as almonds from Australia and cherries from Chile.

blocks.caption: Ashley Chapman, CEO of Chapman's Ice Cream, says trade dispute between Canada and the U.S. has prompted Canadian companies like Chapman's to reconsider what they produce domestically. (Chapman's Ice Cream)

blocks.text: The trade dispute has prompted Canadian companies like Chapman's to reconsider what they produce domestically, he said.

“The first round last year of tariffs really opened the eyes of a lot of industry in Canada. Companies that we’ve known for years that would never consider producing certain products, suddenly they were saying, 'You know what, maybe we should look at this.'”
He said some of the changes have also proved to be more affordable than expected.

“It’s crazy what this has done for businesses in this country. Almonds from Australia, are you crazy? How is that possible that we could get an even better price, plus freight, from Australia instead of the United States? So we’re finding a lot of opportunities out there.”

items: Consumers say 'resolve is strengthened' to buy Canadian, bringing patriotic shopping movement back to life

blocks.text: Chapman said some of the changes are long-term commitments, including the five-year contract for Canadian-made cones.
Chapman’s is also working to make its production more efficient to help control costs, he added.
“I am fully confident that we are going to make it to the other side of this."
The company said it will continue to use 100 per cent Canadian dairy in its ice cream.

articles.title: Quebec party leaders make their pitches as election campaign kicks off

image.caption: Éric Duhaime, the leader of Conservative Party of Quebec, speaking during today's news conference. (Jacques Boissinot/The Canadian Press)

items: August 27That's a wrap — for nowThe election period is officially underway and all five leaders of Quebec's main political parties have made their initial pitch. As leaders tour the province, you can expect them to release their party platforms and announce campaign promises in the coming weeks.In the meantime, try out CBC's Vote Compass to see which party aligns most with your views.

60,000 workers needed for upcoming electionBenjamin ShinglerWith the election campaign now underway, Élections Québec says it faces a major challenge: recruiting enough staff to run the polls.In a statement to CBC News, the agency confirmed it needs to hire and train more than 60,000 people across the province ahead of the advanced polls and Oct. 5 vote.The agency noted that staffing is an issue leading into every election, adding that an advertising campaign is already underway and applications are open online. The statement stressed that teenagers aged 16 and 17 are eligible to work during the campaign and can learn more about how elections work in the process.

‘I’m the only leader,’ Milliard tells voterMélissa FrançoisThe leader of the Quebec Liberals stopped for an ice cream in the municipality of Batiscan in the Mauricie region. He chose a vanilla and chocolate twist. During the stop, a man approached him and said, “Please get rid of Pablo Rodriguez!” Milliard replied, “I’m the only leader.” Rodriguez, the former leader of the Quebec Liberals, stepped down last December after controversies involving him and his party.

Duhaime's message to Quebec anglophonesHolly CabreraÉric Duhaime, the leader of Conservative Party of Quebec, speaking during today's news conference. (Jacques Boissinot/The Canadian Press)The PCQ leader had a message to the province's English speakers: "The English community in Quebec has been hostage to the Liberals forever." Duhaime pointed to polls that suggest the Quebec Liberals have lost popularity among francophones.He said that hopefully anglophones realize that they would be better off with Conservative MNAs.

Quebec's economic model is at the ‘end of its rope,’ Duhaime saysHolly CabreraThe PCQ leader said that in the next few hours he would announce the "greatest" tax reduction. He also accused Fréchette of instrumentalizing the tariff war during the election and called her a protectionist. "This election, I want to fight for Quebecers and get more money in their pockets," Duhaime said. "Quebecers aren't fools. They know our [economic] model is not viable," Duhaime said, noting that the model is at the "end of its rope."

Quebec's prosperity shouldn't rely on the U.S., Duhaime saysHolly CabreraÉric Duhaime, the leader of Conservative Party of Quebec, speaks during a news conference, in Sainte-Claire, Que., on Thursday. (Jacques Boissinot/The Canadian Press)Speaking to Quebecers who are "tired of turning in circles," Duhaime said his party wants to be the "true alternative" to the province's old parties. He said he wants to remove interprovincial barriers to lessen Quebec's reliance on the United States."It's not up to Americans to determine our prosperity. It's up to us. Only us, in Quebec," Duhaime said.

Sole Conservative MNA introduces DuhaimeHolly CabreraBefore Duhaime steps up to the podium, Maïté Blanchette Vézina — the Conservatives’ only MNA — took some time to promote her party's ambitions. "If we're doing politics, it's first and foremost to represent real people," said Blanchette Vézina , who used to be a member of the CAQ. She said the Conservatives have "pragmatic and courageous" solutions for Quebecers.

Duhaime is speaking in BellechasseKwabena OduroÉric Duhaime's campaign bus. (Kwabena Oduro/CBC)The Conservative Party of Quebec leader Éric Duhaime is speaking at a news conference in the riding of Bellechasse, where he is hoping to win a seat. The party is holding an event that started at 5 p.m. to officially launch the party’s campaign. During the campaign, the Conservatives will focus on the cost of living, health care, housing and the autonomy of Quebec and its regions.

Conservative leader feeling ‘confident’Kwabena Oduro3 questions with the leader of the Quebec ConservativesOn the first day of the campaign, CBC's Kwabena Oduro caught up and had a brief chat with Éric Duhaime, the leader of the Conservative Party of Quebec.I just had a quick chat with Éric Duhaime. He says he's feeling confident about his campaign. Duhaime says his team has been preparing for this for the last four years and he's feeling more ready than he was four years ago.He is looking to get a seat at the National Assembly for the first time.He's running in the riding of Bellechasse, just south of Quebec City – one of a few areas where he is hoping his party will make gains.

Montreal mayor’s wish list for next Quebec governmentHénia Ould-HammouMontreal Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada laid out her requests from the next Quebec government on Wednesday. (Ivanoh Demers/Radio-Canada)Montreal Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada outlined her expectations for the next Quebec government at a news conference on Wednesday. Her requests focus on three key points: homelessness and housing, infrastructure and mobility, and public safety. She called on the next government to allocate recurring funding for 3,200 emergency shelter spots and to create three centres specializing in mental health and addiction by the summer of 2027. She reiterated her calls for a REM light-rail train system in the eastern part of the city.She also called for more funding to help with policing and youth violence prevention. Last week, Martinez Ferrada announced that she was moving forward with her plan to gradually equip the city's police officers with body cameras.She also demanded that Quebec change its approach toward Montreal and that the city be consulted before any decision affecting it is made.

articles.title: More than 1,300 missing after deadly Nepal-Tibet floods
articles.summary: NUWAKOT, Nepal — Rescue teams rushed Thursday to find more than 1,300 people missing on the Nepal-Tibet border in flash floods and landslides that killed at least 165 and swept away entire…

blocks.caption: A house lies deluged in sludge after flash floods at Trishuli Bazar in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on August 26, 2026. Agence France-Presse

blocks.text: NUWAKOT, Nepal — Rescue teams rushed Thursday to find more than 1,300 people missing on the Nepal-Tibet border in flash floods and landslides that killed at least 165 and swept away entire villages.

A terrifying clip of surveillance video from the Chinese side of the frontier shows a massive wall of mud and debris crashing over a building several stories high on Wednesday morning, engulfing it as dozens of people ran for their lives below. The surge swept away buses and cars like they were toys.

Many of the missing are foreign tourists, officials said of the disaster, which the US Geological Survey believe was caused by a glacial collapse that sent a flow of debris engulfing homes along the way.
The tsunami-like rumble of water and mud struck villages and towns on the path of two rivers — Bhote Koshi and Trishuli, with Nepali police saying they had recovered 162 bodies.
Another 823 people, including 579 Nepali and foreign tourists, remained out of contact in Nepal, according to the country’s disaster agency.
Across the border, Chinese state media said the “mudslide disaster” at the Gyirong Port in Tibet claimed three lives while 558 people, including 260 foreigners, were still missing.
Raju Bhadel, 56, a businessman in Nepal’s Nuwakot district, recounted receiving a call from his brother-in-law in distress.
“They were crying and said their entire house had been swept away. Three family members were rescued, but his brother is still missing,” he said.
Also at Nuwakot, teacher Manok Mishra witnessed “nine trucks being swept away by the floods including people”.
‘Inland tsunami’
Rescuers waded through mud and sludge to look for survivors after floodwaters buried the lower floors of multi-storey buildings.
Among those hunting for their missing family members was Subash Khatani, who told AFP he was looking for his big brother.
“He is among the missing from Rasuwa. That’s why we are out to search for him,” he said.
The foreigners out of contact included Indians, and others from Australia, Britain, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Portugal, South Africa, South Korea and the United States, Nepal’s tourism board said.
Hiking company Himalayan Glacier told AFP 47 people from a group including two children were missing in Nepal.
“Our teams are checking hospitals where victims are coming in,” said the company’s director Sanket Pandey.

The sudden rush of mud and debris was “like an inland tsunami, travelling nearly 170 kilometres down the Bhote Koshi valley into Central Nepal”, said environmental historian Ruth Gamble of La Trobe University in Australia.
“It is a popular route for international tourists travelling from Kathmandu to Lhasa,” she added.

Rasuwa, in the north of Nepal, was the first district to be affected. But deaths have been reported from seven Nepali districts in total as the flood waters raged through to Chitwan in the south, on the border with India.
The Nepali Army was carrying out flights and had rescued scores of people, while others living near the river in danger zones had been told to relocate.
China’s leader Xi Jinping said that “the most urgent task is doing everything possible to search for and rescue the missing people”, according to CCTV.
Tibet government officials mobilised nearly 800 emergency workers and 150 vehicles as well as sniffer dogs and speed boats to help the rescue efforts, China’s state-run news agency Xinhua said.
The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) said it was dispatching emergency supplies including blankets, first aid kits, stretchers and body bags.
Glacial collapse

The cause of the disaster was not immediately clear in the hours after it occurred early Wednesday, but the US Geological Survey said it was a glacial collapse that caused seismic activity and the “catastrophic” downstream impacts in Nepal and Tibet.
“This event was initially reported as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake,” it said.

“Additional analysis of nearby seismic stations, long period seismic waves, and satellite imagery led to the determination that the seismic event was instead a glacial collapse and debris flow, and that no earthquake had occurred.”
Climate change is causing glaciers to melt worldwide, increasing the risks of glacial lake floods and glacial collapses.
Qianggong Zhang, head of climate and environmental risks at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), warned of the potential for a second flood.
“With a blockage still lodged upstream on the Nepal-China border river, authorities warn a second flood may occur,” he told AFP
Many trekking companies were not running tours during the monsoon season, but there remains significant numbers of travellers including pilgrims in the region.
Among sites hit by the flood was Syabrubesi, the gateway to the popular trekking areas, as well as by pilgrims travelling to the base of the Mount Kailash, a holy site for Buddhists and Hindus.

articles.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: No Filipino casualties reported, says Palace
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — There are no reported Filipino casualties from the major floods and landslides that hit the Nepal-Tibet border as of Thursday, according to Palace Press Officer Claire Castro.…

blocks.caption: An aerial view shows houses lying deluged in sludge after flash floods at Devighat, Bidur Municipality in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on August 27, 2026. Nepal’s disaster agency said that 823 people remained out of contact on August 27, more than 24 hours after a deadly flood tore through the border…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — There are no reported Filipino casualties from the major floods and landslides that hit the Nepal-Tibet border as of Thursday, according to Palace Press Officer Claire Castro.

Citing information from the Department of Foreign Affairs and the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration, Castro said there are 128 Filipinos in Nepal, mostly women married to Nepalese. From this, 18 are overseas Filipino workers.
“No reported Filipino casualty as of this morning,” said Castro at a briefing.
The two agencies are coordinating with officials in Nepal, as well as with the Filipino community, to determine whether any Filipinos were affected, she said.
Meanwhile, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. urged the public to continue praying for the safety and recovery of the victims.

“Ang pamahalaan po, ang administrasyon, sa pangunguna po ng ating Pangulo…ang kanyang mensahe ay nakakalungkot ang ganitong pangyayari at patuloy nating ipagdasal ang maganda kondisyon ng mga taong naapektuhan ng kalamidad sa Nepal,” Castro said.
(The government—the administration, led by our President—conveys that this event is truly saddening, and we continue to pray for the well-being of those affected by the calamity in Nepal.)
The catastrophic flash flooding happened at around 8:37 a.m. to 9 a.m. (Nepal time) on Wednesday.
At least 165 people died while hundreds are missing as of posting time, an Agence France-Presse report said. /dl

articles.title: Chinese lecturer confesses to killing university student in S. Korea
articles.summary: A Chinese university lecturer in his 30s has admitted to killing a 25-year-old Chinese student in North Gyeongsang Province, South Korea, police said Thursday, as the Daegu District Court held a…

blocks.text: A Chinese university lecturer in his 30s has admitted to killing a 25-year-old Chinese student in North Gyeongsang Province, South Korea, police said Thursday, as the Daegu District Court held a hearing on whether to detain him.
Officials at Gyeongsan Police Station said the suspect, surnamed Jeong, admitted to parts of the allegations against him, including killing the victim in the early hours of Aug. 20.
He reportedly told investigators that he strangled her.
Jeong has been relatively cooperative with the investigation and has provided statements related to the crime, police said.

The victim, a Chinese student, was last seen on surveillance footage outside Jeong’s studio apartment in Hayang-eup, Gyeongsan, at around 2 a.m. that day. She also made her last contact with family members in China at around the same time.
The footage did not show Jeong forcibly taking her into the home, and she was not seen leaving afterward.
Police said an autopsy is needed to determine the time and cause of death.

Investigators have also found indications that Jeong mutilated and disposed of the victim’s body and are considering additional related charges. Police have been tracing his movements and checking locations believed to be connected to the disposal of the body.
Investigators believe Jeong also tried to make it appear that the victim had left his home on her own.
At around 10:30 p.m. on Aug. 20, a person wearing the victim’s clothes was captured on CCTV heading to Dongdaegu Station. Police later determined that the person was Jeong.
He allegedly disguised himself in women’s clothing, took the victim’s suitcase and cellphone to the station, turned off the phone there and then returned to his home in Gyeongsan.
The following day, Jeong called police himself and reported the victim missing, allegedly pretending to be her boyfriend and saying he had not heard from her since she left for Daegu.
Police are investigating him on suspicion of obstruction of official duties by deception in connection with the missing-person report.
Police became suspicious while questioning Jeong and later found the victim’s body at his home. Jeong was apprehended at around 7:29 p.m. Tuesday on a street in Hayang-eup.
Police applied for a warrant for his detention Wednesday, citing concerns that he could flee or destroy evidence. The Daegu District Court held a hearing on the warrant at 10:30 a.m. Thursday.
Jeong worked as an outside lecturer at a graduate school in Gyeongsan attended by the victim.
The woman, who had been working in China, entered Korea on Aug. 14 to receive documents related to her degree, according to police.

articles.title: Tanker hit by ‘unknown projectile’ in Strait of Hormuz – UKMTO
articles.summary: DUBAI — An “unknown projectile” struck a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz this week, causing a fire that has since been put out, a British maritime agency said early on Thursday. Iran…

blocks.caption: A sculpture overlooking the Strait of Hormuz is seen along the seafront in the port city of Bandar Abbas, in southern Iran on August 10, 2026. Agence France-Presse

blocks.text: DUBAI — An “unknown projectile” struck a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz this week, causing a fire that has since been put out, a British maritime agency said early on Thursday.
Iran has effectively blockaded the Strait of Hormuz since the United States and Israel attacked the Islamic republic in late February.
Tehran wants to charge tolls for passage, and has attacked ships it accuses of trying to skirt its preferred route.

“Local authorities have reported a tanker has been hit by an unknown projectile causing fire to the vessel which has since been extinguished,” the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said.
The incident occurred near the Omani coastal city of Khasab and was reported to the UKMTO on Tuesday, the agency said.
There were no casualties among the crew and no adverse environmental impact, it said.
Authorities are investigating the cause, it added.
The online notice did not specify the vessel’s nationality or direction of travel.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent laid out plans on Monday for the “economic asphyxiation” of Iran.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Wednesday that the new sanctions “will not achieve anything”. /dl

articles.title: Thieves steal Bronze Age artefacts from Spanish museum in four-minute heist
articles.summary: The Treasure of Villena is a unique trove of almost ten kilos of gold, bowls, bottles and bracelets dating back to the Bronze Age.

blocks.text: The operation at Villena Museum was "super fast and super professional", a spokesman for Villena town council said.
The city council said the robbery began with a diversion. Around 05:15 local time (03:15 GMT), the alarms went off at the local sports centre, sending police there first, Spanish media reported.
The museum's alarm then went off around 05:20. It took the thieves just four minutes to sweep through museum and leave the building before officers arrived.
The Mayor of Villena, Fulgencio Cerdán, said the thieves "stole a large part of the treasure," specifically all the gold, El Pais reported.
The museum's collection, which dates back to around 1,000 BC, is mainly gold items, but there are also pieces of silver, iron and amber.
It consists of more than 60 bronze age objects, including 29 bracelets, 11 bowls, three bottles and other miscellaneous pieces.
The town is "devastated," Cerdán said. "They've taken most of the treasure."
"I'm even trembling. The truth is that for those of us from Villena, this destroys us. It's part of our heritage, of our wealth," the mayor said.
The collection was discovered in 1963 by archaeologist Jose María Soler in a vessel sunk in a dried-out riverbed in Villena.
The Villena council spokesman insisted there had been "no failure" by the museum.
"All security systems were activated."

The past year has seen a series of raids on European museums. In October 2025, thieves broke into the Louvre museum in Paris in broad daylight, stealing jewellery worth $102m (£75m) before escaping on scooters, in a heist that took about eight minutes.
Last week, four works "of extraordinary value" by Renaissance artist Antonello da Messina were stolen from a museum in Sicily, Italy's culture ministry said.
Earlier this month, Italian police said they had recovered paintings by Renoir, Cezanne and Matisse worth over $10.4m (£7.6m) which were stolen from the Magnani-Rocca Foundation museum near Parma.

blocks.text: Bomb threats were emailed to 80 courts across South Korea on Wednesday, prompting police searches, tightened security and temporary disruptions to some court proceedings.
Police said they first received a report from the Incheon District Court at around 9:17 a.m. after the court received an email threatening an explosion.
Authorities deployed 37 officers, 11 members of a police special operations unit and three detection dogs to search the courthouse and surrounding area for approximately three hours.

Similar threats were sent to courts nationwide, including in Busan; Changwon, South Gyeongsang Province; Cheongju, North Chungcheong Province; Daejeon; Incheon; Jeonju, North Jeolla Province; Gwangju; Seoul; and Ulsan.

blocks.caption: A police dog searches the premises of Jeonju District Court in North Jeolla Province on Wednesday after the courthouse received an email threatening an explosion. (Yonhap)

blocks.text: The emails were largely similar in content, claiming that homemade explosives had been planted inside and around court buildings and threatening detonations later Wednesday.

The sender also claimed to be a member of a Japanese idol group. The emails reportedly said the sender had suffered malicious comments and criticism after being subject to a contract termination decision and had hired a lawyer, but became distraught after nothing changed.

The Jeonju District Court restricted public access to the courthouse as a precaution. Court proceedings scheduled from 2 p.m. were temporarily suspended until security restrictions imposed during the bomb search were lifted.
The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency’s task force dedicated to public threat cases has begun tracing the sender, while regional police agencies are coordinating with courts to strengthen security.
“We will conduct thorough searches even though the likelihood of an actual attack appears to be low,” a police official said. /dl

articles.title: Nepal-Tibet disaster: what we know
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — Catastrophic flooding and landslides on the Nepal-Tibet border unleashed waves of water and debris that have killed at least 160 people and left hundreds more missing. Here is what…

blocks.caption: This frame grab taken from video released by the Armed Police Force of Nepal on August 26, 2026 shows rescue workers carrying a person after massive floods and landslides in Rasuwa. Rescue teams rushed on August 27 to find hundreds of people missing on the Nepal-Tibet border in flash floods and l…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — Catastrophic flooding and landslides on the Nepal-Tibet border unleashed waves of water and debris that have killed at least 160 people and left hundreds more missing.
Here is what we know so far:
What happened?
The exact sequence of events is still unclear, but on Wednesday morning, torrents of water and debris crashed downstream on both sides of the border.
Surveillance video from the Chinese side showed a wall of mud and water crashing over a building as terrified people ran away.
In Nepal, a surge of water hit villages and towns on the path of two rivers — Bhote Koshi and Trishuli.
The disaster was intially described as a flood on the Nepalese side, and a mudslide by Chinese authorities.
Hundreds missing, many dead
At least 165 people have been reported dead, 162 in Nepal and three in Tibet.
Chinese authorities have said the disaster caused “major casualties” and reported another 265 missing.
On the Nepalese side, authorities said Thursday that 468 tourists, 393 of them foreigners, were unaccounted for.
The missing include Indians and others from Ukraine, Malaysia, the United Kingdom, South Africa and elsewhere.
Australia said 34 of its citizens were missing in Nepal.
Another 93 Nepalese citizens have also been reported missing.
Aid
Promises of aid and assistance came in soon after reports of the scale of the disaster.
The United States has pledged $500,000 in emergency assistance, and the International Federation of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies released $1.4 million.
“The priority now is to reach affected communities and get assistance to people who have lost their homes, suffered injuries or have been cut off,” its Nepal head David Fisher said.

The European Union said it had activated its Copernicus satellite surveillance system to help recovery efforts and was ready to provide more help, while the World Health Organisation said it had dispatched emergency medical supplies.
Neighbouring India has sent an initial 10 tonnes of humanitarian assistance.
Cause
The explanation for the calamity has evolved since it struck, but appears linked to a collapsing glacier.
Within hours of the flooding, Nepal’s Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal said an earthquake likely triggered a landslide, in turn blocking a river and sending water gushing downstream.
China also reported a landslide, saying a border hub between Tibet and Nepal had been hit by a surge of debris.
The Nepali foreign minister’s statement aligned with a US Geological Survey report of a quake in Tibet that was north of the disaster zone.

articles.title: LIVE UPDATES: First BARMM parliamentary elections
articles.summary: Bookmark and refresh this page for the latest news, photos, videos, and analyses as Rappler closely follows the historic elections

blocks.text: The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao is holding its first parliamentary elections on September 14, 2026, after being postponed at least four times: first in May 2022, then in May 2025, October 2025, and again in March 2026.

The historic polls are seen as a pivotal moment in the decades-long peace process in a region that was mired in conflict and socioeconomic and political challenges. The upcoming elections are also a test for the Bangsamoro transition and the institutions and systems established in the last seven years.
Bookmark and refresh this page for the latest news, photos, videos, and analyses as Rappler closely follows the regional elections.
LATEST UPDATES
10 hours ago
Bangsamoro parties clash over key reforms in first debate

blocks.caption: Crowd, Person, Adult

blocks.text: Thirteen political parties faced off in Cotabato on Thursday, August 27, for the first BARMM Parliamentary Elections Debate organized by the Institute for Autonomy and Governance. Held at Notre Dame University, the historic face-off showcased competing platforms for the regional government ahead of the landmark polls.

The debates centered on socioeconomic reforms, service decentralization, and resolving clan feuds or rido. Candidates also clashed over Sulu’s exclusion, electoral integrity, and resisting national government interference.

The event ended with party-list groups signing posters to pledge their commitment to civil society advocacies. This included signing covenants of commitment with Duyog Bangsamoro and the Coalition for Social Accountability and Transparency. – Rappler.com
10 hours ago
Delayed services an injustice to Bangsamoro — Loong

“Sang-ayon tayo sa decentralization kasi bakit natin i-centralize dito kung ang outcome ay kalahati ang nagagastos natin, kung ang outcome ay two years tayong delayed sa implementation. Because that is an injustice to the Bangsamoro people,” said engineer Don Mustapha Loong of the Progresibong Bangsamoro Party.
Loong defended decentralization as a way to make government services more efficient and responsive to communities.
He questioned the value of centralizing services when it results in lower spending outcomes and delays of up to two years in implementation.
Loong called the failure to deliver the gains of the Bangsamoro transition “the greatest injustice that could possibly happen.”
He said the “fruits of the revolution” may already be within reach, yet many Bangsamoro people remain unable to experience their benefits. – Angelle Matura
Angelle Matura is a Mover from Cotabato City.
10 hours ago
Lim urges responsible spending, Kashim hits BARMM failures

“We have to take care of taxpayers’ money. Every family, every working-class family, every month, nakikita nila sa payroll nila, tax withheld. Can you imagine that money could’ve gone to one more sack of rice, one week’s worth of grocery?” said Nur-Ainee Tan Lim Misuari of the Mahardika Party.

Lim called for greater accountability in the use of public funds, pointing to the underutilization of the block grant, limited absorptive capacity, and inefficiency in spending within the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.
She said the region needs leaders who can restrain themselves, put people first, and use public funds for the Bangsamoro.
“This is a government of failure,” Abdulhussein Kashim of Indigenous, Settles, Sama and Minorities Alliance Party described the situation bluntly.
He said the government has a strong legal foundation to deliver resources to the people but has failed to do so.
Despite the criticisms, Lim said there remains an opportunity for the Bangsamoro to “rise from the ashes,” particularly for undecided voters who are weighing their choices.
She reminded the audience that “our children are watching,” and that the region’s youth continue to dream of a better future. – Angelle Matura
Angelle Matura is a Mover from Cotabato City.
11 hours ago
Sema, Basher clash over national interference in BARMM polls

A tense exchange unfolded between lawyer Omar Yasser Sema of the Bangsamoro Party and Alipikre Basher of the People’s Consultative Party, also known as the Mushawara Party, over electoral reform and possible national government interference in the regional elections.
Sema asked whether Basher would support reforms if interference occurs, clarifying that it was a serious question.
Basher affirmed his commitment to an “honest and credible election,” saying they are “101%” committed to a credible electoral process.
“Hindi ka matatakot sa national government?” Sema asked.
Basher hesitated before cackling in response, drawing attention from the audience. – Angelle Matura
Angelle Matura is a Mover from Cotabato City.
11 hours ago
UBJP, BGC urge more representation for women, PWDs
“Ako po ay isa sa living [examples] of UBJP, kung paano itinaas ng UBJP ang participation ng kababaihan,” said lawyer Sha Elijah Dumama-Alba of the United Bangsamoro Justice Party.
Dumama-Alba highlighted the political participation of women and persons with disabilities as part of the party’s future advocacy.

She cited the Bangsamoro Women Commission, women’s empowerment, political subsidy funds for women candidates, and gender-based audits as pathways to strengthen women’s representation and participation.
Meanwhile, Amir Mawalil of the BARMM Grand Coalition said the coalition wants to work with all political parties and support initiatives that advance inclusion.
Both groups pointed to the Bangsamoro Gender and Development Code and stronger institutional mandates as mechanisms in expanding political participation and representation. – Angelle Matura
Angelle Matura is a Mover from Cotabato City.

blocks.caption: What you need to know about the first BARMM parliamentary elections

blocks.text: 11 hours ago
UBJP backs national transitional justice commission

blocks.caption: People, Person, Crowd

blocks.text: “Kung gusto nating ma-address ang historical injustices, hindi lamang ito sa Bangsamoro region, kundi sa buong Pilipinas,” said lawyer Sha Elijah Dumama-Alba of the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP).
Dumama-Alba called for the establishment of a national transitional justice commission under the national government to address historical injustices and legitimate grievances.
She said lasting peace requires justice, healing, and credible institutions.
As one of the signatories to the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro, the UBJP supports strengthening the Transitional Justice and Reconciliation Commission.
The party calls for adequate funding, technical capacity, and legal and institutional protection, with communities and the ulama included in its implementation and governance. – Angelle Matura
Angelle Matura is a Mover from Cotabato City.
12 hours ago
Bangsamoro groups push for justice-based solutions to rido

blocks.caption: Crowd, Person, Press Conference

blocks.text: “Sinusuportahan natin ang hybrid at restorative justice,” said Amir Mawalil of the BARMM Grand Coalition. Rido is a clan or family feud that can lead to repeated conflict and violence.
Mawalil called for the institutionalization of a dispute resolution framework across the Bangsamoro government, with all agencies helping implement it.
He identified land ownership and loose firearms among the issues that can fuel rido, stressing the need for responsive land distribution and addressing its root causes.
Meanwhile, lawyer Omar Yasser Sema of the Bangsamoro Party argued that the root of rido is not simply land conflict but the failure to address crimes through the justice system.
Sema called for greater access to justice and equal application of the law to prevent conflicts from escalating and recurring. – Angelle Matura
Angelle Matura is a Mover from Cotabato City.
12 hours ago
ABOT, PBB back settlers’ rights, inclusive Bangsamoro
“‘Di po natin sasayangin ang ating nasimulan na interfaith dialogue, kasama na doon ang culture of peace natin,” said Emran Mohammad of the Alliance of Bangsamoro Tri-People’s Party (ABOT).
Mohammad emphasized inclusivity for Moro, indigenous peoples, and settlers, including the concerns of Christian settlers, schools, churches, and other institutions.
He stressed the importance of continuing interfaith dialogue and fostering a culture of peace.

“Kailangan ng pagkakaintindihan at pagkakaunawaan para matamo ang pagkakaisa,” said engineer Addie Unsi of the Partido Bangon Bangsamoro (PBB), who also studied at Notre Dame University alongside Mohammad.
Unsi expressed support for ABOT’s position on recognizing settlers’ rights.
“Ang PBB ay susuportahan po ang posisyon ng ABOT doon sa pagkilala ng karapatan ng settlers,” Unsi said.
He also pledged support for a settlers’ office with a dedicated budget to enable it to carry out its programs. – Angelle Matura
Angelle Matura is a Mover from Cotabato City.
12 hours ago
Progresibong Bangsamoro Party urges open economic zones in Basilan, Tawi-Tawi

blocks.caption: Crowd, Person, People

blocks.text: “The island region is the front door in terms of economic development,” said engineer Don Mustapha Loong of the Progresibong Bangsamoro Party.
Loong highlighted the strategic position of Basilan and Tawi-Tawi as gateways for economic development in the Bangsamoro.
He said the focus should not only be on smuggling but also on creating a framework for open economic zones and free ports that would maximize the region’s strategic position and resources.
He stressed that despite this advantage, Basilan and Tawi-Tawi have yet to fully benefit from it. – Angelle Matura
Angelle Matura is a Mover from Cotabato City.

articles.title: Man who attacked nun on CCTV in Jerusalem acquitted on grounds of mental health
articles.summary: A Jerusalem court said the Jewish attacker was having a psychotic episode when he assaulted the nun, in an incident which caused outrage.

blocks.text: An Israeli court has acquitted a Jewish man who attacked a nun in Jerusalem, in an incident caught on CCTV which drew widespread condemnation.

Jerusalem Magistrates Court said Yona Schreiber was experiencing a psychotic episode when he pushed over and kicked the French nun in the Old City in occupied East Jerusalem in April. It ruled that he was not criminally responsible for his actions and ordered him to be sent to a psychiatric hospital for up to six years.
Video of the attack caused outrage, and deepened concerns after a rise in harassment of Christian clergy and pilgrims by Jewish extremists in the Old City.
The victim, who hit her head on a stone block, suffered a bruised face and leg.
Schreiber, 36, had been charged with assault motivated by hostility towards a religious group.
According to the district psychiatrist's report, Schreiber "was in a psychotic state at the time of the act and is not substantively fit to stand trial".
The prosecution accepted the psychiatrist's opinion and asked for Schreiber to be acquitted and committed to hospital.
Judge Ofir Tishler said that although Schrieber had attacked the nun, he was ordering his acquittal due to his mental health.
At the time of the attack, the French Consulate in Jerusalem said it strongly condemned Schreiber's "aggression".
The director of the French Biblical and Archaeological School, where the nun is a researcher, called the assault an "act of sectarian violence".

Israel's foreign ministry denounced the attack, calling it a "shameful act [which] stands in direct contradiction to the values of respect, coexistence, and religious freedom upon which Israel is founded and to which it remains deeply committed."

"Israel remains firmly committed to safeguarding freedom of religion and freedom of worship for all faiths, and to ensuring that Jerusalem remains a city where every community can live, pray, and practice its faith in safety and dignity," the ministry said on X.

While the violence of the attack on the nun is unusual, in the past few years in Jerusalem's Old City there have been regular cases of religious Jews spitting and acting aggressively towards those wearing Christian religious dress or symbols.

Church properties have been vandalised and there have also been bitter disputes caused by settler takeovers. Church leaders accuse Israel of trying to change the status quo – long-standing agreements on ownership and responsibilities - at their holy places.

A 2025 report by the Rossing Center, a Jerusalem-based organisation which aims to foster better inter-faith relations in the Holy Land, describes a "recent surge in overt animosity towards Christianity", putting this down to "a continued deepening of polarisation and ultra-nationalist political trends".

articles.title: Group of 47, including 2 children, missing in Nepal floods – hiking firm
articles.summary: SYDNEY — Forty-seven people from a group including two children are missing in Nepal following devastating flooding on the country’s border with Tibet, their tour company told AFP on…

blocks.caption: Army Rescue team arrive to bring aid in Devghat following flash floods and a landslide disaster in the Nepal’s Nuwakot district on August 26, 2026. Agence France-Presse

blocks.text: SYDNEY — Forty-seven people from a group including two children are missing in Nepal following devastating flooding on the country’s border with Tibet, their tour company told AFP on Thursday.

The group included 15 Australians, 10 Canadians, nine Nepalese, eight Americans, two Britons, two Singaporeans, and one Russian-American dual citizen, Himalayan Glacier managing director Sanket Pandey said.
“At this time they are still missing,” he told AFP.
“Our team are checking hospitals where victims are coming in.”
The US-based trekking company’s founder, Sagar Pandey, is also the president for trekking agencies in Nepal, and had flown over the affected area in a helicopter but was unable to land.
Among the 15 Australians missing are two teenage boys, he said.
Most of the group were staying in the Rasuwagadhi area hit by the flood, with several travelling into the town, he said.
Seven Nepali guides are among the missing group. /dl
