articles.title: What caused the Nepal-Tibet flash floods?
articles.summary: At least 270 people have died in the massive flash floods, while more than 800 others are missing.

blocks.text: The US Geological Survey says the floods in the Nepal-Tibet border were triggered by a "glacial collapse" - meaning a glacier or part of a glacier had disintegrated.
Initial reports led authorities to believe that an earthquake had been the cause.
The cause of the glacial collapse has not been determined, but scientists have warned that Himalayan glaciers are melting at an accelerating rate due to rising temperatures and climate change.

articles.title: Death toll at least 359, with more than 1,000 missing in Nepal, Tibet after catastrophic floods

image.caption: Police personnel rescue stranded residents from houses lying deluged in sludge after flash floods at Trishuli in Nepal's Nuwakot district on Thursday. (Arun Sankar/AFP/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Rescuers in Nepal, Tibet race to find flood survivors, including multiple Canadians

Rescue teams searched on Thursday for hundreds of missing people along the Nepal-Tibet border, where a catastrophic and deadly torrent of water and mud several stories high swept through communities a day earlier following a glacier collapse.

Citing authorities in Nepal and China, The Associated Press says more than 390 people have been killed and more than 1,400 others are missing. Reuters says at least 359 people are dead and nearly 1,000 are missing, including the citizens of several countries from around the world, after the flash floods that occurred Wednesday morning local time.

Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand said in a statement the government is "aware of 30 Canadians and permanent residents in Nepal and the Tibet region whose whereabouts and well-being have not yet been confirmed." Though she stressed the number could change given the difficult circumstances on the ground, which have included communication issues.
A relative of Dhaval and Megha Shah said the couple from Port Moody, B.C., are among the missing Canadians.
Nikita Shah, Dhaval's cousin, said the couple was on a "spiritual journey" in Nepal, and the last time they heard from them was Tuesday night.
Shah said the couple was staying at Hotel Kailash.

"We don't know if the infrastructure is still there or not, like we get a lot of misinformation, so it would be very helpful if the Canadian government can help," said Shah. "The Canadian government needs to do something about this."
Global Affairs Canada said in a statement that it is sending five consular officials to Kathmandu to support Canadians and co-ordinate with local officials on the ground.
"In addition to working closely with Nepalese and Chinese counterparts, we are also co-ordinating with international partners and allies who also have citizens in the region," it said.
The Nepal Tourism Board, which has provided numbers of those missing from a number of countries, had earlier said 25 Canadians were among the missing.

blocks.caption: Police personnel rescue stranded residents from houses lying deluged in sludge after flash floods at Trishuli in Nepal's Nuwakot district on Thursday. (Arun Sankar/AFP/Getty Images)

blocks.text: The region's steep valleys are economic lifelines and travel corridors, but are precarious when disaster strikes. Images showed what appeared to be the second floors of buildings in Nuwakot slathered in mud after the torrent rushed by. Debris hung from tree branches and wires, vehicles were buried and some stunned survivors were caked in mud.

"When I reached Dhunge bazaar, in half an hour, the flood came and damaged all the market. People were preparing to go to the office then," resident Shoyam Rajbhandari said. "How many people are missing or dead, we don't know."
PHOTOS | Before and after the floods:
UN dips into rescue fund

The United Nations' humanitarian chief, Tom Fletcher, announced Thursday he has ordered the release of $2 million US from the UN's Central Emergency Response Fund to help with medical care, shelter and water.
Fletcher added that emergency teams had been mobilized and additional ones were on standby.

The vast majority of the dead and 826 of the missing were in Nepal, with three dead and 558 missing in Tibet, authorities said. According to Nepal's Tourism Board, 517 of the missing people in the country were foreigners and 178 of them were from India.

items: Flash floods kill more than 160 in Nepal, Tibet
Hundreds of people, including tourists, missing after flood in Nepal

blocks.text: In addition, China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Lin Jian said that nearly 100 Chinese citizens were missing on the Nepal side.
Nepalese officials said that dozens of bridges were destroyed and nearly 40 kilometres of roads were damaged, complicating search efforts.
The Nepalese army has rescued more than 100 people from flood-affected areas through helicopter operations on Thursday morning, army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said.
The science behind Nepal's violent flash flood

At least eight foreign nationals were airlifted to the country's capital, Kathmandu, he said, adding that army teams also rescued people trapped inside facilities linked to the Trishuli hydropower project.
Rescuers found bodies about 100 kilometres downstream from the disaster zone in Chitwan district. Dozens of injured people have been transported to Kathmandu for advanced medical care.

Bishal Kumar Bhandari, chairman of the Nepal Red Cross Society, said they have shifted focus from rescue to large-scale relief operations in the flood-hit districts. He said that around 1,200 people were displaced from at least three villages.

In Tibet, a mudslide that struck near the land border crossing of Gyirong Port on Wednesday left mud in the surrounding areas more than 1.5 metres deep on average, with some road sections exceeding two metres, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported. Roads leading to the port were all damaged, while secondary collapses or landslides might occur as rain continued in the area, it added.
Melting glaciers more common
The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) first reported a magnitude 4.4 earthquake early Wednesday, about 66 kilometres north of Kathmandu, near the border.

The USGS later updated its analysis to say the seismic event it measured was a magnitude 5.2 glacier collapse that sent debris flowing downstream with catastrophic impact on communities. It said its determination was based on data from nearby seismic stations, long-period seismic waves and satellite imagery, and that no earthquake had occurred.
Climate experts at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development said an avalanche from a glacier likely caused Wednesday's flash flood.

"Hydrological observations indicate the exceptional speed and magnitude of the flood wave," they said in an emailed statement, noting that water levels at one point on the Trishuli river rose by as much as nine metres over half an hour.
The Lhende Khola River, a tributary of the Bhotekoshi, had maximum flooding, they said.
Drone footage shows destructive aftermath of Nepal floods

The steep slopes and the lush valleys below the Himalayan mountain range, which span several Asian countries, are especially vulnerable to flooding and landslides. Melting glaciers have become more common because of warming because of human-caused climate change.
Researchers in Kathmandu found earlier this year that glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya region are melting faster, with ice loss rates doubling since 2000.

blocks.caption: A man who was airlifted from Rasuwa district receives first aid at a mobile hospital staffed by army personnel in Trishuli, in Nuwakot district, Nepal. (Navesh Chitrakar/Reuters)

articles.title: 'The flood took everything': Nepal survivors describe horror of loved ones being swept away
articles.summary: One woman says her father, mother, sister and sister's children were carried away before her eyes.
articles.byline: Shaktimaya Tamang, Shreejana Shrestha, Gabriela Pomeroy

blocks.text: Survivors of massive flash floods in Nepal have recounted how they saw their loved ones disappear into torrents of mud.

At least 389 people have died and 900 others are missing after floods wiped out entire villages on the border of Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday, with a force so powerful seismologists initially identified it as an earthquake.
Rescuers trudged through thick mud and debris on Thursday as Nepalese authorities rushed to bring aid and relief supplies to the affected areas.
"My family members were swept away by the flood in front of my eyes," Kalpana Malla from Nepal's Nuwakot district told the BBC.
Malla said her father, mother, sister and sister's children were all claimed by the disaster.
"They could not escape the flood; there was no chance at all," she said. "This flood took everything, but my son and I climbed the rooftop of a house and survived but couldn't explain how."
Her son, Sugam Malla, said he saved his mother by pulling her hand.
He said he had given his phone to his sister so she could keep in touch, but the mobile was no longer reachable.
"I am worried she must be swept away."
Another woman, Goma Pandit, said she had lost her buffaloes and all her other cattle.
"My farmland is also swept away. Ten sacks of mustard seeds, tons of corn and rice paddy are all gone. Nothing is left."
At Kathmandu's TU Teaching Hospital, families of those missing in the floods wait anxiously for updates.
Holding up her phone, Ram Khumari Shrestha says: "This is my husband. He was off to Rasuwa as a part of his driving job. He was in contact with me until 8 pm yesterday.
"But I couldn't call him this morning. The phone was switched off," she told the BBC.
Mani Shrestha Bishwa was also camped out at the hospital on Wednesday night, hoping to hear from his younger brother, cousin, uncle and friend.
"I last contacted them at 8:30 in the morning," he said.
Trekking guide Sonam Dorjee missed the flood in his home village of Rasiwa Syafru by about an hour. He had left at 08:00 local time.
As he was driving to Kathmandu, Dorjee told the BBC he had heard the sound of floods gushing into their village.
"It [sounded] like an earthquake," he said. "My house has collapsed... I have seen a photo."
Dorjee said his sister, Dechen Tamang, was missing, along with her husband and several other family members.
He described the flood as "sudden and devastating".
"Many survivors are now left without homes and they need emergency rescue and evacuation, as well as food, temporary accommodation and medical support."
He is praying his sister is found alive. "There is a 10% chance, we hope," he said.

articles.title: People pulled from mud in Nepal after deadly flash floods
articles.summary: At least 160 people have been killed along the Nepal-Tibet border as rescuers struggle to reach the disaster zone.

blocks.text: Video from northern Nepal shows people being rescued from mud after deadly flash floods swept through the Nepal-Tibet border leaving more than 160 people dead and hundreds missing.
The Nepalese army and armed police forces have been rescuing flooding victims, although many rescuers are struggling to reach the disaster zone on the Tibet side.

articles.title: What scientists know so far about Nepal's deadly floods
articles.summary: WASHINGTON — Lethal surges of mud and water that hit “like liquid concrete” are nearly impossible to predict and can’t be outrun. The cause of the deadly landslide and flood…

blocks.caption: This satellite image released by Planet Labs on August 26, 2026 shows an aerial view of the Shyaphrubesi village and Trishuli River after a massive flood in Rasuwa district of Nepal on August 26, 2026. A massive flood and landslide disaster unleashed on the Nepal-Tibet border killed nearly 100 on…

blocks.text: WASHINGTON — Lethal surges of mud and water that hit “like liquid concrete” are nearly impossible to predict and can’t be outrun.
The cause of the deadly landslide and flood along the Nepal-Tibet border isn’t yet certain, but experts say the risk of such events is compounded by the extreme topography of the Himalayas.
At least 160 were killed and hundreds are missing in the wake of the disaster Wednesday morning.
Video from the Chinese side shows a raging wall of mud and debris crashing over a building several stories high, engulfing it and sweeping away buses and cars like they are toys.
It is too soon to draw any firm links to climate change, but there are well-documented trends in the “Roof of the World” that have increased the likelihood of such hazards.
Landslide, then tremors, says USGS
Nepal’s Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal said an earthquake likely triggered a landslide that in turn blocked a river, sending water gushing downstream after it eventually breached the obstruction.

But in a new note, the US Geological Survey said that while the event was initially reported as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake, “additional analysis of long period seismic waves indicate that the seismic energy was instead generated by a landslide.”
A preliminary assessment by the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) found “no anomalies” from the Chinese side of the border.

“We believe a rock-ice avalanche occurred in Nepal, blocking the Lhende river and causing the cascading flood event,” Sarthak Shrestha, a remote sensing and geo information analyst with the intergovernmental institute, told AFP.
Hatim Sharif, a hydrologist at the University of Texas San Antonio, told AFP one thing that struck him was the lack of rainfall beforehand.
“That defeats essentially every operational flood warning system in the world,” he said.
Running won’t help
By the time you see the mud flow coming, it’s too late, said Sharif.
“Running will not help,” nor will trying to flee by vehicle, Sharif added, because the mud and water moving at high speed form a lethal combination “like liquid concrete.”
The only solution is to climb up a hill, at least 20 feet (six meters), he estimates.
One possible long-term remedy might be river level gauges that relay changes to authorities in real-time, giving residents 20-30 minutes of warning, he said.
Dorothy Heinrich, a researcher at the UK’s University of Reading, told AFP: “In these mountain environments, the rivers can be quite narrow in areas.”
Anything that blocks them, be it an avalanche or landslide, will lead to a “big accumulation of water, then it creates these incredibly fast floods.”
Qianggong Zhang, head of climate and environmental risks at ICIMOD, warned of the potential for a second flood because of an ongoing blockage upstream.
Climate change trends
Nepal is also prone to glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) — the sudden and catastrophic release of vast volumes of water from melting glacier-fed lakes.
One such catastrophe in July 2025 originated in China’s Gyirong County, then surged into Nepal’s Rasuwa District, though authorities have not yet said a GLOF was responsible for the latest event.

In the coming days and weeks scientists around the world will be investigating potential climate links through what are known as attribution studies, which analyze how likely an event was in the fossil-fuel-warmed climate of today, versus the pre-industrial era.

blocks.text: KATHMANDU, Nepul — Hundreds of tourists have gone missing in Nepal after devastating flash floods on Wednesday killed at least 95 people.
Official figures suggested at least 291 foreigners were among the missing.
Hikers and climbers from around the world flock to the Himalayan nation to test themselves on some of the world’s highest peaks, Mount Everest among them.
Here is the latest on the missing:
India
According to the Nepal Tourism Board, 142 nationals from neighbouring India were missing.
The missing Indians were in the country with three travel agencies: Samrat Tours & Travels, Leaf Holiday and Himalayan Glacier.
Ukraine
Ukraine’s foreign ministry said Nepal’s Tourist Police had informed them that they considered 53 Ukrainian nationals to be missing.
They included a group of 46 Ukrainian tourists with whom the authorities in Nepal had lost contact, the ministry added.
Malaysia
Seventeen Malaysians travelling with Fishtail Tours & Travels were missing in the floods, the board said.
Malaysia’s foreign ministry said its embassy in Kathmandu had received reports from travel agencies suggesting they had lost contact with 11 Malaysian nationals believed to be in the Rasuwa district.
United Kingdom
Twelve UK citizens with the Alpine Eco Trek agency were unaccounted for, the tourism board said.
South Korea
South Korean officials confirmed eight hydropower workers were out of contact in the Rasuwa district following the floods.
South Africa
Four South Africans travelling with the same Alpine Eco Trek agency as the missing British citizens were missing, according to the tourism board.
United States
Three US citizens, also with Fishtail Tours & Travels, were unaccounted for, the board said.
Portugal
A Portuguese woman had gone missing in the floods, the country’s foreign ministry told AFP.
“She was with a group at the border post on the Nepal side,” a ministry spokeswoman said.
Australia
One Australian with Kathmandu Holiday Tours & Travel was missing, according to the board.
Netherlands
A Dutch citizen travelling with the same company as the missing Australian was also unaccounted for, the board added.
Italy
The Italian foreign ministry said two of its nationals and their guide were stranded upstream from a landslide but were receiving help.
The ministry is aware of 90 Italian citizens currently in Nepal and Tibet, but does not know if any might have been affected.
Nationalities unconfirmed
Several of the tour groups also announced missing foreigners whose nationalities had not been confirmed.
They included 77 with Trekkers Society, 26 with Kailash Journey and eight with Richa Tours & Travels.

articles.title: Nepal-Tibet floods kill at least 160, rescue crews rush to find missing
articles.summary: NUWAKOT, Nepal — Rescue teams rushed Thursday to find hundreds of people missing on the Nepal-Tibet border in flash floods and landslides that killed at least 160. Many of the missing are foreign…

blocks.caption: Rescuers look for survivors among the mud and the rubbles of buildings following flash floods and a landslide disaster in in Devghat, in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on August 26, 2026. A massive flood and landslide disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border killed at least 103 people on August 26, 2026 and…

blocks.text: NUWAKOT, Nepal — Rescue teams rushed Thursday to find hundreds of people missing on the Nepal-Tibet border in flash floods and landslides that killed at least 160.
Many of the missing are foreign tourists, officials said of the disaster that wiped out entire villages. The death toll appeared likely to rise.

One terrifying clip of surveillance video from the Chinese side of the frontier shows a raging wall of mud and debris crashing over a building several stories high on Wednesday morning, engulfing it as dozens of people run for their lives below. The surge sweeps away buses and cars like they are toys.
Chinese state media reported “major casualties” from a mudslide at a Tibet border hub, reporting three dead and another 265 people missing.
Nepali police said they had recovered 157 bodies after “devastating floods”, with officers working to move families in flood-risk areas to safety.
Tibet government officials mobilized nearly 800 emergency workers and 150 vehicles as well as sniffer dogs and speed boats to help the rescue efforts, China’s official Xinhua news agency said.
In the area hit by the disaster, rescuers waded through mud and sludge to look for survivors after floodwaters buried the lower floors of multi-storey buildings.
Some 403 tourists — 341 of them foreigners — were unaccounted for several hours after the disaster struck, according to Nepal’s tourism ministry.
The missing foreigners included 142 Indians, and others from Australia, Britain, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Portugal, South Africa, South Korea and the United States, the tourism board said.
“Entire villages and market areas have been wiped out,” said David Fisher, the Nepal head of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC).
It said it was was dispatching emergency supplies including blankets, first aid kits, stretchers and body bags.
Risk of new flood?
Locals were traumatised, while experts cautioned that a lingering blockage in a river could produce an additional flood.

“I got a call from (my brother-in-law) this morning, and they were crying and said their entire house had been swept away. Three family members were rescued, but his brother is still missing,” said 56-year-old local Raju Bhadel.
The cause of the flooding was not immediately clear.
But Nepal’s Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal said an earthquake likely triggered a landslide, which in turn blocked a river, sending water gushing downstream.
Nepal’s disaster authority said that satellite data indicated that a “snow-rock landslide” on the Nepal-China border may have caused the flood.
Images shared by Nepali police showed floodwater surging through a river, sweeping away houses in its path, while AFP images depicted the top floor of a house sticking out from muddy soil.
The Nepali Army was carrying out flights and had rescued scores of people, while others living near the river in danger zones had been told to relocate.
‘Mudslide disaster’

Sarthak Shrestha, a remote sensing and geo information analyst at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), said a preliminary assessment showed “no anomalies” from China’s side of the border.
“We believe a rock-ice avalanche occurred in Nepal, blocking the Lhende river and causing the cascading flood event,” he told AFP.
Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported on Wednesday that “a mudslide disaster” on the Nepali side resulted in “major casualties and missing people” at the Gyirong Port in Tibet.
China’s leader Xi Jinping said that “the most urgent task is doing everything possible to search for and rescue the missing people”, according to CCTV.
Traffic authorities in Tibet’s Shigatse said roads in the area were “at risk of mudslides and unsafe for passage”.
Monsoon rains from June to September regularly trigger deadly floods and landslides across South Asia.
Scientists say climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events in the region.
Qianggong Zhang, head of climate and environmental risks at ICIMOD, warned of the potential for a second flood.
“With a blockage still lodged upstream on the Nepal-China border river, authorities warn a second flood may occur,” he told AFP.

articles.title: Davao Region growth drives residential expansion with Camella
articles.summary: Economic expansion, infrastructure investment, and intercity connectivity are steadily reshaping Davao Region, solidifying its position as one of the principal centers of tourism, commerce, mobility,…

blocks.text: Economic expansion, infrastructure investment, and intercity connectivity are steadily reshaping Davao Region, solidifying its position as one of the principal centers of tourism, commerce, mobility, and residential development.

blocks.caption: Camella communities in Davao reflect the housing brand’s over three-decade presence in the region, providing thoughtfully planned neighborhoods as cities and emerging growth areas continue to expand.

blocks.text: It entered from a substantial base: data from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) show that Davao grew by 5.1 percent in 2025, bringing its gross regional domestic product (GRDP) to approximately PHP 1.14 trillion at constant 2018 prices. Services accounted for 62.1 percent of output, while transportation and storage grew by 8.2 percent. Wholesale and retail trade was the largest contributor to overall growth, followed by financial and insurance activities and public administration.

The composition of the local economy is essential to real estate development: transport, services, healthcare, and personal activities expand enterprise, create employment, and increase demand for residences linked to tourism destinations, growth centers, infralink projects, and retail parks. Davao Region also represents a sizable property market: the 2024 Census of Population placed it at 5.39 million, equivalent to about 4.8 percent of the national total. Household population reached 5.37 million, increasing by nearly half a million people between 2015 and 2024.
Enterprise drives residential demand

blocks.caption: Davao City’s expanding urban landscape reflects the region’s sustained economic growth, strengthening its role as a key center for commerce, tourism, and residential development.

blocks.text: Robust business activity across the Davao Region is directly strengthening its real estate market. As of March 2025, the region’s 19 operating economic zones hosted 55 companies, employing over 50,000 people and generating more than USD 275 million in export revenue during the first half of the year.

Total regional employment reached 2.48 million individuals, with the services sector comprising 56.4 percent of the workforce. This consistent enterprise and job growth broadens the property market, fueling strong demand for residential developments situated near core workplaces, commercial centers, and emerging business hubs.
Tourism transforms the regional economy

blocks.caption: The Kadayawan Festival draws visitors to Davao City each year, contributing to the region’s vibrant tourism economy and supporting growth across hospitality, retail, transportation, and other local enterprises.

blocks.text: Davao City welcomed over two million visitors in 2025, according to the City Tourism Operations Office. Kadayawan Festival alone attracted more than 206,000 guests in August, demonstrating how major celebrations generate activity for hotels, restaurants, retailers, transport providers, and local enterprises.

Across Davao Region, nearly 2.9 million overnight travelers were recorded during the first three quarters of 2025, representing an 11-percent increase from the comparable period a year earlier. Improved air connectivity, stronger domestic travel, private-sector investment, and a range of tourism products were among the factors supporting the increase.

The region offers a diverse portfolio, home to attractions such as the Philippine Eagle Center, Malagos Garden Resort, Eden Nature Park, cultural destinations, museums, and major celebrations. Nearby Samal Island adds beaches, resorts, marine recreation, and island experiences.

For the property sector, tourism contributes more than visitor spending. A larger hospitality and leisure economy sustains job creation, stimulates surrounding businesses, strengthens the movement of goods and services, and raises the residential relevance of well-connected, well-planned locations.
Connectivity creates new corridors

blocks.caption: Ongoing investments in roads, bridges, and other infrastructure are strengthening connectivity across Davao, opening new corridors for commerce, mobility, and residential growth.

blocks.text: This economic and demographic base is supported by a transport network undergoing considerable modernization.

Established arteries such as Daang Maharlika, Davao-Bukidnon Road, and Davao-Cotabato Road link regional cities and growth centers across Mindanao. Road rehabilitation, widening, bridges, bypasses, and complementary infrastructure are further improving momentum.

Among the most significant is the 45.5-kilometer Davao City Bypass Construction Project, designed to connect Toril in southern Davao City with Panabo City in Davao del Norte. The four-lane corridor includes the first twin-tube mountain road tunnel in the country. Upon completion, the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) estimates that travel time between Toril and Panabo could decrease from one hour and 44 minutes to approximately 49 minutes.

Closer to the coast, the Davao River Bucana Bridge and adjacent roads forming Segment B of the Davao City Coastal Bypass Road opened to vehicles in December 2025, providing another route between areas traditionally dependent on inland thoroughfares.

Across Davao Gulf, construction also continues on the nearly five-kilometer Samal Island-Davao City Connector Bridge. The project is expected to modernize movement between the two locations, strengthening linkages between the metropolitan center and one of the premier regional leisure destinations.

Such infrastructure carries implications beyond shorter journeys. Better roads and bridges can expand catchments, improve logistics, and allow residential demand to extend beyond established epicenters.

A broader employment base, active visitor economy, and expanding transport network are widening the range of locations that can support residential demand across Davao. These conditions provide the context for Camella, which has built alongside the region as its cities, markets, and communities have evolved.
More than three decades of building homes in Davao Region

blocks.caption: In the heart of Davao, Camella communities bring together multigenerational homes, open spaces, and premium amenities to create connected neighborhoods designed around the evolving needs of Filipino families.

blocks.text: Camella, the Philippines’ most trusted and preferred housing brand, has grown with Davao Region for more than 30 years, leaving a footprint alongside its demographic, commercial, and physical progress.

Camella, the flagship housing brand of Vista Land, the country’s leading integrated property, has created communities across Davao City, including Toril, and Tagum, bringing lifelong homeownership closer to Overseas kababayans and established Filipinos. This geographic reach reflects a long-term approach, serving urbanizing districts while extending into emerging locations as the region expands.

Shifting residential priorities reinforce this direction: for homebuyers and investors, location is measured not simply by distance from the metropolitan center, but by proximity to employment, education, and everyday essentials. These considerations gain importance as public works improve mobility between municipalities, businesses build beyond city limits, and tourism stimulates local enterprise.

Camella continues to move with this progression: its communities are supported by an inclusive economy, stronger connections, urbanizing livelihoods and lifestyles, and ongoing investment by public and private institutions. As Davao develops into a more integrated regional network, residential opportunities are rising with it —as prosperity produces possibilities, mobility multiplies markets, and communities contribute to sustained growth.
The Philippines’ largest homebuilder

For nearly five decades, Camella has delivered over 600,000 homes in more than 1,250 communities across 49 provinces and 147 key cities and municipalities in the country. Crafted for the upper- to middle-income segment, it places family and community life at the center—creating a legacy of value for generations of Filipinos.
Learn more about Camella communities nationwide. Visit www.camella.com.ph and follow @CamellaOfficial for news and offerings. Make your dream home a reality today!

articles.title: Mamburao SK councils call out continued postponement of 2026 polls
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro – The Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) councils of Mamburao, the capital town in Occidental Mindoro, have united in opposing the continued postponement of the Barangay…

blocks.caption: Oriental Mindoro map.

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro – The Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) councils of Mamburao, the capital town in Occidental Mindoro, have united in opposing the continued postponement of the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE), saying it is time to give a new generation of young leaders the opportunity to serve.
In a joint statement issued by the Mamburao SK Federation, the SK councils of the municipality’s barangays said they were “strongly” opposed to any further postponement of the BSKE.

“We, the Sangguniang Kabataan Councils of all barangays of Mamburao, Occidental Mindoro, stand united in respectfully expressing our strong opposition to the continued postponement of the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE),” the statement said.
The youth leaders acknowledged the trust placed in them by their constituents and said they remained committed to fulfilling their responsibilities.
However, they stressed that public service should also provide opportunities for new leaders to emerge and for other young people to serve their communities.
The statement framed the Mamburao SK position as a call for democratic leadership transition rather than a rejection of their responsibilities.

“Hindi ito pagtalikod sa tungkulin, kundi panawagan para sa demokratikong pagpapalit ng liderato at pagbibigay ng pagkakataon sa bagong henerasyon ng kabataan na makapaglingkod,” the SK federation said.
(We are not turning our backs to responsibility rather we appeal for a democratic transition of leadership that would give a new generation of leaders the opportunity to serve the public).
The statement was endorsed by SK councils from 15 barangays in Mamburao: Barangay Uno, Dos, Tres, Cuatro, 5, 6, 7, 8, Payompon, Tayamaan, San Luis, Fatima, Balansay, Tangkalan and Talabaan. INQ

articles.title: Tim Curry, iconic character actor, dies at 80
articles.summary: Tim Curry, a character actor who created a gallery of delicious, very loony villains for stage and screen, including Dr. Frank-N-Furter in “The Rocky Horror Picture Show” and the smug concierge in…

blocks.text: Tim Curry, a character actor who created a gallery of delicious, very loony villains for stage and screen, including Dr. Frank-N-Furter in “The Rocky Horror Picture Show” and the smug concierge in “Home Alone 2: Lost in New York,” has died. He was 80.
Curry, who suffered a stroke in 2012 that put him in a wheelchair, died Tuesday night at his home in Los Angeles, according to his longtime manager and friend Marcia Hurwitz. No cause was disclosed.
Known for his arch humor, a puttylike face and gift with voices, Curry earned three Tony nominations — for “Spamalot,” “My Favorite Year” and “Amadeus” — and a Primetime Emmy nod in 1994.
“I like playing the more curious corners of the human mind and human behavior, partly because they’re a tad more interesting,” Curry told The Associated Press in 1993.

Curry burst onto the scene as the Transylvanian Frank-N-Furter in the sci-fi, cross-dressing rock musical “The Rocky Horror Show,” which premiered in 1973 at the Royal Court Theatre in London. He went with it to Broadway and then starred in the 1975 cult-classic movie alongside Barry Bostwick, Meat Loaf and Susan Sarandon.

The show was ahead of its time in terms of its representation of LGBTQ+ characters and has entered the pop culture lexicon for its many iconic and memorable scenes, including the song “The Time Warp,” which has been covered by handfuls of artists, and the often-quoted phrase, “Dammit, Janet!” The show was twice revived on Broadway, most recently in 2026 with Luke Evans playing Frank-N-Furter.

“He was a force, a bright fierce flame, an exquisite charm and that rich vocal tone,” Evans wrote on Instagram. “I hope, wherever you are, you’d approve of one more Frank having the time of his life in those heels.”
Tim Curry’s take on Frank-N-Furter

Curry’s Frank-N-Furter had a posh British accent, but that almost wasn’t the case. He said he tried German and American accents but pivoted after he heard a British woman on a bus talking with her friend.
“I met a woman on a bus who said, ‘Do you have a house in town or a house in the country’ and I thought, ‘That’s the voice!’” he told LA Magazine in 2015.

For many years after the film’s premiere, the British-born actor declined to discuss it. He didn’t participate in activities promoting the film, which morphed into an interactive event at midnight shows. But he later warmed again to the project and embraced it at public events. Asked by LA Magazine how he viewed “Rocky Horror,” he responded: “With a sort of bemused tolerance. It’s neither a blessing nor a curse. I was lucky to get it.”

Curry’s Broadway career included starring in Tom Stoppard’s “Travesties” in 1975-76, playing Mozart opposite Ian McKellen’s Antonio Salieri in Peter Shaffer’s “Amadeus” and King Arthur in the 2005 production of “Spamalot.” The New York Times said his “stalwart, plummy-voiced Arthur wears a smile as inflexible as armor.” He also played Scrooge in “A Christmas Carol,” at the Theater at Madison Square Garden in 2001.

His screen credits included starring as the child-killing monster in the 1990 miniseries version of Stephen King’s horror novel “It,” as a medical officer in “The Hunt for Red October” in 1990 and the double-dealing Cardinal Richelieu in 1993’s “The Three Musketeers” with Kiefer Sutherland, Charlie Sheen and Chris O’Donnell.
“Tim Curry was someone I cared deeply about, he was someone I loved working with and I am so lucky to have these memories,” Sutherland said in a statement.

In his 2025 memoir, “Vagabond,” Curry warned readers that while there were scraps of his nature in his characters, he was none of them. “The distinctions between who I really am and who I’ve pretended to be as an actor have proven to be a source of great disappointment to some audiences. It has not caused me much personal distress beyond the periodic necessity to deter stalkers,” he wrote.
Tim Curry’s life and career began in England

Born in Cheshire, England, Curry was the son of a Navy chaplain and a school secretary. He was 12 when his father died and his mother subsequently went to work. Young Tim learned to cook his own breakfast, resulting in a lifelong passion for cooking, and sharpened his humor muscles.

“My father was a Methodist chaplain in the Navy, and we moved pretty much every 18 months,” he said. “So I had to make my mark in new schools and new playgrounds pretty quickly. And a sense of humor is the best way to do that. I was always a kind of mimic, one of those awful, relentless children, I should think.”
Acting did not occur to him until his middle teens, when he attended a school for the sons of Methodist ministers.

“I was lucky that it was a liberal kind of school; many of them in England are rather Dickensian,” he recalled to the AP. “There was a lot of theater, and I sang, too; I had been singing in church from the age of 7. I had enormous opportunities to express myself in that way. I just got hooked, really.”

His training continued in 1965 when he entered the University of Birmingham, at that time one of three English universities with a drama department. “I took an academic course, which I largely ignored, I’m afraid, and just acted all the time,” he said.

He then went down to London and talked his way into his first job, “Hair,” in the West End. Curry went on to the more formalized theater of the Royal Shakespeare Company and the Royal Court Theatre, where he was enlisted for “The Rocky Horror Show.”
Tim Curry’s other roles

He went on to futilely try to stop Macaulay Culkin’s Kevin McCallister from taking advantage of New York’s swanky Plaza Hotel in “Home Alone 2: Lost in New York.” Curry also was Wadsworth, the unhinged butler with a secret past, in the quotable “Clue.” He played a wealthy philanthropist in 1995’s “Congo” and a baddie opposite Carol Burnett in the movie “Annie.”
“Nobody could play lovable villains better than he could,” Burnett wrote on Instagram. “He was a dear friend. I was blessed to know him.”

In later years, Curry lent his baritone voice to many voice-acting roles in children’s TV series, including “Star Wars: The Clone Wars,” “The Wild Thornberrys” and “The Adventures of Jimmy Neutron, Boy Genius.”

He won a Daytime Emmy in 1991 for voicing Captain Hook in “Peter Pan and the Pirates” and earned a Grammy nomination in 2002 for the audiobook of the first “Lemony Snicket” novel, “A Series of Unfortunate Events.”
After a yearslong break from live-action roles, Curry played a plague doctor-masked man in a wheelchair in 2024’s “Stream,” something the film’s director Michael Leavy called a dream come true.

Curry, who never married and had no children, was deeply private about his personal life. But he wrote in his memoir that he was convinced to tell his story thanks to so many moving encounters with fans.

articles.title: Trump declares emergency over foreign equipment in US power grid
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, United States — US President Donald Trump declared a national emergency Wednesday over foreign-made equipment inside the country’s electric grid, saying the growing need for power…

blocks.caption: US President Donald Trump closes his eyes before signing an executive order calling for more research and flexibility on vaccines, in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, DC, on August 10, 2026.(Photo by Jim WATSON / AFP)

blocks.text: WASHINGTON, United States — US President Donald Trump declared a national emergency Wednesday over foreign-made equipment inside the country’s electric grid, saying the growing need for power has made the system a target for hostile governments.
The executive order blocks companies from buying, importing or installing certain foreign-made parts used in what the government calls the bulk-power system.
A bulk-power system is the network of high-voltage lines, substations and power plants that transmits electricity across the country.
In the order, Trump said the boom in AI data centers and other advanced technology projects has left the United States more dependent on stable electricity than ever.
If the grid went down, he argued, the damage would be far worse than in the past.
The order also warns that foreign-built equipment could contain hidden digital “backdoors” in its software — secret access points that would let another country control or shut off the equipment.
The order applies to countries under US arms embargoes or sanctions, or governments the administration decides are working against American interests.
China is not named, but Chinese-made grid parts have worried US security officials for years.

Washington has used a similar playbook before, pressing allies to keep Huawei and fellow Chinese telecom supplier ZTE out of new mobile phone networks and arguing that Beijing could force the companies to spy or sabotage.
Both were later blacklisted by US regulators.

articles.title: PH urged to push for united Asean front to make Big Tech accountable
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Internet security watchdog Scam Watch Pilipinas on Wednesday urged the government, as the current Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) chair, to push for a partnership…

blocks.caption: A man uses a smartphone as various social media apps are displayed on screen in Pugoda on June 12, 2026. AFP

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Internet security watchdog Scam Watch Pilipinas on Wednesday urged the government, as the current Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) chair, to push for a partnership with other members of the regional bloc in holding social media platforms accountable for harmful content and scams.

In a statement, Scam Watch Pilipinas lead convenor Jocel de Guzman said the Philippines should initiate discussions for an Asean Big Tech Accountability Framework to set rules for major platforms in addressing harmful content and scams, and strengthening protection for children and vulnerable users, among other concerns.
“For too long, countries like the Philippines have been dealing with the world’s biggest technology companies individually,” De Guzman said.

“When we ask platforms to act on harmful content, scam advertisements, fake accounts or other digital threats, cooperation often depends on the willingness of the platform because our jurisdiction and enforcement reach are limited,” he added.

De Guzman said that instead of being limited to just banning or blocking platforms, the government should strengthen its ability to regulate and compel cooperation by forging “a united Asean front in dealing with Big Tech.”
“If the platforms want access to Asean consumers, then Asean must also have the power to demand accountability from them,” he said.
EU experience

De Guzman cited the Digital Services Act and Digital Markets Act of the European Union (EU), which required the world’s largest platforms to address systemic risks, improve transparency, protect consumers and cooperate with regulators at the risk of being slapped with penalties.

“The Philippines has the Asean Chairship in 2026 and we should use it. Secretary [Henry] Aguda and the [Department of Information and Communications Technology] have an opportunity to put Big Tech accountability and Asean digital sovereignty on the regional agenda and start building a stronger negotiating position for Southeast Asia,” he said.
According to him, Europe proved that even the world’s biggest technology companies listen when governments act together, adding: “Asean should do the same.”

Sen. Erwin Tulfo on Tuesday criticized social media companies for allowing the spread of content on recent school shootings in Tacloban City and Zamboanga City in violation of current community standards.

The Tacloban shooting in June was carried out by two teenagers and left three students dead, while the Zamboanga shooting was perpetrated by a 14-year-old Grade 8 student who killed another student before shooting himself.
The Zamboanga shooter live-streamed the shooting on his Facebook account and on another livestreaming platform, the footage of which has since circulated online.

Another shooting was carried out by a teenage gunman in a school in Thailand on Aug. 7. The shooter, who killed 6 people before turning the gun on himself, had reportedly been exposed to violent content on social media, including how to use a gun.
“Big Tech operates across borders … harmful content spreads across borders. Regulation cannot remain trapped within national borders,” De Guzman said.

articles.title: France eases cow diets as cheesemakers sweat
articles.summary: FRANCE — Widespread drought and record-breaking heat waves have forced France to relax some of its famously strict rules on cheese production, with authorities announcing on Wednesday special…

blocks.caption: A pasture in Beaufort, France, where cheesemakers can usually feed their cows only local grass. (AFP)

blocks.text: FRANCE — Widespread drought and record-breaking heat waves have forced France to relax some of its famously strict rules on cheese production, with authorities announcing on Wednesday special measures for abondance, beaufort and comte.
France’s vast array of local cheeses are a source of national pride and authorities go to great lengths to protect traditional production methods and ensure authenticity.

To earn a coveted “appellation d’origine protegee” (Protected Designation of Origin) label—and the right to give their cheese a particular protected name—producers must follow rigid rules on where their animals graze and what they eat.
Parched pastures
But the summer’s drought, which affected 95 percent of mainland France in July, has left normally rich pastures dry and bare.

In response, the government has said producers of abondance, beaufort and comte, hard cheeses made from the raw milk of cows grazing in the Alps and Jura mountains, can supplement the animals’ diet with more fodder and grain brought in from elsewhere.
Growth on permanent grasslands as of Aug. 10 is a third less than the 1989-2018 average, according to the Agriculture Ministry’s statistical service.
The fodder situation is “highly degraded” in almost all regions, the ministry said earlier this month.
Record-breaking heat

The National Institute of Origin and Quality, the government agency that administers and enforces rules of origin, says it will also grant temporary relief for several other cheeses including reblochon, cantal, bleu d’Auvergne, and fourme d’Ambert.
Europe’s record-breaking summer heat has caused thousands of excess deaths, set wildfires blazing and seen major rivers drop to record lows.
In France, farmers are bracing for their smallest corn crop since 1980, and winegrowers are reporting some of the earliest harvests on record.

articles.title: Comelec ‘in full control’ ahead of BARMM polls
articles.summary: COTABATO CITY—Despite the series of gun attacks mostly in the Maguindanao provinces that so far left 14 people dead, the Commission on Elections (Comelec) on Wednesday remained hopeful that the first…

blocks.caption: Police officers check vehicles at a checkpoint in Shariff Aguak, Maguindanao del Sur, on Aug. 5, 2026, as part of the implementation of the election gun ban in the Bangsamoro region. —Photo from the Maguindanao del Sur Police Provincial Office

blocks.text: COTABATO CITY, Philippines — Despite the series of gun attacks mostly in the Maguindanao provinces that so far have left 14 people dead, the Commission on Elections (Comelec) on Wednesday remained hopeful that the first parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) next month will be “peaceful, orderly and credible.”

“We are upbeat for the Sept. 14 regional elections,” Comelec Chair George Erwin Garcia told reporters at the sidelines of “Botong Bangsamoro,” the poll body’s voter education and information activity held here on Wednesday.

“We would like to assure [you] that elections on Sept. 14 will happen as scheduled. Nothing can stop that from happening. We are on top of the situation. We recorded only one election-related [incident of] violence,” Garcia said.

He was referring to the Aug. 15 ambush on the convoy of BARMM interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua in Datu Odin Sinsuat, Maguindanao del Norte. Macacua and his companions were unhurt during the incident.
Garcia said there were no plans to place any areas in the Bangsamoro under Comelec control following the ambush of Macacua.

He said the security situation in the region had markedly improved compared to previous elections. It is the “first time in the history of Bangsamoro,” Garcia noted, that there were fewer than 20 weapons confiscated at checkpoints, and there was only one election-related incident recorded.
He added that in previous polls, there were “already many incidents this early on.”

Garcia said the poll body and the security sector considered only the ambush on the convoy of Macacua as “election-related” among the 43 shooting incidents since the gun ban was implemented on July 16. He said the ambush was considered as such because Macacua is a candidate for the third district seat of Maguindanao del Norte.
Fewer ‘red’ areas

“Truthfully, there are many towns here in Bangsamoro that used to be ‘red’ category areas. Now, it has lessened. They have become ‘green,’ ‘yellow,’ ‘orange’ [category areas], and the ‘red’ category areas in the entire Bangsamoro have not increased,” Garcia said.
“This only means one thing. The entire Bangsamoro is quiet and peaceful. We are in full control of the situation in the Bangsamoro,” he added.

Areas under the red category are those with serious threats and a history of election-related violence. Earlier, the Comelec reported that there were 26 areas in the Bangsamoro under the red category, while 23 were orange, 41 were yellow, and 18 were green, as of July 29.
Garcia said the Comelec is all set for the historic political exercise, having deployed the needed equipment for the upcoming Bangsamoro polls.
The remaining challenge now, with over two weeks before Election Day, is to heighten the voters’ interest to cast their ballot.
“This is a challenge to everyone. With how long we have asked for an election, having been postponed many times, it might be that only a few people will vote,” Garcia said.
“It is sad if we spend so much [and] prepare for so long, with how many times it has been postponed or reset, only for a small percentage of the Bangsamoro to vote,” he added.

On Tuesday, Garcia briefed the Army’s 6th Infantry Division (6ID), police and other election stakeholders about the Comelec’s committees on “kontra bigay” (vote-buying) and on environmentally sustainable elections.

The briefing served as a platform to strengthen interagency coordination and deepen the participants’ understanding of the mandates, roles, and responsibilities of the committees, particularly in preventing and addressing vote-buying and vote-selling.

Garcia stressed the Comelec’s commitment to credible, efficient, fair, peaceful, and orderly elections. He also underscored the importance of sustained coordination and cooperation among government agencies, election stakeholders, and other partners to address potential challenges and safeguard the integrity of the electoral process.
Military, police support

Brig. Gen. Ricky Bunayog, 6ID commander, reaffirmed the military’s commitment to supporting the Comelec in fulfilling its constitutional mandate, particularly by maintaining a secure environment for voters, election personnel, and other stakeholders throughout the electoral process.
“I assure you that the 6ID will fully support Comelec in the performance of its duties to help ensure a peaceful and successful election,” Bunayog told Garcia.
Capt. Steffi Salanguit, spokesperson for the Bangsamoro regional police, said the 43 shooting incidents were recorded from July 16 to Aug. 25.
Maguindanao del Sur recorded the highest number of shooting incidents at 16, followed by Maguindanao del Norte with 14, seven in Lanao del Sur, four in Basilan and two in Cotabato City.
Salanguit said these were either due to personal grudge, “rido” (family feud), revenge, or drug-related activities. The gun-related incidents left 14 people dead and eight wounded.

articles.title: Partial lunar eclipse to grace Canadian skies tonight
articles.summary: On the night of Aug. 27-28, a partial lunar eclipse will be visible across the country. Here's when to see it.

image.caption: A partial lunar eclipse will occur on Aug. 27 and 28, and will be seen across most of Canada. (Nicole Mortillaro)

blocks.text: Science
On the night of Aug. 27-28, a partial lunar eclipse will be visible across the country. Here's when to see it.
Lunar eclipse comes 2 weeks after total solar eclipse seen in parts of Europe
Listen to this article
Estimated 3 minutes
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

blocks.caption: A partial lunar eclipse will occur on Aug. 27 and 28, and will be seen across most of Canada. (Nicole Mortillaro)

blocks.text: On the night of Aug. 27-28, a partial lunar eclipse will be visible across the country.
The eclipse comes roughly two weeks after the total solar eclipse that was seen across Iceland, Spain and a small portion of Portugal.
While this will be a partial eclipse, it will be a deep one, with 93 per cent coverage at its maximum.

Lunar eclipses occur when the moon moves through Earth’s shadow, called its umbra. Before it enters the umbra, however, it passes through Earth’s outer, dimmer shadow, called the penumbra. However, because it is much dimmer, it’s difficult to see with the naked eye when this occurs.

blocks.caption: This illustration shows the movement of the moon through Earth's shadow for the Aug. 27-28 partial eclipse. (Sky &Telescope)

blocks.text: Most of Canada will see the entire duration of the eclipse, while Western Canada will see the partial eclipse already taking place as the moon rises.

items: NASA says it will put humans on the surface of the moon in 2028. How realistic is that?
The International Space Station is old and leaky. Should it be decommissioned sooner rather than later?

blocks.text: The great news is that, unlike with a solar eclipse, you don’t need any protective eyewear to watch the event.
Also unlike a solar eclipse, a lunar eclipse takes place over hours, not minutes.

blocks.caption: All (or most) of the lunar eclipse on August 27-28 will be viewable across North and South America. (Leah Tiscione/Sky & Telescope)

blocks.text: When to see it
The eclipse will begin as the moon enters Earth’s penumbra at roughly 10 p.m. ET, but that’s not when you want to go out to start observing.

Instead, the visible part of the eclipse begins at 10:33 p.m. ET on Aug. 27 and ends at 1:52 a.m. on Aug. 28. The deepest part of the eclipse will occur at 12:13 a.m. with almost all of the moon appearing darkened.
This is just one of many astronomical events taking place this month.

"It's kind of a fun one because … August had so many great things going on for it and still does," said Elaina Hyde, director of the Allan I. Carswell Observatory York University’s department of physics and astronomy in Toronto.

"We had, of course, the very, very partial solar eclipse back on August 12th. We had the Perseids, which were either fabulous or slightly less fabulous, depending on how cloudy your skies were. And, of course, the Jupiter-Mercury conjunction."
Will it be a "blood moon"?
"It's a partial eclipse, so it's not going to turn 100 per cent red, but depending on where you are in Canada, it will still be pretty red," Hyde said.
The great thing about lunar eclipses is that there's no need for any equipment — just your eyes.
"This is a naked eye object, but if you have binoculars or a small telescope or just a [cellphone] camera with a really good night mode, you should be able to get pretty good pictures," Hyde said.

image.caption: A map labelling Lake Ontario as 'Lake America' is seen behind U.S. President Donald Trump as he speaks in the Oval Office of the White House on Thursday. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

blocks.text: World

Carney pushes back on move, says Canadians will call it Lake Ontario 'now and always'
Listen to this article
Estimated 4 minutes

Trump signs executive order to rename Lake Ontario to ‘Lake America’
U.S. President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Thursday to change the name of Lake Ontario to "Lake America" as tensions with Canada worsen.
Sitting near a map with the name "Lake America" over the body of water, Trump said "entitled" Canada has been difficult to deal with and repeated claims the country was ripping off the United States.
"They want to be treated like a state, but they are not a state," Trump said.
When asked why he was targeting American allies with these types of actions instead of American adversaries, Trump said, "they haven't treated us well."
"The Canadian officials have treated us very badly," Trump said. "They are nasty people."

blocks.caption: A map labelling Lake Ontario as 'Lake America' is seen behind U.S. President Donald Trump as he speaks in the Oval Office of the White House on Thursday. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Tensions between the two countries have escalated since trade negotiations fell apart on Friday. Both countries have accused each other of implementing 11th-hour changes.
Prime Minister Mark Carney has said the agreement became untenable. The federal government unveiled its retaliatory measures, set to go in place on Sept. 8.

items: Trump's top trade negotiator disputes Canadian assertion that U.S. made last-minute demands

blocks.text: Trump first threatened to rename the body of water during an escalating war of words with Ontario Premier Doug Ford.
The two exchanged insults, with Ford calling the president a bully, among other things, and Trump saying the premier was a "less charismatic, intelligent" version of his late brother, Rob.

blocks.caption: Boats float on Lake Ontario Tuesday with Toronto's skyline seen in the background. (Adrian Kraus/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum — who previously was governor of border state North Dakota — posted on social media "the places and waters that border our nation and support our economy should reflect the greatness of the United States."
He said he's proud to enact the name change.
'Real foolishness'
In Canada, the move prompted incredulity by officials on social media.
Carney said Canadians will call the body of water Lake Ontario "now and always," while Nova Scotia Premier Tim Houston said "we're into some real foolishness now."
"It's Lake Ontario, buddy," Houston said.
At an unrelated news conference in Winnipeg, Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew described the situation as an over-the-hill rock star playing old hits at a casino.
"I think that's the part of Donald Trump's presidency we're at now," Kinew said.

"He thought he had a real hit, a real golden oldie with the Gulf of Mexico, and he's trying to bring back that, and he's trying to play the hits for his base. But I think everybody here thinks it's a little sad and it's not his best work."
Where Trump’s trade war with Canada could backfire | About That
Lake Ontario — one of the five Great Lakes — is located between Ontario and New York. The province of Ontario, founded in 1867, took its name from the lake.
The lake's name comes from the Huron Indigenous people's word "oniatarí:io," which means "lake of shining waters."
Carney said on social media that the name is more than 400 years old, and predates both Canada and the U.S. as countries.
Gulf of Mexico saga
Last year, Trump signed an executive order to change the name of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America.
It only applies to U.S. federal documents and geographic services, but some online map services also made the change.

items: 'Gulf of America' shift won't be the first time Google Maps has changed names depending on your location

blocks.text: The geographic controversy led to the White House removing The Associated Press from certain duties covering the president after the news service did not use "Gulf of America" in its reporting.

The Associated Press took the White House to court in a dust-up that led to Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt ripping many authorities away from the White House Correspondents' Association, the organization of journalists who cover the president.
